# UNSLOP

A design and writing rulebook for interfaces that do not look or read like they came out of a model on default settings.

Feed this file to a coding agent as context, or read it yourself before a review. Every rule in it is enforceable: each one names the default it replaces, the values to use instead, and a way to check for it.

The file practices what it preaches. It contains no box shadows outside of quarantined bad examples, no emoji, no glowing status pills, no blue or purple gradients, no em dashes, no exclamation marks, and none of the 350 banned words in its own prose. Banned words appear only as mentions: inside inline code, or inside code fences tagged `slop`, which hold the bad examples. `scripts/lint.py` in the source repository checks all of this on every build.

## Part 1. Ground Rules

### 1.1 What this file is for

Language models and the starter kits they lean on produce the same interface every time. Indigo button. Rounded card with a soft shadow. A hero with a radial glow, a gradient headline, a pill that says "Now with AI", and two buttons. A grid of six features, each icon sitting in a pastel rounded square. A green dot next to the word LIVE. Copy that promises to `unlock` something `seamless`.

None of these choices is wrong on its own. Together they are a signature, and readers have learned to see it. Once a visitor spots the signature, they stop reading the product and start reading the process that made it. They assume nobody looked closely, and they are usually right.

This file replaces each default with a specific decision. It is long because the defaults are many, and because "make it look less generic" is not an instruction anyone, human or model, can follow. "Use a 1px `#D9D5CB` border and no shadow" is.

### 1.2 How to use it

With a coding agent:

1. Put this whole file in the agent's context, or put Part 1 and the agent instructions block from Part 6.7 in the system prompt and the rest in a docs folder the agent can search.
2. Tell the agent which parts apply to the task: Parts 2 to 6 for interface work, Parts 7 and 8 for any text a person will read, Part 9 before merging.
3. Run the checks in Part 9 on the agent's output. Do not trust a claim of compliance; grep for it.

With a person:

1. Read Part 1 in full. It takes ten minutes.
2. Skim the chapter headings of Parts 2 to 6 and read the ones that match what you are building this week.
3. Keep Part 7 open while writing copy. Search it for any word that feels like filler.

During review:

1. Run `scripts/lint.py` on Markdown, and the grep commands in Part 9 on source code.
2. Walk the page with the checklist at the end of each Part.
3. Reject on any hard rule. Discuss everything else.

### 1.3 The hard rules

These hold everywhere, with no exceptions for a deadline, a client request, or a framework default. Each is checked by a command in Part 9.

1. **No shadows.** `box-shadow`, `text-shadow`, `filter: drop-shadow()`, and every Tailwind `shadow-*` utility except `shadow-none` are banned. Separate layers with a 1px border and a tonal step in the background. Part 2.5.
2. **No gradients in blue, indigo, violet, purple or fuchsia.** Zero. Not in buttons, not in text, not in borders, not as a glow behind the hero. In practice this file bans gradients of every color in interface chrome, because the exceptions people ask for are almost always the same blue-to-purple sweep with a new name. Part 2.2.
3. **No emoji in the interface, in copy, in docs, in commit messages, or in code comments.** Icons come from one SVG set. Status comes from words. Part 3.7.
4. **No glowing status pills.** No green dot with "LIVE", "Online", "New" or "Beta" inside a rounded capsule. State the status in text with the time it was last true: "Connected. Last sync 14:02." Part 4.4.
5. **No banned words.** None of the 350 entries in Part 7 appear in shipped copy, in any form. If a sentence needs one of them to stand up, the sentence has nothing to say. Rewrite it with the specific claim, or delete it.
6. **No glass, glow, blur or neon.** `backdrop-filter`, frosted panels, outer glows, and animated borders are banned. Part 2.8.
7. **Radius is 0 or 2px.** Never above 4px on any rectangle. Circles are allowed only for avatars and radio buttons. Part 2.7.
8. **One accent color, outside the blue-violet band.** Hue between 235 and 335 degrees in OKLCH is off limits for the brand accent. Links may be underlined ink instead. Part 2.3.
9. **No em dashes, no exclamation marks in interface copy.** Use a period or a comma. Part 8.
10. **Show the real thing.** Real screenshots, real numbers with units and dates, real names with permission. No 3D blobs, no isometric illustrations, no stock photos of a smiling team around a laptop, no testimonials you cannot source. Part 3.8 and Part 5.

### 1.4 The soft rules

These are defaults. Break one when you can write down, in a sentence, what the break buys the reader.

1. Left-align text. Center only single lines: a short heading, a button label, a number in a stat.
2. Body text is 16px at 1.5 line height, at most 66 characters per line.
3. Use the spacing scale in 1.6. Group with space first, rules second, background third, borders on boxes last.
4. One typeface family for the interface, plus a mono. A serif for long reading is allowed.
5. Motion stays at or under 150ms, moves only opacity and transform, and stops completely under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
6. Headings say what the section contains. "Pricing", not "Simple, transparent pricing for teams of every size".
7. Buttons say what they do: "Create invoice", "Send 3 invites", "Delete project". Never "Get started" when something more exact exists.
8. Every number on a page has a unit, a source or a date.
9. Lists hold items that are actually parallel. Paragraphs hold reasoning.
10. A page has one primary action. Every other action is visibly secondary.

### 1.5 The signature, in one table

The table lists the patterns that most often mark an interface as generated, the default each comes from, and the replacement this file uses. The details live in the Part named in the last column.

| Pattern | Usual source | Replace with | Part |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-indigo-600` primary button | Tailwind docs and UI kits | Accent `#B4441C` or ink `#1A1A18` fill, 2px radius | 2.3, 4.6 |
| `rounded-2xl shadow-lg` card | Tailwind UI, shadcn `Card` | 1px rule, `--paper-2` fill, or no box at all | 2.5, 4.7 |
| Blue-to-purple gradient headline | Landing page templates | Solid ink, size and weight for hierarchy | 2.2, 3.2 |
| Radial glow behind the hero | Vercel-style templates | Nothing. Or a real product screenshot with a 1px border | 4.21 |
| "Now with AI" pill above the headline | AI landing templates | A dated line in the changelog | 4.21 |
| Six features in icon tiles | Every SaaS template | Three to five features as rows, with screenshots and numbers | 5.16 |
| Green dot plus LIVE | Status pill components | "Running since 09:41" in text | 4.4 |
| Emoji as bullets or section icons | Model-written READMEs | Plain list markers, or nothing | 3.7 |
| Inter at every size, tracking tight | Next.js starters | A chosen face, default tracking | 3.1 |
| Glass card with backdrop blur | Dribbble trends | Opaque `--paper-2` surface with a 1px rule | 2.8 |
| Fade-up on every section | Animation libraries | Static content | 3.9 |
| Five-star testimonial with stock avatar | Template filler | Sourced quote with name, role, company, date | 5.12 |
| "10x faster" stat row | Marketing filler | One measured number with method and date | 5.18 |
| Everything centered | Hero templates | A shared left edge | 3.5 |

### 1.6 Tokens at a glance

The whole file uses one set of tokens. Copy them as written, then change the accent if you have a brand color that passes the rules in Part 2.3.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F7F5F0;
  --paper-2: #EFECE4;
  --paper-3: #E5E1D6;
  --ink: #1A1A18;
  --ink-2: #4A4843;
  --ink-3: #6F6C64;
  --rule: #D9D5CB;
  --rule-strong: #1A1A18;
  --accent: #B4441C;
  --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #2F6B3A;
  --warn: #8A6100;
  --bad: #A3271F;
  --focus: #1A1A18;
  --radius: 2px;
  --font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --font-serif: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  --font-mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", Menlo, monospace;
}

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --paper: #141412;
  --paper-2: #1E1D1A;
  --paper-3: #2A2925;
  --ink: #ECE9E1;
  --ink-2: #B5B1A7;
  --ink-3: #8F8B81;
  --rule: #34322E;
  --rule-strong: #ECE9E1;
  --accent: #E2703F;
  --accent-ink: #141412;
  --ok: #7FB38A;
  --warn: #D9A93A;
  --bad: #E0705F;
  --focus: #ECE9E1;
}

*, *::before, *::after { box-shadow: none; }

:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

| Scale | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Spacing (px) | 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 |
| Type (px) | 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 32, 40, 56 |
| Line height | 1.5 body, 1.15 to 1.25 headings |
| Measure | 66ch for prose |
| Border | 1px solid `var(--rule)` |
| Radius | 0 or 2px, never above 4px |
| Motion | 0 to 150ms, `ease-out`, opacity and transform only |
| Icons | One SVG set, 16 or 20px, 1.5px stroke |

### 1.7 How the rules are worded

Each rule in this file has the same shape, so an agent can apply it without interpretation:

- **The default it replaces**, named by source: a Tailwind class, a component library default, a template, a habit of model output.
- **The replacement**, with values: hex, px, ms, ratio, count.
- **The check**: a grep pattern, a lint rule, or a question with a yes or no answer.

When a rule seems to conflict with a framework, the rule wins and the framework gets configured. Part 6 shows the configuration for Tailwind v3 and v4, shadcn/ui, plain CSS, and design token JSON.

When two rules in this file conflict, the more specific one wins: a chapter rule beats a Part rule, and a Part rule beats this ground-rules Part. Accessibility rules beat every visual rule.

### 1.8 What this file does not do

It does not pick a brand for you. The canonical tokens are a working default, chosen to be plainly unlike the generated look: warm paper, near-black ink, one burnt orange accent. Swap them for your own as long as the new values pass the same checks.

It does not ban taste. A product can be playful, loud, dense or sparse and still follow every rule here. The rules remove the defaults that read as nobody deciding. They leave every real decision to you.

It does not promise that following it makes a product good. It promises the product will not look like it was made by not looking.

### 1.9 Checklist for Part 1

- The agent or reviewer has read 1.3 and 1.4.
- The tokens in 1.6 are in the codebase, or a documented replacement set is.
- `box-shadow` other than `none` returns zero results in source.
- Gradient functions return zero results in source.
- Emoji ranges return zero results in source and copy.
- No status pill with a dot exists in the component library.
- Shipped copy passes `scripts/lint.py` or the equivalent string check from Part 9.

## Part 2. Color, Surfaces and Depth

Color is where generated interfaces give themselves away first: color defaults are the easiest thing for a model to reproduce and the hardest for a reviewer to catch one decision at a time. The rules here are strict on purpose: no box shadows, no gradients, no glass, no glow, and one accent per product, outside the blue to violet band.

Every value in this Part uses the canonical tokens from the authoring guide. When this Part says `--paper`, it means `#F7F5F0` in light mode and `#141412` in dark mode. Contrast ratios quoted here were computed with the WCAG 2.x relative luminance formula, not estimated.

### 2.1 Why generated interfaces all look alike

A generated interface is the sum of library defaults. Each default was picked by a different team for a different reason, and none of them is wrong in isolation. Stacked together on one screen, they produce a page that a reader recognizes in under a second as unedited output: indigo button, bluish gray text, white card with a 16px corner and a soft shadow, a purple gradient behind the headline, Inter for everything.

Language models reproduce this stack because their training data is full of documentation snippets, starter templates and component library examples, which repeat the same handful of classes thousands of times. The most likely class for a button is the one from the docs, and so is the most likely class for a card. Every decision lands on the median, and a page made only of medians has no author.

#### The default stack, traced to its sources

| Symptom | Exact value | Where it comes from | Replace with |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indigo primary button | `bg-indigo-600` = `#4F46E5`, OKLCH hue 277 | Tailwind UI components and most Tailwind docs examples use indigo as the brand stand-in | One accent outside OKLCH 235 to 335, such as `--accent: #B4441C` |
| Blue focus ring | Tailwind v3 default ring color, `blue-500` at 50% opacity | The `ring` utility default; Laravel Breeze inputs add `focus:ring-indigo-500` | `outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px` |
| Bluish gray text | `text-gray-500` = `#6B7280`, OKLCH chroma 0.023 at hue 264 | Tailwind's `gray` scale is tinted toward blue; `slate` is tinted harder (chroma 0.04) | A neutral with a stated temperature, chroma under 0.012 |
| Navy dark mode | `#020817`, which is `hsl(222.2 84% 4.9%)` | The shadcn/ui slate theme dark `--background` | `--paper: #141412`, a warm near-black |
| Card with soft lift | `rounded-xl border shadow-sm`, or `rounded-2xl shadow-lg` | The shadcn/ui `Card` component; the Tailwind docs card examples | `border: 1px solid var(--rule)`, `border-radius: 2px`, no shadow |
| One typeface for all text | Inter, or Geist | Figma's default text style, Tailwind UI templates, Vercel starters | A deliberate pairing (Part 3), Plex Sans and Source Serif 4 here |
| Gradient hero | `from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500` | The Tailwind docs example for gradient color stops; the 2020 Stripe mesh header; the 2021 Linear site | A flat `--paper-2` band with a 2px `--ink` rule |
| Glass panel | `bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-md border-white/20` | macOS Big Sur vibrancy and the 2020 to 2021 Dribbble glass trend | An opaque `--paper` panel with a 1px `--rule-strong` border |
| Glow behind the headline | A blurred indigo circle at 20% to 40% opacity | Landing page kits such as Aceternity UI ("Spotlight", "Background Beams") | Nothing. Let the headline sit on the paper. |
| Green pulsing dot | `h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-green-500 animate-pulse` | Status page templates and dashboard kits | A text label with an icon: "Running", "Paused" |
| Purple for anything with a model behind it | Violet text, a four-point star icon, a violet to blue gradient | AI feature branding across large products since 2023 | The product's normal accent and a plain label |

Each row is one decision. A screen that hits three or more rows reads as generated, even if the rest of the work is careful.

#### Why indigo in particular

Indigo became the default brand color of the web because Tailwind UI, launched in 2020, used `indigo-600` as the placeholder brand in almost every component. The intent was "replace this with your brand". Thousands of projects never replaced it, then those projects became training data. The OKLCH values make the cluster visible:

| Tailwind color | Hex | OKLCH | White text contrast |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sky-500` | `#0EA5E9` | `0.685 0.148 237` | 2.77:1 |
| `blue-500` | `#3B82F6` | `0.623 0.188 260` | 3.68:1 |
| `blue-600` | `#2563EB` | `0.546 0.215 263` | 5.17:1 |
| `indigo-500` | `#6366F1` | `0.585 0.204 277` | 4.47:1 |
| `indigo-600` | `#4F46E5` | `0.511 0.230 277` | 6.29:1 |
| `violet-500` | `#8B5CF6` | `0.606 0.219 293` | 4.23:1 |
| `purple-500` | `#A855F7` | `0.627 0.233 304` | 3.96:1 |
| `fuchsia-500` | `#D946EF` | `0.667 0.259 322` | 3.46:1 |

All eight sit between OKLCH hue 237 and 322. That is the band this handbook bans for accents and gradients (2.3 gives the exact limits). Note the third column too: `indigo-500` with white text is 4.47:1, just under the 4.5:1 floor, so the most copied button color on the web fails contrast at its most copied weight.

#### Why the same card appears everywhere

The card is a white rectangle on a light gray page (`bg-gray-50`, `#F9FAFB`), corner radius 12px or 16px, padding 24px, and a shadow. The shadow does the work that a border or a tone step would do, and it does it badly: on a `#F9FAFB` page, a `shadow-sm` is a 1px smear at 5% black that most displays render as a faint gray line. The radius is large enough to read as "app", and small enough to read as "not a pill". Nobody chose it. It is `rounded-xl`, because that is what the component library ships.

```slop
<div class="min-h-screen bg-gray-50">
  <div class="mx-auto max-w-sm rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow-lg ring-1 ring-black/5">
    <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
      <span class="h-2 w-2 animate-pulse rounded-full bg-green-500"></span>
      <span class="text-xs font-medium text-green-600">LIVE</span>
    </div>
    <h3 class="mt-4 bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 bg-clip-text text-2xl font-bold text-transparent">
      Supercharge your workflow
    </h3>
    <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-gray-500">Seamless insights, powered by AI.</p>
    <button class="mt-6 w-full rounded-xl bg-indigo-600 px-4 py-2.5 text-white shadow-md hover:bg-indigo-500">
      Get started
    </button>
  </div>
</div>
```

Count the tells: gray-50 page, `rounded-2xl`, `shadow-lg`, `ring-black/5`, pulsing green dot, LIVE label, gradient text, indigo to purple, bluish gray body text, indigo button with a shadow, and a headline built from banned verbs. Eleven defaults in fourteen lines.

The same content, with every decision made on purpose:

```html
<article class="job">
  <p class="job-status"><svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16"><use href="#i-play"/></svg> Running since 09:14</p>
  <h3 class="job-title">Nightly invoice export</h3>
  <p class="job-meta">2,418 invoices written to <code>exports/2026-10-15.csv</code></p>
  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Open the file</button>
</article>
```

```css
.job {
  max-width: 28rem;
  padding: 24px;
  background: var(--paper);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
.job-status {
  display: flex;
  gap: 8px;
  align-items: center;
  margin: 0;
  font: 500 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--ok);
}
.job-title {
  margin: 16px 0 4px;
  font: 600 21px/1.2 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--ink);
}
.job-meta {
  margin: 0 0 24px;
  font: 400 14px/1.5 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--ink-2);
}
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
  color: var(--accent-ink);
  border: 1px solid var(--accent);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 8px 16px;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

One border, one accent, one status color paired with an icon and a time, and copy that says what happened. Nothing traces to a library default.

#### The fingerprint scan

Run this scan on any screen before review. Each line is a tell; each tell has a grep string so it can run in CI (2.11 has the full commands).

1. A primary color between OKLCH hue 235 and 335. Grep for `indigo-`, `violet-`, `purple-`, `blue-6`, `#6366F1`, `#4F46E5`.
2. Any CSS gradient or Tailwind gradient utility. Grep for `gradient`, `from-`, `via-`.
3. Any `box-shadow` other than `none`, any `shadow-*` utility, any `ring-*` utility (Tailwind rings compile to box shadows).
4. Corner radius above 4px on anything that is not a circle. Grep for `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl`, `rounded-3xl`.
5. `backdrop-filter`, `backdrop-blur`, or a translucent white panel (`bg-white/10`).
6. A blurred decorative element: `blur-3xl`, `filter: blur(` on a `div` with no content.
7. Gray text from a blue-tinted scale: `text-gray-500`, `text-slate-`, `#6B7280`, `#64748B`.
8. Dark mode background with blue chroma: `#020817`, `#0F172A`, `slate-900`, `slate-950`.
9. Status shown only by a colored dot, or an `animate-pulse` on a status element.
10. A LIVE, NEW or BETA pill with a dot.
11. A sparkle or star icon next to anything automated.
12. Emoji used as icons or bullets.

The target is zero. A system built from this Part gets there by default: its tokens hold none of the raw material.

#### Review checklist for 2.1

- The accent hue is outside OKLCH 235 to 335, and nobody on the team can say "we kept it from the template".
- No class or value in the markup can be found verbatim in the Tailwind UI or shadcn/ui example code without a deliberate reason written next to it.
- The neutral scale is the product's own, with a chroma under 0.012, not Tailwind `gray`, `slate` or `zinc`.
- The fingerprint scan returns zero hits.

### 2.2 The gradient ban

The rule has two levels. First, zero blue, purple, indigo or violet gradients, anywhere, in any medium, with no exceptions. Second, zero CSS gradients of any hue in interface chrome. A gradient that exists in a photograph is part of the photograph and is fine. A gradient written in CSS or a Tailwind class is not.

The first level exists because the blue to purple gradient is the single most reliable marker of generated work. The second level exists because every other gradient is one hue change away from the first, and because the replacements are better in every measurable way: they print, they pass contrast checks, they survive forced colors mode, and they do not band.

#### The forms a gradient takes

Each shape below is banned and has a direct replacement.

##### Background gradient on a hero or section

```slop
<section class="bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-600 via-purple-600 to-pink-500 py-24 text-white">
  <h1 class="text-5xl font-bold">The future of work is here</h1>
</section>
```

Source: the Tailwind docs color stop example and every SaaS template since 2020. The text contrast changes across the section: white on `pink-500` (`#EC4899`) is 3.53:1, white on `indigo-600` is 6.29:1, so the headline passes at one end and fails at the other.

Replacement: a flat band. Use `--paper-2` for a quiet band or `--ink` for an inverted band, with a rule to mark the edge.

```css
.hero {
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--ink);
  padding: 96px 16px 64px;
}
.hero h1 {
  max-width: 18ch;
  margin: 0;
  font: 600 56px/1.1 var(--font-serif);
  color: var(--ink);
}
.hero-inverted {
  background: var(--ink);
  color: var(--paper);
}
```

##### Gradient text

```slop
<h1 class="bg-gradient-to-r from-violet-600 to-indigo-600 bg-clip-text text-transparent">
  Ship faster
</h1>
```

Gradient text sets `color: transparent` and paints the letters with a clipped background. Contrast cannot be computed for it, so axe and Lighthouse report it as "needs review" and move on, which means nobody checks it. Selected text shows the selection color on transparent glyphs, and copied text loses its emphasis.

Replacement: emphasis through type. Use weight, size, a serif against a sans, or an accent underline.

```css
.headline em {
  font-style: normal;
  text-decoration-line: underline;
  text-decoration-color: var(--accent);
  text-decoration-thickness: 3px;
  text-underline-offset: 6px;
}
```

```html
<h1 class="headline">Invoices that reconcile <em>before</em> month end</h1>
```

##### Gradient border

```slop
<div class="rounded-2xl bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-fuchsia-500 p-[1px]">
  <div class="rounded-2xl bg-white p-6">Pro plan</div>
</div>
```

The wrapper trick (a 1px padded gradient parent behind a solid child), `border-image` with a gradient, and the `mask-composite: exclude` trick all produce the same result: an outline that glows from one hue to another.

Replacement: a solid border with a weight difference. To single out one item in a set, give it a 2px `--ink` border while the others keep 1px `--rule`, and say why in text.

```css
.plan { border: 1px solid var(--rule); padding: 24px; border-radius: var(--radius); }
.plan[data-recommended] {
  border: 2px solid var(--ink);
  padding: 23px; /* keeps outer size equal to the 1px plans */
}
.plan-flag {
  margin: 0 0 8px;
  font: 600 12px/1.3 var(--font-sans);
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--accent);
}
```

##### Mesh blobs

```slop
<div class="absolute -top-40 left-1/2 h-[600px] w-[600px] -translate-x-1/2 rounded-full bg-purple-500 opacity-30 blur-3xl"></div>
<div class="absolute top-20 right-0 h-[400px] w-[400px] rounded-full bg-blue-500 opacity-20 blur-3xl"></div>
```

Two to four large circles in blue, purple and pink, blurred by 64px or more and placed behind the hero copy. Source: the Stripe header of 2020, then every template that imitated it. A 64px blur on a 600px element forces the browser to rasterize a large offscreen layer, and on low-end phones it costs frames on every scroll.

Replacement: delete the elements. If the hero feels empty without them, the hero needs content: a product screenshot at 1:1 scale, a real photograph, a table of numbers, or a large set headline.

##### Radial glow behind the hero

```slop
.hero::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background: radial-gradient(ellipse at top, rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.35), transparent 60%);
}
```

The radial glow is the dark mode sibling of the mesh blob: an indigo ellipse fading out behind the headline on a near-black page. It says "launch page" and nothing else.

Replacement: none. A dark hero is `--paper` dark (`#141412`) with `--ink` dark text (`#ECE9E1`). Mark the end of the hero with a rule or a change of band.

##### Animated gradient button

```slop
.btn-shine {
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, #6366F1, #A855F7, #6366F1);
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  animation: shine 3s linear infinite;
}
@keyframes shine { to { background-position: -200% 0; } }
```

Also sold as "shimmer button", "border beam" and "rainbow button" in the component kits that grew out of the `magicui` and Aceternity collections. It animates `background-position`, which repaints on every frame, it runs forever, and it ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`. It breaks three motion rules from the authoring guide at once: animate only opacity and transform, stay at or under 150ms, and stop for reduced motion.

Replacement: a static fill and a 120ms tone change on hover.

```css
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
  color: var(--accent-ink);
  border: 1px solid var(--accent);
  transition: background-color 120ms ease-out;
}
.btn-primary:hover { background: #933511; border-color: #933511; } /* one step darker, see 2.3 */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .btn-primary { transition: none; }
}
```

##### Fading divider

```slop
<div class="h-px w-full bg-gradient-to-r from-transparent via-gray-300 to-transparent"></div>
```

This one hides well because it is gray and thin. It is the most common gradient in generated layouts after the hero, and it is still a gradient. A line that fades out at both ends tells the reader the designer was not sure where the line should stop.

Replacement: a rule with defined ends. Either full width of the container, or a short fixed length.

```css
.divider { border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); margin: 32px 0; }
.divider-short { width: 64px; border-top: 2px solid var(--ink); margin: 24px 0; }
```

##### Image scrim

```slop
.card-image::after {
  background: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(0,0,0,0.8), transparent);
}
```

The dark fade at the bottom of a photo, there to make white caption text legible. It darkens a third of every photo and the text contrast still depends on the image.

Replacement: move the text off the image. A caption bar below the photo has a known background and a known ratio.

```css
.figure { margin: 0; border: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.figure img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
.figure figcaption {
  padding: 8px 12px;
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
  font: 400 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--ink-2);
}
```

If the text must sit on the image (a poster, a cover), set it on a solid block of `--ink` with `--paper` text. The ratio is then 16.0:1, whatever the photo does.

##### Conic spinners and gradient rings

A conic gradient rotated forever is the spinner of choice in generated code; aurora and beam backgrounds are the same idea at page size. Use a plain stroked SVG arc in `--ink-2`, rotated with `transform`, and a static "Loading" label under reduced motion. Delete the moving backgrounds.

#### Why the ban covers every hue

A warm orange to red gradient avoids the blue-violet tell, but it keeps every other cost:

1. Banding. An 8-bit display has 256 levels per channel. A gradient between two close colors across 1200px has fewer distinct steps than pixels, and visible bands appear every 20 to 40px on most laptop panels. Designers add noise to hide it, which adds a second banned effect.
2. Contrast. Text on a gradient has a different ratio at every pixel. Automated checkers cannot measure it and skip it.
3. Print. Browsers drop background colors and images when printing unless `print-color-adjust: exact` is set, so gradient-led pages print as white boxes with missing text.
4. Tone. A gradient implies light falling on a surface. The rest of this system draws flat surfaces separated by rules. A single gradient makes everything else look unfinished.
5. Drift. Allow one gradient and a year later there are twelve, drifting toward the default hues.

#### What to use instead

Every job a gradient does has a flat replacement.

| Job the gradient was doing | Flat replacement |
|---|---|
| Making the hero feel "designed" | Large serif headline (56px), a 2px `--ink` rule, a real image or a product screenshot |
| Separating sections | Alternate `--paper` and `--paper-2` bands, with a 1px `--rule` at each edge |
| Highlighting the recommended plan | 2px `--ink` border plus a text flag ("Picked by 61% of teams") |
| Making a button look clickable | A solid `--accent` fill with `--accent-ink` text, 40px tall, a verb label |
| Adding texture | Typography: numerals, a dateline, small caps labels, a visible grid of rules |
| Showing brand color | One full-bleed `--accent` block per page, used once |
| Making a dark page less flat | Tone steps: `#141412`, `#1E1D1A`, `#2A2925`, plus `--rule` lines |
| Drawing focus to a number | Size and weight: 40px tabular numerals in `--ink`, label in 12px `--ink-3` |

The most underused replacement is the full-bleed accent block. Use it once per page, for one thing, at full saturation, with no tint, fade or overlay:

```css
.callout-band {
  background: var(--accent);
  color: var(--accent-ink);
  padding: 48px 16px;
}
.callout-band a {
  color: var(--accent-ink);
  text-decoration-thickness: 2px;
  text-underline-offset: 4px;
}
```

White on `#B4441C` is 5.55:1, so body text and links in the band pass AA.

#### Review checklist for 2.2

- `rg -n 'gradient'` over the styles and templates returns zero lines outside comments and lint config.
- No `from-*`, `via-*` or `to-*` color stop classes remain.
- No element exists only to hold a blur or a glow.
- No text is `color: transparent` or `text-transparent`.
- Every section break is a rule, a tone step or white space with a defined size.
- Photos carry their own gradients; CSS adds none on top.

### 2.3 Building a palette that is not the default

A palette has three parts: a neutral scale that does most of the work, one accent, and four semantic colors. Build them in that order. Most screens are 90% neutral by area, so the neutral scale decides how the product feels far more than the accent does.

#### Step 1: neutrals with a temperature

A neutral scale with zero chroma looks like an unstyled browser. A neutral scale tinted blue looks like Tailwind. Pick a hue on purpose and keep the chroma low enough that the scale still reads as gray.

Rules:

- Pick a hue for the neutrals. Warm: OKLCH 60 to 95 (paper, cream, stone). Cool without blue: OKLCH 160 to 200 (green-gray, slate-green). Avoid 235 to 335 for neutrals with chroma above 0.012.
- Keep chroma between 0.004 and 0.012 for surfaces, and under 0.008 for text. Text with visible chroma looks muddy.
- Set lightness by role, in OKLCH L, not by eye.

The canonical scale, measured:

| Token | Hex | OKLCH | Role | Contrast on `--paper` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#F7F5F0` | `0.970 0.007 89` | Page background | 1.00:1 |
| `--paper-2` | `#EFECE4` | `0.943 0.011 90` | Recessed: table header, sidebar, code | 1.08:1 |
| `--paper-3` | `#E5E1D6` | `0.910 0.015 90` | Pressed, selected | 1.20:1 |
| `--rule` | `#D9D5CB` | `0.873 0.014 89` | Default 1px border | 1.34:1 |
| `--ink-3` | `#6F6C64` | `0.531 0.013 90` | Tertiary text, placeholders, input borders | 4.81:1 |
| `--ink-2` | `#4A4843` | `0.402 0.009 89` | Secondary text | 8.38:1 |
| `--ink` | `#1A1A18` | `0.217 0.004 107` | Primary text, strong rules | 16.00:1 |

The surface steps are about 0.03 apart in L (0.970, 0.943, 0.910). Below 0.02, two adjacent surfaces look like the same color on an uncalibrated laptop panel. Above 0.05, the recessed surfaces start to look like separate cards. Hold to 0.025 to 0.035 per step.

To build a scale at a different temperature, keep the L values and change the hue:

```css
/* Spruce neutrals: same L steps as the canonical scale, hue 177 to 184 */
:root {
  --paper:   oklch(0.970 0.008 177); /* #F0F7F5 */
  --paper-2: oklch(0.943 0.012 178); /* #E4EFEC */
  --paper-3: oklch(0.910 0.015 182); /* #D7E5E2 */
  --rule:    oklch(0.873 0.016 177); /* #CBD9D5 */
  --ink-3:   oklch(0.525 0.014 184); /* #626D6B */
  --ink-2:   oklch(0.401 0.011 179); /* #424A48 */
  --ink:     oklch(0.214 0.005 174); /* #171A19 */
}
```

Ship the hex values, not only the `oklch()` calls, in any context where the color must match across tools (Figma, email, PDF export, native apps).

#### Step 2: one accent outside the blue-violet band

Pick one accent hue for the product. Not two, not a primary and a secondary. Every extra accent halves the meaning of the first.

The hue bands, in OKLCH hue degrees, with rough HSL equivalents:

| OKLCH hue | HSL hue (approx.) | Family | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 to 30 | 340 to 10 | Raspberry, crimson, red | Allowed. Red conflicts with `--bad`; see Newsprint below. |
| 30 to 60 | 10 to 30 | Vermilion, burnt orange, rust | Allowed. The canonical accent sits at 39. |
| 60 to 100 | 30 to 55 | Ochre, amber, mustard | Allowed. Conflicts with `--warn`; move warn toward orange. |
| 100 to 140 | 55 to 95 | Olive, moss, chartreuse | Allowed. Needs low L to pass contrast. |
| 140 to 170 | 95 to 160 | Green, forest | Allowed. Conflicts with `--ok`; move ok toward yellow-green or teal. |
| 170 to 215 | 160 to 190 | Teal, petrol, sea green | Allowed. |
| 215 to 235 | 190 to 200 | Cyan-blue | Caution. At chroma above 0.10 it reads as Tailwind `sky`. |
| 235 to 335 | 200 to 300 | Blue, indigo, violet, purple, fuchsia | Banned for accents, gradients and highlights. |
| 335 to 360 | 300 to 340 | Magenta, rose | Caution. Keep L below 0.55 so it reads as raspberry, not fuchsia. |

HSL hue does not map linearly to OKLCH hue, which is why the second column is approximate. Measure in OKLCH. A quick check in the browser console:

```js
// Paste in DevTools. Prints the OKLCH hue of any hex color.
function oklchHue(hex) {
  const c = hex.replace("#", "").match(/../g).map(h => parseInt(h, 16) / 255)
    .map(v => (v <= 0.04045 ? v / 12.92 : ((v + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4));
  const [r, g, b] = c;
  const l = Math.cbrt(0.4122214708 * r + 0.5363325363 * g + 0.0514459929 * b);
  const m = Math.cbrt(0.2119034982 * r + 0.6806995451 * g + 0.1073969566 * b);
  const s = Math.cbrt(0.0883024619 * r + 0.2817188376 * g + 0.6299787005 * b);
  const A = 1.9779984951 * l - 2.4285922050 * m + 0.4505937099 * s;
  const B = 0.0259040371 * l + 0.7827717662 * m - 0.8086757660 * s;
  return { chroma: Math.hypot(A, B).toFixed(3), hue: ((Math.atan2(B, A) * 180 / Math.PI) + 360) % 360 };
}
oklchHue("#B4441C"); // { chroma: "0.154", hue: 38.5... }
oklchHue("#6366F1"); // { chroma: "0.204", hue: 277.1... }
```

Accent rules:

- The accent text color passes 4.5:1 on `--paper`. The canonical `#B4441C` is 5.09:1.
- Text on the accent passes 4.5:1. White on `#B4441C` is 5.55:1.
- The accent appears on at most 10% of a screen by area. Primary button, current navigation item, links, one highlight. Not headings, not icons in a feature grid, not borders on every card.
- Brand marks may use colors outside these rules. The interface accent may not.

#### Step 3: derive the steps in OKLCH

A product needs five to ten steps of its accent: a wash for highlighted rows, a light step for selected backgrounds, the base, a hover step, a pressed step, and text steps for both themes. Derive them in OKLCH, holding the hue and adjusting lightness and chroma.

Do not derive steps in HSL. HSL lightness ignores how bright a hue looks. `hsl(60 100% 50%)` (`#FFFF00`) and `hsl(240 100% 50%)` (`#0000FF`) share the same L of 50%, yet the yellow has a contrast of 1.07:1 against white and the blue has 8.59:1. A ramp built with HSL lightness gives a different contrast at every hue, so swapping the accent breaks every text pairing in the system. OKLCH L tracks perceived lightness: those two colors measure 0.968 and 0.452.

The canonical accent ramp, hue held at 39, chroma rising to a peak at L 0.62 and tapering at both ends:

| Step | Hex | OKLCH | On `--paper` | White on it | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | `#FFF2EE` | `0.970 0.015 39` | 1.00:1 | 1.09:1 | Row highlight wash |
| 200 | `#FEE1D7` | `0.931 0.035 39` | 1.14:1 | 1.24:1 | Selected background |
| 300 | `#FBC6B5` | `0.869 0.065 39` | 1.39:1 | 1.52:1 | Tag fill with `--ink` text |
| 400 | `#F2A48B` | `0.789 0.100 39` | 1.84:1 | 2.01:1 | Chart fill |
| 500 | `#E47E5D` | `0.699 0.135 39` | 2.59:1 | 2.82:1 | Chart fill, dark mode text |
| 600 | `#D15F37` | `0.620 0.154 39` | 3.57:1 | 3.89:1 | Large text only, icons |
| 700 | `#B4441C` | `0.535 0.154 39` | 5.09:1 | 5.55:1 | `--accent`: buttons, links |
| 800 | `#933511` | `0.459 0.135 39` | 6.99:1 | 7.61:1 | Hover |
| 900 | `#71280C` | `0.381 0.110 39` | 9.58:1 | 10.44:1 | Pressed, text on wash |
| 950 | `#4E1C0B` | `0.300 0.080 39` | 12.89:1 | 14.05:1 | Text on 200 and 300 |

Chroma tapers at the light end because a light color at full chroma falls outside the sRGB gamut and gets clipped unevenly by each browser. It tapers at the dark end because dark colors at high chroma look neon rather than deep. Peak chroma near L 0.55 to 0.65 holds for reds and oranges. For yellows and ochres, peak chroma sits higher, near L 0.80, and the hue should rotate 10 to 15 degrees toward orange as it darkens (from 90 to about 75), or the dark steps turn olive.

```css
:root {
  --orange-100: #FFF2EE;
  --orange-200: #FEE1D7;
  --orange-300: #FBC6B5;
  --orange-700: #B4441C;
  --orange-800: #933511;
  --orange-900: #71280C;
  --orange-950: #4E1C0B;

  --accent: var(--orange-700);
  --accent-hover: var(--orange-800);
  --accent-press: var(--orange-900);
  --accent-wash: var(--orange-100);
  --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
}

@supports (color: oklch(0 0 0)) {
  :root {
    --accent: oklch(0.535 0.154 39);
    --accent-hover: oklch(0.459 0.135 39);
  }
}
```

Primitives (`--orange-700`) hold the values. Roles (`--accent`) point at primitives. Components only ever read roles. That is the full rule for color tokens, and 2.11 shows it in a Tailwind config.

#### Step 4: contrast targets

Use WCAG 2.2 contrast as the floor:

- Body text and any text under 24px regular or 18.66px bold: 4.5:1 against its actual background.
- Large text (24px regular, or 18.66px bold and up): 3:1.
- UI component boundaries and states, and graphics needed to understand content (input borders, checkbox outlines, focus indicators, chart marks, icons that carry meaning): 3:1 against adjacent colors.
- Aim for 7:1 on body text where the palette allows it. The canonical `--ink` and `--ink-2` both clear it.

Measure every pairing that ships, not just text on `--paper`. Text moves onto recessed and selected surfaces, and the ratio drops each time:

| Foreground | On `--paper` | On `--paper-2` | On `--paper-3` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ink` `#1A1A18` | 16.00:1 | 14.76:1 | 13.34:1 |
| `--ink-2` `#4A4843` | 8.38:1 | 7.74:1 | 6.99:1 |
| `--ink-3` `#6F6C64` | 4.81:1 | 4.44:1 | 4.01:1 |
| `--accent` `#B4441C` | 5.09:1 | 4.70:1 | 4.25:1 |
| `--ok` `#2F6B3A` | 5.87:1 | 5.42:1 | 4.89:1 |
| `--warn` `#8A6100` | 5.08:1 | 4.69:1 | 4.24:1 |
| `--bad` `#A3271F` | 6.72:1 | 6.20:1 | 5.61:1 |

Three failures fall out of this table, and each becomes a rule:

1. `--ink-3` fails on `--paper-2` (4.44:1) and `--paper-3` (4.01:1). Tertiary text appears only on `--paper`. On recessed or selected surfaces, use `--ink-2` for secondary and tertiary text alike.
2. `--accent` and `--warn` fail on `--paper-3`. A selected row does not contain accent-colored text or warn text at 14px. Use `--ink` for the text and put the meaning in an icon or a label.
3. `--rule` against `--paper` is 1.34:1. That is correct for a decorative divider and wrong for a form field. WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 on the boundary that identifies a control, so text inputs, selects and checkboxes use `border-color: var(--ink-3)` (4.81:1).

```css
.field input,
.field select,
.field textarea {
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
  border: 1px solid var(--ink-3);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
.field input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-3); opacity: 1; }
.field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
```

APCA, the candidate method for WCAG 3, rates `--ink-2` on `--paper` at about Lc 85 and `--ink-3` at about Lc 70. Under APCA guidance Lc 75 is the floor for body text columns, so `--ink-3` is fine for 14px metadata and captions and wrong for paragraphs. The same conclusion as WCAG 2: tertiary ink is for labels, never for prose.

#### Eight complete palettes

Each palette below is a full token set: three surfaces, a rule, three inks, one accent, text on accent, and three status colors. None is led by blue or purple. Every ratio was measured. Copy a palette whole; do not mix steps from two palettes, because the L values were matched across each set.

The tables give the ratio against `--paper` first and `--paper-2` second.

##### 1. Ledger (the canonical set)

Warm cream paper, warm near-black ink, burnt orange accent at OKLCH hue 39. For finance tools, editorial products, documentation, anything read for a long time.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F7F5F0;  --paper-2: #EFECE4;  --paper-3: #E5E1D6;  --rule: #D9D5CB;
  --ink: #1A1A18;    --ink-2: #4A4843;    --ink-3: #6F6C64;
  --accent: #B4441C; --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #2F6B3A;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #A3271F;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.00 / 14.76 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.81 / 4.44 |
| `--accent` as text | 5.09 / 4.70 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 5.55 |

Rule specific to Ledger: `--ink-3` is never placed on `--paper-2`.

##### 2. Newsprint

Near-neutral cool paper (hue 250 at chroma 0.003, far below the 0.012 limit, so it reads as gray), black ink, signal red accent at hue 30.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F4F5F7;  --paper-2: #EBECEE;  --paper-3: #E0E1E3;  --rule: #D4D5D7;
  --ink: #181A1B;    --ink-2: #464849;    --ink-3: #696A6C;
  --accent: #CA3324; --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #2F6B3A;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #901F1A;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.01 / 14.77 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.96 / 4.58 |
| `--accent` as text | 4.80 / 4.43 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 5.24 |
| `--bad` | 8.03 / 7.41 |

A red accent creates a specific failure: every red primary button reads as "Delete". Newsprint solves it by role. Red is for the masthead rule, links, the current navigation item and highlighted figures. Primary buttons are `--ink` filled with `--paper` text (16.01:1). `--bad` is pushed darker (L 0.43) and always carries an icon and a word, so a destructive action never looks like the brand color. Red links fail on `--paper-2` (4.43:1), so links inside recessed panels use `--ink` with an underline.

##### 3. Spruce

Green-gray paper at hue 177 to 184, teal-green accent at hue 175. For health, logistics, field operations, anything that wants calm without blue.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F0F7F5;  --paper-2: #E4EFEC;  --paper-3: #D7E5E2;  --rule: #CBD9D5;
  --ink: #171A19;    --ink-2: #424A48;    --ink-3: #626D6B;
  --accent: #196958; --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #416B25;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #A3271F;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.13 / 14.90 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.93 / 4.56 |
| `--accent` as text | 6.03 / 5.58 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 6.56 |

The accent is green, so `--ok` moves from hue 148 to 135 (`#416B25`, a yellow-green) to separate it from the brand, and `--ok` text always sits next to a check icon. If the product shows many success states, pick a different palette: green accent plus green success is a weak pairing however carefully the hues are split.

##### 4. Lichen

Yellow-gray paper at hue 110, olive accent at hue 120. For agriculture, outdoor, archives, print-adjacent products.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F5F6ED;  --paper-2: #ECEDE0;  --paper-3: #E2E3D1;  --rule: #D6D7C5;
  --ink: #1A1A16;    --ink-2: #48493F;    --ink-3: #6B6C5D;
  --accent: #566613; --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #176A4E;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #A3271F;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.03 / 14.76 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.91 / 4.52 |
| `--accent` as text | 5.83 / 5.37 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 6.35 |

Olive only works at low lightness. Above L 0.55 it turns into a yellow-green that looks like a warning light. Keep the accent at L 0.48 and use it as a fill, not as small text on `--paper-3`. `--ok` moves to hue 165, a deep sea green, to keep it apart from the olive.

##### 5. Raspberry

Faintly pink paper at hue 17, raspberry accent at OKLCH hue 2 (HSL 336). For consumer products, publishing, food, anything that needs warmth without orange.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #FAF3F3;  --paper-2: #F4E9E9;  --paper-3: #ECDDDD;  --rule: #E0D1D1;
  --ink: #1C1918;    --ink-2: #4D4645;    --ink-3: #736767;
  --accent: #A02857; --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --ok: #2F6B3A;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #A14206;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 15.96 / 14.71 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.96 / 4.57 |
| `--accent` as text | 6.53 / 6.02 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 7.15 |

The accent sits at hue 2, 40 degrees clear of fuchsia (322). Pushing it toward 340 or raising its lightness above 0.55 turns it into Tailwind `pink-500` (`#EC4899`, hue 354, L 0.656), which is the third stop of the default gradient. `--bad` rotates to hue 45 (`#A14206`, a rust) to stay distinct from the accent.

##### 6. Signal

Graphite neutrals and a yellow accent at hue 90 that is used only as a fill. For tools used in bright light, transit, construction, safety, kiosks.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F6F5F2;  --paper-2: #EDECE8;  --paper-3: #E3E1DB;  --rule: #D7D5CF;
  --ink: #1A1918;    --ink-2: #484845;    --ink-3: #6B6A66;
  --accent: #F4C423;       /* fill only */
  --accent-ink: #1A1918;   /* text on the fill */
  --accent-text: #7E5D00;  /* when the accent must be text */
  --ok: #2F6B3A;     --warn: #A05000;     --bad: #A3271F;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.10 / 14.85 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.97 / 4.58 |
| `--accent` as text | 1.51 (fails, never used as text) |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 10.67 |
| `--accent-text` | 5.58 / 5.14 |

A bright accent needs a split token. `--accent` is the fill for the primary button and the selected tab underline; `--accent-text` is a dark gold for links and highlighted figures. The yellow button with ink text (10.67:1) is the most legible primary button in this list. A yellow fill alone is 1.51:1 against the paper, below the 3:1 boundary rule, so the yellow button carries a 1px `--ink` border. `--warn` moves to hue 54 (`#A05000`, a burnt amber) so it does not look like the brand.

##### 7. Mono

Zero-chroma neutrals and no chromatic accent at all. The accent is the ink. For developer tools, legal, reference, and any product where the only color on screen should be status.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #F5F5F5;  --paper-2: #ECECEC;  --paper-3: #E1E1E1;  --rule: #D5D5D5;
  --ink: #191919;    --ink-2: #484848;    --ink-3: #6A6A6A;
  --accent: #191919; --accent-ink: #F5F5F5;
  --ok: #2F6B3A;     --warn: #8A6100;     --bad: #A3271F;
}
a { color: var(--ink); text-decoration-line: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 3px; }
a:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 2px; }
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 16.13 / 14.88 |
| `--ink-3` | 4.96 / 4.58 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 16.13 |

In Mono, links are distinguished by underline, never by color, which satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 without effort. Status colors become the only hues on screen, so they read instantly. Mono is the safest palette for a team that keeps drifting back to indigo: there is no accent slot left to drift with.

##### 8. Ochre Night (dark-first)

For products used mostly at night or in dim rooms: monitoring, audio, broadcast, trading floors. Warm near-black at hue 67 to 81, ochre accent at hue 75. This is a primary dark palette, not a dark mode of a light one.

```css
:root {
  --paper: #141210;  --paper-2: #1E1B18;  --paper-3: #292622;  --rule: #33302B;
  --ink: #EDE7DF;    --ink-2: #B7B0A7;    --ink-3: #918B83;
  --accent: #E1A447; --accent-ink: #141210;
  --ok: #75B683;     --warn: #EB883B;     --bad: #E66F62;
}
```

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| `--ink` | 15.21 / 13.95 |
| `--ink-3` | 5.54 / 5.08 |
| `--accent` as text | 8.55 / 7.84 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 8.55 |
| `--warn` | 7.22 / 6.63 |

On dark grounds, `--ink-3` keeps passing on `--paper-2`, which makes dark palettes more forgiving for tertiary text than light ones. The ochre accent and an amber warning would collide, so `--warn` moves to hue 55 (`#EB883B`, orange).

#### Using the canonical tokens

Components read role tokens. They never contain a hex value, a Tailwind palette class (`bg-orange-700`) or a raw `oklch()` call.

| Element | Background | Text | Border |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page | `--paper` | `--ink` | |
| Body copy | | `--ink` | |
| Metadata, captions | | `--ink-2`, or `--ink-3` on `--paper` only | |
| Sidebar, table header, code block | `--paper-2` | `--ink`, `--ink-2` | `--rule` on the shared edge |
| Selected row, pressed button | `--paper-3` | `--ink` | |
| Card, panel | `--paper` | `--ink` | `--rule` |
| Menu, popover, dialog | `--paper` | `--ink` | `--rule-strong` |
| Tooltip, toast | `--ink` | `--paper` | |
| Text input | `--paper` | `--ink` | `--ink-3` (3:1 rule) |
| Primary button | `--accent` | `--accent-ink` | `--accent` |
| Secondary button | `--paper` | `--ink` | `--ink` |
| Link | | `--accent`, underlined | |
| Focus | | | `outline: 2px solid var(--focus)` |

Derived tokens are computed from roles, so they change when the palette changes:

```css
:root {
  --accent-wash: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 8%, var(--paper));
  --ok-wash:     color-mix(in oklab, var(--ok) 8%, var(--paper));
  --warn-wash:   color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 8%, var(--paper));
  --bad-wash:    color-mix(in oklab, var(--bad) 8%, var(--paper));
  --scrim:       color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 56%, transparent);
}
```

Mix in `oklab`, not `oklch`. The paper has a hue of its own (89 for Ledger) at almost no chroma, and `oklch` interpolation rotates the result's hue toward it. An 8% mix of `--bad` (hue 29) into `--paper` in `oklch` lands at hue 84, a beige with no red in it. The same mix in `oklab` gives `#F2E5DE`, a visible red wash. Write the hex fallback next to each derived token for browsers older than 2023, which lack `color-mix()`.

#### Review checklist for 2.3

- The neutral scale has a stated hue and a chroma under 0.012, with surface steps 0.025 to 0.035 apart in OKLCH L.
- There is exactly one accent, its OKLCH hue is outside 235 to 335, and it covers under 10% of any screen.
- Accent steps were derived in OKLCH with the hue held (or rotated toward orange, for yellows).
- Every text and surface pairing that ships was measured, including on `--paper-2` and `--paper-3`.
- Input, checkbox and select borders are at 3:1 or higher (`--ink-3` or darker), not `--rule`.
- No component contains a hex value or a Tailwind palette class.
- Bright accents are split into a fill token and a text token.

### 2.4 Semantic color

Semantic colors tell the reader the state of something: it worked, it needs attention, it failed. Use exactly three hues for this: `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad`. A fourth "info" blue is not part of the system. Information is the default state of all text, so it gets the default color: `--ink`, with an info icon when it needs marking.

#### The four roles

| Role | Light | Dark | Icon shape | Word | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ok | `#2F6B3A` | `#7FB38A` | Check in a circle | Done, Saved, Paid, Running | Completed actions, healthy systems |
| warn | `#8A6100` | `#D9A93A` | Triangle with a bar | Check, Expires, Low, Slow | States that will become failures if ignored |
| bad | `#A3271F` | `#E0705F` | Octagon or circle with a cross | Failed, Declined, Down, Missing | Failures, destructive actions, blocking errors |
| info | `--ink` | `--ink` | Circle with an "i" | Note, Tip | Neutral notices |

The info role costs nothing and removes the most common source of stray blue in generated interfaces: the `bg-blue-50 text-blue-700` info banner from Tailwind UI's alert component.

#### Never color alone

WCAG 1.4.1 forbids color as the only way to convey information. The reason is measurable. Under a simulation of deuteranopia (Machado 2009, full severity), the canonical `--ok` `#2F6B3A` becomes `#645D3D` and `--bad` `#A3271F` becomes `#6C6019`. Their perceptual distance (OKLab ΔE) drops from 22.8 to 4.2, about the same as two adjacent steps of a gray ramp. The two colors also share almost the same lightness (OKLCH L 0.475 and 0.473), so a grayscale print shows no difference at all. Default Tailwind `green-500` and `red-500` fare no better: their deuteranopia ΔE is 7.5.

So every status carries at least two of these three, and in practice all three:

1. A word. "Failed", not just a red row.
2. An icon with a distinct shape. A check, a triangle and an octagon differ in silhouette at 16px; three identical circles in different colors do not.
3. The color.

```html
<p class="status status-bad">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16"><use href="#i-octagon-x"/></svg>
  <span>Payment failed</span>
  <span class="status-detail">Card declined by issuer, code 05</span>
</p>
```

```css
.status {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 0;
  font: 500 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans);
}
.status .icon { flex: none; align-self: center; }
.status-ok   { color: var(--ok); }
.status-warn { color: var(--warn); }
.status-bad  { color: var(--bad); }
.status-detail { font-weight: 400; color: var(--ink-2); }
```

The detail line is `--ink-2`, not the status color. Color marks the state word; the explanation is plain text, which keeps long messages readable and keeps the colored area small.

#### Status without glowing dots

The green dot (`h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-green-500`), often pulsing (`animate-pulse`), often beside an uppercase "LIVE" in a pill, is a dashboard kit default. It fails in five ways: an 8px circle of `green-500` has 2.28:1 contrast on white, below the 3:1 graphics floor; it says nothing without the label; the pulse is decoration that never stops; the pill and dot shapes are identical across states, so only hue separates them; and LIVE is vague about what is live and since when.

```slop
<span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full bg-green-50 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-green-700 ring-1 ring-green-600/20">
  <span class="h-1.5 w-1.5 animate-pulse rounded-full bg-green-500"></span>
  LIVE
</span>
```

Replace it with a specific statement:

```html
<p class="status status-ok">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16"><use href="#i-broadcast"/></svg>
  <span>Streaming</span>
  <span class="status-detail">since 18:02, 1,204 watching</span>
</p>
```

When a dense table needs a compact marker in every row, use a shape glyph (an SVG check, triangle or square at 12px) in the status color, followed by the word in `--ink`. Never animate it. A state change can be announced once with an `aria-live="polite"` region and a single 150ms opacity fade on the changed row, then nothing.

#### Badges and tags

A badge is a short label with a border, not a pill. Keep the 2px radius. Use the status color for the border and the text, with the wash behind it, or skip the wash.

```css
.badge {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 4px;
  padding: 2px 6px;
  font: 600 12px/1.3 var(--font-sans);
  letter-spacing: 0.02em;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--paper);
}
.badge-ok   { color: var(--ok);   background: var(--ok-wash);   } /* #E6E9E0, text 5.20:1 */
.badge-warn { color: var(--warn); background: var(--warn-wash); } /* #EEE9DE, text 4.58:1 */
.badge-bad  { color: var(--bad);  background: var(--bad-wash);  } /* #F2E5DE, text 5.94:1 */
```

The wash stays at 8%. At 12%, the warn text drops to 4.34:1 and fails. In dark mode the same 8% mix is too faint to see; use 14%, which gives `#212720` for ok (text 6.34:1), `#2B261A` for warn (6.94:1) and `#2D201C` for bad (4.98:1).

Neutral tags (categories, labels, filters) do not use status colors. They are `--paper-2` with `--ink` text and no border, or `--paper` with a 1px `--rule` border.

#### Alerts and banners

The Tailwind UI alert is a tinted box with a 4px colored left border (`border-l-4 border-yellow-400 bg-yellow-50`). It has become a tell of its own. Use a full 1px border in the status color, the icon, a bold first sentence that names the problem, and a second sentence that says what to do.

```html
<div class="alert alert-warn" role="status">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" width="20" height="20"><use href="#i-triangle"/></svg>
  <div>
    <p class="alert-title">Your card expires on 31 October.</p>
    <p class="alert-body">Add a new card before then so the November invoice is paid on time. <a href="/billing">Update card</a></p>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.alert {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 20px 1fr;
  gap: 12px;
  padding: 16px;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--paper);
}
.alert-warn { color: var(--warn); }
.alert-bad  { color: var(--bad); }
.alert-title { margin: 0; font: 600 16px/1.4 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink); }
.alert-body  { margin: 4px 0 0; font: 400 14px/1.5 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink-2); }
.alert a { color: var(--ink); }
```

The border and the icon carry the state color. The text is ink. A warning at `#8A6100` across 40 words of body text would sit at 5.08:1, legal but tiring, and would make the whole box shout.

#### Form validation

- Mark the field with a 2px `--bad` border (pad 1px less to keep the size), set `aria-invalid="true"`, and point `aria-describedby` at the message.
- Put the message directly under the field, in `--bad`, starting with an icon, and say how to fix it: "Enter a date after 1 January 2026", not "Invalid input".
- Keep the label in `--ink`. A red label plus a red border plus red text turns the whole field into an alarm.
- Do not use a green border for valid fields. A field the user filled in correctly needs no reward.

```css
.field input[aria-invalid="true"] {
  border: 2px solid var(--bad);
  padding: 7px 11px; /* 8px 12px minus the extra 1px of border */
}
.field-error {
  display: flex;
  gap: 6px;
  margin: 6px 0 0;
  font: 500 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--bad);
}
```

#### Numbers that go up and down

Color a change by its meaning, not its direction. Revenue up is good; costs up, latency up and churn up are bad. A rule that paints every positive delta green will one day paint a doubled error rate green.

- Always print the sign: "+4.2%", and use a true minus (`&minus;`, U+2212) for negatives so the column aligns with tabular numerals.
- Put the meaning in words when it matters: "+38 ms slower".
- When the direction has no fixed meaning (a population count, a temperature), show the change in `--ink-2` with no status color.

#### Review checklist for 2.4

- Exactly three status hues exist. Info notices use ink and an icon.
- Every status shows a word and a distinct icon shape, and still reads correctly in grayscale.
- No status dot pulses, glows or stands alone. No LIVE pill.
- Status color is applied to the icon, the border and the state word, never to paragraphs.
- Washes are 8% in light mode and 14% in dark mode, mixed in `oklab`, and every text color on them passes 4.5:1.
- Deltas are colored by meaning, with an explicit sign.

### 2.5 Depth without shadows

Depth tells the reader which surface is on top, which surface belongs to which, and what will move when they interact. This system draws depth with four signals and never with shadows:

1. Tone. Steps between `--paper`, `--paper-2` and `--paper-3`.
2. Edge. A border, its weight and its color.
3. Offset. Spacing, overlap and position.
4. Inversion. An `--ink` surface with `--paper` text, for the few things that sit above everything.

#### Why shadows go

- Forced colors. In Windows contrast themes (`forced-colors: active`), browsers force `box-shadow` to `none`. A menu drawn with a shadow and no border loses its outline completely and merges into the page. A menu drawn with a border keeps it, recolored to the system `CanvasText`.
- Dark mode. A black shadow on `#141412` has nothing to darken. Material Design hit this and switched dark surfaces to lighter tonal overlays; every shadow-led system ends up maintaining a second depth language for dark mode.
- Print. Shadows are dropped or rasterized badly by print engines and PDF exporters.
- Ambiguity. A blurred edge has no position. A border tells the eye exactly where a hit target ends; `shadow-lg` spreads 15px of gray beyond the box, so the visible extent and the clickable extent differ.
- Cost. Large blur radii on many elements repaint on scroll and on every hover lift.
- Default. `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md` and `shadow-lg` are the Tailwind defaults behind every generated card. Removing them removes the tell at the root.

#### The level table

| Level | What lives there | Light mode | Dark mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| -2 Pressed | Selected row, pressed button, active tab panel background | `--paper-3` | `--paper-3` (lighter than page) |
| -1 Recessed | Sidebar, table header, code block, input group, footer band | `--paper-2`, `--rule` on the shared edge | `--paper-2` |
| 0 Page | Page, cards, panels, content | `--paper`, cards with 1px `--rule` | `--paper`, cards with 1px `--rule` |
| +1 Floating | Menu, dropdown, popover, dialog, sticky header once stuck | `--paper` plus 1px `--rule-strong` | `--paper-2` plus 1px `--rule-strong` |
| +2 Transient | Tooltip, toast, drag preview label | `--ink` with `--paper` text | `--ink` with `--paper` text |

Two languages are at work. Inset language says "this is part of the page, pushed in": a darker tone in light mode, no strong border, at most a 1px `--rule` on the edge it shares with the page. Outset language says "this sits on top of the page": a strong 1px border in `--rule-strong`, the page tone or one step lighter, and a position that overlaps content. Do not mix them. A recessed sidebar with a strong border reads as a floating panel that got stuck.

In dark mode, lighter means closer. Floating layers move from `--paper` (`#141412`) to `--paper-2` (`#1E1D1A`) so the menu reads as nearer than the page, and keep the `--rule-strong` edge. Recessed regions in dark mode still use `--paper-2`; the border on the shared edge and the position tell them apart from floating ones.

#### Z-index scale

Depth in tone needs a matching order in the stack. Use five named layers and nothing else:

```css
:root {
  --z-base: 0;
  --z-sticky: 100;
  --z-dropdown: 200;
  --z-dialog: 300;
  --z-toast: 400;
}
```

#### Card at rest, hover and selected

A card is a bordered region on the page. It does not lift on hover. The hover pattern in generated code (`hover:-translate-y-1 hover:shadow-xl transition-all duration-300`) animates layout-adjacent properties for 300ms and makes the whole grid twitch under the cursor.

```slop
<a class="block rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow-md transition-all duration-300 hover:-translate-y-1 hover:shadow-xl">
```

```css
.card {
  display: block;
  padding: 24px;
  background: var(--paper);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  color: var(--ink);
  text-decoration: none;
  box-shadow: none;
  transition: border-color 120ms ease-out;
}
.card:hover { border-color: var(--ink); }
.card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

.card[aria-pressed="true"],
.card[aria-checked="true"] {
  background: var(--paper-3);
  border: 2px solid var(--ink);
  padding: 23px;   /* 24px minus the extra 1px of border, so nothing reflows */
}
.card[aria-checked="true"] .card-check { visibility: visible; }
.card-check { visibility: hidden; color: var(--ink); }

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .card { transition: none; }
}
```

The selected state uses three signals: tone (`--paper-3`), edge (a 2px `--ink` border with the padding reduced by 1px, so nothing reflows), and a check icon. Removing any one still leaves two. The selection edge is a border and the focus ring is an outline, so both can show at once: focus sits 2px beyond the edge, selection sits on it. Do not draw selection with `outline`, or the focus rule and the selection rule will overwrite each other.

#### Dropdown menu

```html
<div class="menu-anchor">
  <button class="btn" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="m1">Sort: Newest</button>
  <ul class="menu" id="m1" role="menu">
    <li role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true"><svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16"><use href="#i-check"/></svg>Newest</li>
    <li role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">Oldest</li>
    <li role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">Largest amount</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

```css
.menu-anchor { position: relative; }
.menu {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(100% + 4px);
  left: 0;
  z-index: var(--z-dropdown);
  min-width: 200px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 4px 0;
  list-style: none;
  background: var(--paper);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"] {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  min-height: 32px;
  padding: 0 12px 0 32px;
  font: 400 14px/1.3 var(--font-sans);
  color: var(--ink);
  cursor: default;
}
.menu [aria-checked="true"] { padding-left: 8px; font-weight: 600; }
.menu [role^="menuitem"]:hover,
.menu [role^="menuitem"][data-active] { background: var(--paper-2); }
.menu hr { margin: 4px 0; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }

:root[data-theme="dark"] .menu { background: var(--paper-2); }
:root[data-theme="dark"] .menu [role^="menuitem"]:hover { background: var(--paper-3); }
```

The 4px gap between trigger and menu shows the page behind, which separates the two better than a shadow would. The border is `--rule-strong` (16:1 against the page), not `--rule` (1.34:1), because the menu must read as a separate object at a glance even when it overlaps a card with its own `--rule` border.

#### Popover with the native API

```css
[popover] {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 12px;
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
[popover]::backdrop { background: transparent; }
```

User agents give `[popover]` and `dialog` default styles. Chrome's default dialog has no shadow, but component libraries add one; set `box-shadow: none` on both selectors in the reset so nothing returns through a library update.

#### Modal dialog

A dialog interrupts the page. It needs the page to recede and the dialog to stand forward. Use a flat scrim, a strong border, and spacing.

```css
dialog {
  width: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px));
  max-height: calc(100vh - 64px);
  padding: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgb(20 20 18 / 0.56); /* flat, no blur */
  backdrop-filter: none;
}
.dialog-head {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  padding: 16px 24px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
.dialog-body { padding: 24px; }
.dialog-foot {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 16px 24px;
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
```

The scrim is `--ink` at 56% opacity. Below 40% the page behind still competes for attention; above 70% the user loses the context they need to answer the dialog. The footer is recessed (`--paper-2`), which groups the actions and gives the dialog an internal depth step without a single extra line of decoration. In dark mode, raise the dialog to `--paper-2` and its footer to `--paper-3`, and darken the scrim to 64% black.

#### Sticky header

A sticky header sits over scrolling content, so it must be opaque. A translucent header with `backdrop-blur` is the glass tell (2.8). At the top of the page the header needs no edge. Once content scrolls under it, it needs one.

```html
<div class="sticky-sentinel" aria-hidden="true"></div>
<header class="site-header">...</header>
```

```css
.site-header {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: var(--z-sticky);
  background: var(--paper);
  border-bottom: 1px solid transparent;
  box-shadow: none;
  transition: border-color 120ms ease-out;
}
.site-header[data-stuck] { border-bottom-color: var(--rule-strong); }
.sticky-sentinel { height: 1px; margin-bottom: -1px; }
```

```js
const header = document.querySelector(".site-header");
const sentinel = document.querySelector(".sticky-sentinel");
new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => {
  header.toggleAttribute("data-stuck", !entry.isIntersecting);
}).observe(sentinel);
```

The border starts transparent rather than absent so the header height does not change by 1px when it appears.

#### Sticky table header and first column

```css
.table-wrap { overflow: auto; max-height: 70vh; border: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.table-wrap thead th {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: 2;
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
}
.table-wrap tbody th[scope="row"] {
  position: sticky;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 1;
  background: var(--paper);
  border-right: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
}
```

With `border-collapse: collapse`, sticky cells lose their borders in some engines as they scroll. Use `border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0` on sticky tables and draw the rules on the cells.

#### Dragged item

The default dragged card in generated code is rotated 2 to 3 degrees, scaled to 105% and given `shadow-2xl`. Replace all three with an edge and a placeholder.

```css
.sortable-item[data-dragging] {
  position: relative;
  z-index: var(--z-dropdown);
  background: var(--paper);
  border: 2px solid var(--ink);
  cursor: grabbing;
  box-shadow: none;
  /* position comes from transform: translate(x, y), set by the drag script */
}
.sortable-placeholder {
  min-height: var(--drag-height, 48px);
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border: 1px dashed var(--ink-3);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
```

The dragged item keeps its size and angle, so its text stays readable while it moves. The placeholder shows exactly where it will land: a recessed slot (`--paper-2`) with a dashed edge, which is inset language for "empty space waiting". Announce the move through an `aria-live` region ("Invoice 1042 moved to position 3 of 8"), since none of this is visible to a screen reader.

#### Tooltip and toast

The highest layers invert. An `--ink` surface is the furthest possible tone from the page, so it reads as on top without any edge.

```css
.tooltip {
  position: absolute;
  z-index: var(--z-toast);
  max-width: 240px;
  padding: 6px 8px;
  background: var(--ink);
  color: var(--paper);
  font: 400 12px/1.4 var(--font-sans);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
.toast {
  position: fixed;
  left: 16px;
  bottom: 16px;
  z-index: var(--z-toast);
  display: flex;
  gap: 12px;
  align-items: center;
  max-width: min(420px, calc(100vw - 32px));
  padding: 12px 16px;
  background: var(--ink);
  color: var(--paper);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: none;
}
.toast button { color: var(--paper); background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--paper); }
```

`--paper` on `--ink` is 16.00:1 in light mode and 15.20:1 in dark mode.

#### Overlap as depth

Overlap is the strongest depth cue that needs no effect at all: when one object covers part of another, the reader knows which is in front. Use it once or twice per page, deliberately.

```css
.band {
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
  padding: 64px 16px 112px;   /* 64 + 48 of overlap room */
}
.figures {
  position: relative;
  max-width: 960px;
  margin: -48px auto 0;       /* pulls the strip up across the band edge */
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr));
  background: var(--paper);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
}
.figures > div { padding: 24px; border-left: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.figures > div:first-child { border-left: 0; }
```

The figures strip crosses the boundary between the recessed band and the page. The strong border and the page tone mark it as on top. No shadow could say it more clearly.

#### Spacing as depth

Proximity groups things before any tone or border does. Use the spacing scale to build three distances and keep them apart by at least a factor of two:

- Inside a group (label to field, icon to text, lines in a list item): 4 to 8px.
- Between groups (field to field, card to card): 16 to 24px.
- Between sections: 48 to 96px.

When those three distances are clear, many borders can go. A form with 8px from label to input and 24px between fields needs no box around each field. A settings page with 64px between sections needs no card around each section.

#### Review checklist for 2.5

- `box-shadow: none` on every component; no `shadow-*` or `ring-*` classes.
- Every floating layer (menu, popover, dialog) has a 1px `--rule-strong` border and an opaque background.
- Recessed regions use `--paper-2` and at most a 1px `--rule` on the shared edge.
- Selected states combine tone, edge and an icon; none relies on a lift or a glow.
- Hover changes a border color or a background tone within 120ms; nothing translates upward.
- Sticky headers are opaque and gain a rule only when stuck.
- The z-index values come from the five named layers.
- The page still shows every layer edge in forced colors mode (test with Chrome DevTools, Rendering, "Emulate CSS media feature forced-colors").

### 2.6 Borders and rules

With shadows gone, borders and rules carry most of the structure. That makes them easy to overuse. The rules below keep them few, thin and meaningful.

#### Weights

| Weight | Color | Meaning | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1px | `--rule` | Separates | Card edges, list dividers, table row rules, section dividers, the shared edge of a recessed region |
| 1px | `--ink-3` | Identifies a control | Text inputs, selects, checkboxes, radio buttons (the 3:1 rule from 2.3) |
| 1px | `--rule-strong` | Sits on top | Menus, popovers, dialogs, a stuck header, the bottom of a table header row |
| 2px | `--ink` | This one | Selected item, recommended plan, active section top rule, invalid field in `--bad` |
| 2px | `--accent` | Current location | Active tab underline, current navigation item marker |
| 3px double | `--ink` | Grand total | The bottom rule under a final total row, as in printed accounts |
| 4px | `--ink` | Masthead | One rule at the top of a page or report, at most once |

Nothing is thicker than 4px. Nothing uses a dotted border. Dashed borders appear in exactly one place: an empty drop target or placeholder (2.5).

1px separates; 2px marks. A 2px rule says "this one, not the others", so a view group contains at most one 2px element of each meaning. If three cards in a row each have a 2px border, none of them is marked.

#### Colors

Borders use five colors: `--rule`, `--rule-strong`, `--ink-3`, `--accent`, and the three status colors in alerts and invalid fields. No border is ever a tint of the accent (`border-orange-200`), a translucent white (`border-white/10`), or a translucent black (`ring-black/5`). Translucent borders are a glass-era habit: their color depends on what sits behind them, so the same component shows a different edge on every surface.

On `--paper-2`, the default `--rule` drops from 1.34:1 to 1.24:1 against its surface. That is still visible for dividers. For anything stronger inside a recessed region, step to `--ink-3`, never to a darker invented gray.

#### 1px on high-density and scaled displays

- Use `border`, not a 1px-high element with a background color. Browsers snap border widths to whole device pixels. A `div` with `height: 1px` is laid out like any other box, so at 125% and 150% Windows display scaling some of these lines land on one device pixel and others on two, and a stack of dividers looks uneven.
- Do not use `0.5px` hairlines. Safari draws them as one device pixel on 2x screens; Chrome and Firefox round sub-pixel border widths up to one device pixel, so the "hairline" is a normal 1px line on most screens and a different weight on Safari. For a lighter line, lighten the color, not the width.
- Do not fake hairlines with `transform: scaleY(0.5)` pseudo-elements. They blur on 1x displays and break when the parent is scaled.
- Keep boxes with borders on whole-pixel positions. `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` on an element with an odd width puts its edges on half pixels, and the 1px border renders as a 2px gray smear. Center with grid or flex instead, or round the size to an even number.

```css
:root { --rule-w: 1px; }
.divider { border: 0; border-top: var(--rule-w) solid var(--rule); }
.center-overlay {
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center; /* no translate(-50%) half-pixel edges */
}
```

#### Dividers or spacing

Pick one per boundary. Never a rule and a 48px gap on the same edge.

Use a rule when:

- Items are of the same kind and the reader scans across rows (tables, inbox lists, settings lists, line items).
- Rows are dense (row height under 48px) and spacing alone would need too much height to separate them.
- A boundary must survive reflow, such as a sticky header meeting the content below.

Use spacing when:

- Groups differ in kind (account details, then billing, then danger zone).
- The content inside each group already has strong edges (inputs, images, buttons).
- There are fewer than five groups on the screen.

For lists, draw rules between items, not around them. A list of eight items needs seven lines, not eight boxes.

```css
.list { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.list > li { padding: 12px 0; }
.list > li + li { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
```

#### Table rules
