Tables follow the conventions of printed financial tables, which solved this problem a century ago.

- Horizontal rules only, 1px `--rule`, between rows.
- No vertical rules, except one 1px `--rule` to separate a group of columns (before a totals column, between "This year" and "Last year" groups).
- The header row sits on `--paper-2` with a 1px `--rule-strong` bottom edge.
- A subtotal row has a 1px `--ink` top rule. A grand total has a 1px `--ink` top rule and a 3px double `--ink` bottom rule.
- Zebra striping is for tables wider than eight columns, where the eye loses the row. When stripes are used, row rules are removed. Never both.
- Row hover is `--paper-2`. Selected row is `--paper-3`, with a checkbox in the first column showing the state.

```css
.ledger { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font: 400 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.ledger th, .ledger td { padding: 8px 12px; text-align: left; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.ledger thead th { background: var(--paper-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); font-weight: 600; }
.ledger td.num, .ledger th.num { text-align: right; }
.ledger .group-start { border-left: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.ledger tr.subtotal td { border-top: 1px solid var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
.ledger tr.total td { border-top: 1px solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 3px double var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
.ledger tbody tr:hover { background: var(--paper-2); }
.ledger tbody tr[aria-selected="true"] { background: var(--paper-3); }
```

#### The "border on everything" failure

When a team removes shadows without a plan, it replaces each shadow with a border. The page turns into box soup: a bordered section containing bordered cards containing bordered inputs inside bordered field groups. Every element announces its edges and none of them stands out.

```slop
<section class="rounded-lg border border-gray-200 p-6">
  <div class="rounded-lg border border-gray-200 p-4">
    <div class="rounded-md border border-gray-200 p-3">
      <label class="text-sm">Email</label>
      <input class="mt-1 w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2">
    </div>
    <div class="rounded-md border border-gray-200 p-3">...</div>
  </div>
</section>
```

Four nested boxes around one input. Fix it with three limits:

1. At most two bordered containers nested inside each other. A bordered card may hold bordered inputs. A bordered card may not hold a bordered card.
2. Inside a bordered container, group with spacing and rules, not boxes.
3. A page section is not a box. Sections are separated by spacing, a tone change or a single rule.

```html
<section class="settings-section">
  <h2>Contact</h2>
  <div class="field"><label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" type="email"></div>
  <div class="field"><label for="phone">Phone</label><input id="phone" type="tel"></div>
</section>
```

```css
.settings-section { padding: 32px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.settings-section h2 { margin: 0 0 24px; font: 600 18px/1.25 var(--font-sans); }
.field { display: grid; gap: 4px; margin-bottom: 24px; max-width: 28rem; }
.field label { font: 500 14px/1.4 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink); }
```

One rule above the section, borders on the inputs, nothing else.

#### Grids of cells without doubled lines

Adjacent bordered cells with no gap draw 2px lines where they meet. Draw the grid with a gap and let the container's background show through it:

```css
.cells {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr));
  gap: 1px;
  background: var(--rule);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
.cells > * { background: var(--paper); padding: 16px; }
```

Every line is exactly 1px, including at the outer edge, at any column count. If the last row is incomplete, the empty area shows as `--rule`; fill it with empty cells or set the container background to `--paper` and give the cells `outline: 1px solid var(--rule)` instead.

#### Review checklist for 2.6

- Every border uses one of the listed weights and colors. No translucent borders.
- No element has more than two bordered ancestors.
- Each boundary is a rule or a gap, not both.
- Tables have horizontal rules only, a strong header edge and accounting rules on totals.
- Rules are drawn with `border`, never with 1px filled elements, and never at 0.5px.
- Dashed borders appear only on placeholders and drop targets.

### 2.7 Corner radius

Use `--radius: 2px` everywhere, or `0` everywhere. Never above 4px on a rectangle.

#### Why large radius reads as generated

Library radius defaults have climbed for a decade and generated code takes the top of the range:

| Source | Value |
|---|---|
| Tailwind `rounded` / `rounded-md` / `rounded-lg` | 4px / 6px / 8px |
| Tailwind `rounded-xl` / `rounded-2xl` / `rounded-3xl` | 12px / 16px / 24px |
| shadcn/ui `--radius` | 0.5rem (8px), later 0.625rem (10px), with `Card` at `rounded-xl` |
| Bootstrap 5 `--bs-border-radius` | 0.375rem (6px) |
| iOS app icon mask | about 22% of the icon width |

`rounded-2xl` on cards and `rounded-xl` on buttons are what a model writes when nothing tells it otherwise. A 16px corner on a 320px card reads as an app-store tile, and putting that tile on every surface makes a document look like a phone home screen. Large radii also cost space: text must clear the curve, so a 16px corner forces padding of at least 16px in every direction, and dense tables or toolbars cannot use it at all.

#### The policy

- `--radius: 2px` for products with controls (apps, dashboards, forms). 2px is enough to soften the anti-aliased corner pixel so edges do not look jagged on 1x screens, and small enough that nobody perceives the shape as rounded.
- `--radius: 0` for editorial products, reports and documents, where everything should feel set on a page.
- One value per product. Buttons, inputs, cards, menus, dialogs, badges, tooltips, code blocks and images all use it.
- 4px is the hard ceiling and is reserved for one case: a component that sits inside a third-party frame with its own larger radius (an embedded payment field, for example) and would look broken at 2px.

```css
:root { --radius: 2px; }
button, input, select, textarea, .card, .menu, dialog, .badge, .tooltip, pre, img.framed {
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
```

#### Nested radius math

When a rounded element sits inside another with padding between them, the inner radius must be the outer radius minus the padding, or the gap between the curves looks thicker at the corners:

```
inner radius = max(0, outer radius - padding)
```

Generated code nests equal radii (`rounded-2xl` inside `rounded-2xl` with `p-2`), which produces a visible fat crescent at each corner. With a 16px outer radius and 8px of padding, the inner should be 8px, not 16px.

With this handbook's policy, the math almost always returns zero: a 2px outer radius with any padding of 2px or more gives an inner radius of 0. That is correct. Square children inside a 2px frame look aligned.

```css
.frame {
  --pad: 4px;
  padding: var(--pad);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
.frame > * {
  border-radius: max(0px, calc(var(--radius) - var(--pad))); /* resolves to 0 */
}
```

The same rule applies to the focus outline. Current browsers draw `outline` following `border-radius` (Chrome 94, Firefox 88, Safari 16.4 and later). With `outline-offset: 2px` the outline's curve has radius `--radius + 2px`, which is 4px with the policy above, and still reads as square.

#### The pill ban

`rounded-full` on a rectangle is banned: no pill buttons, pill badges, pill tags, pill search fields, pill navigation, pill toggle groups. Reasons:

- The LIVE, NEW and BETA pill is a fingerprint (2.1).
- A pill needs end caps of half its height. A 32px tall pill button needs about 16px more horizontal padding than a 2px button to keep the label off the curve, and that space multiplies across a toolbar.
- Pills with long labels stretch into capsules and wrap badly.
- A row of pills reads as one undifferentiated chain; a row of square tags with 8px gaps reads as separate items.

Circles and capsules are allowed only where the shape itself carries meaning:

| Element | Shape | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Avatar | Circle | Convention for a person; separates people from objects |
| Radio input | Circle | Platform convention that separates single choice from checkbox |
| Switch track and thumb | Capsule and circle | Platform convention for an on/off toggle |
| Color swatch in a picker | Circle or square, consistently | The fill is the content |
| Map pin, chart dot | Circle | Data mark, not a container |

A count beside a navigation item (unread messages) is a square badge with `--radius`, not a red circle.

#### Review checklist for 2.7

- One radius value in the whole product: 2px or 0.
- No `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl`, `rounded-3xl` or `rounded-full` on rectangles.
- Nested elements follow `inner = max(0, outer - padding)`.
- Circles appear only for avatars, radio buttons, switch parts, swatches and data marks.
- Images are square-cornered or match `--radius`, never more.

### 2.8 Glass, blur, glow, noise and neon

These five effects share a cause: they try to give a flat screen the look of a lit, physical object. Each one became a trend, then a component library preset, then a default in generated output. All are banned. Each has a flat replacement that is easier to read and cheaper to render.

#### The ban list

| Effect | Typical code | Why it fails | Replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glass panel | `bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-lg border-white/20` | Text contrast depends on whatever scrolls behind; `backdrop-filter` recomposites a blurred copy of the page on every scroll frame | Opaque `--paper` or `--paper-2` panel with a 1px border |
| Frosted header | `sticky top-0 bg-white/70 backdrop-blur` | Headings scroll under the header and show through as gray smears; the header has no fixed contrast | Opaque `--paper` header, rule when stuck (2.5) |
| Blur blobs | `absolute h-96 w-96 bg-purple-500 opacity-30 blur-3xl` | Pure decoration; large offscreen layer; leads straight back to blue-violet | Delete |
| Colored glow | `shadow-lg shadow-indigo-500/50`, `0 0 40px rgba(99,102,241,.5)` | A shadow with a hue; on dark pages it halos text and blurs edges | 1px `--rule-strong` border, or nothing |
| Focus glow | `focus:ring-4 focus:ring-indigo-500/25` | Soft, low-contrast ring (indigo at 25% on white is about 1.4:1) | `outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px` |
| Text glow | `text-shadow: 0 0 12px #22d3ee` | Blurs letter edges; reduces legibility; reads as a synthwave template | Plain text in `--ink` or `--accent` |
| Neon on black | Saturated cyan or magenta text on `#000` | Halation: bright saturated strokes on black bleed into the background for readers with astigmatism | `--ink` dark (`#ECE9E1`) on `--paper` dark (`#141412`) |
| Grain and noise | SVG `feTurbulence` or a noise PNG at 3% to 8% opacity over the page | Exists to hide gradient banding; with no gradients it has no job; costs a full-page layer | Nothing. Texture comes from type and rules. |
| Cursor spotlight | A radial gradient that follows the pointer | Gradient plus motion; invisible to touch and keyboard users | Hover border change on the item under the pointer |
| Tilt cards | `perspective` plus `rotateX/rotateY` following the pointer | Moves text while the user reads it; ignores reduced motion | Static card with hover border |
| Shimmer skeleton | A light gradient sweeping across gray blocks forever | Gradient plus endless motion | Static `--paper-2` blocks, then content |
| Inner glow on inputs | `ring-inset` with a colored blur | Box shadow by another name | `--ink-3` border, 2px `--bad` when invalid |

#### Why glass fails contrast

A glass panel is translucent by definition, so its text sits on a background that changes as the page scrolls. With `bg-white/10` over a dark photo, white text may measure 12:1 over a shadow area and 1.3:1 over a sky. No single ratio exists, and automated tests cannot compute one. The only fix that keeps contrast stable is an opaque background, which is the end of the glass.

The cost is concrete too. `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)` makes the browser render the content behind the element into a separate texture, blur it and composite the result on every frame that the content or the panel moves. On a sticky header that runs on every scroll frame, and on low-end Android phones it is a common cause of scroll jank.

#### Skeletons without shimmer

```css
.skeleton {
  display: block;
  height: 14px;
  margin: 8px 0;
  background: var(--paper-2);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
.skeleton[data-w="60"] { width: 60%; }
.skeleton[data-w="40"] { width: 40%; }
```

A static block tells the user where content will appear. The shimmer adds nothing to that and moves forever. If loading takes longer than about one second, replace the skeleton with a sentence ("Loading 2,418 invoices") rather than animating it.

#### Focus without glow

The focus indicator is an outline. It is not a ring utility, not a box shadow and not a colored halo.

```css
:where(a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]):focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

`--focus` is `#1A1A18` in light mode (16:1 on `--paper`) and `#ECE9E1` in dark mode (15.2:1). It passes WCAG 2.2 focus appearance with room to spare. The Tailwind equivalent is `focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2`, and every `ring-*` class should be removed (2.11 disables them in the config).

#### Review checklist for 2.8

- No `backdrop-filter`, no `backdrop-blur`, no translucent panel backgrounds over content.
- No `blur()` filters on decorative elements.
- No colored shadows, no `text-shadow`, no glow on focus.
- No noise or grain layers.
- No pointer-following or tilt effects.
- Skeletons are static.

### 2.9 Dark mode done by hand

Dark mode is a second palette, designed and measured like the first. It is not the light palette inverted, not `filter: invert(1)`, and not every class doubled with `dark:bg-gray-900 dark:text-white`.

#### What generated dark modes get wrong

```slop
<div class="bg-white text-gray-900 dark:bg-slate-900 dark:text-white">
  <div class="rounded-2xl bg-white shadow-lg dark:bg-slate-800 dark:shadow-indigo-500/10">
```

- `slate-900` is `#0F172A`, a navy at OKLCH chroma 0.040 and hue 266. The whole page turns blue.
- `text-white` on `slate-900` is 17.85:1. Pure white on near-black at that ratio produces halation for many readers: the strokes glow and smear.
- The shadow does nothing on a dark page, so the kit tints it indigo to make it show. That is a glow.
- The card is `slate-800` on `slate-900`, one step lighter, which is right in principle, but chosen from a blue ramp.

#### The canonical dark tokens, measured

| Token | Hex | OKLCH | On dark `--paper` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#141412` | `0.190 0.004 107` | 1.00:1 |
| `--paper-2` | `#1E1D1A` | `0.231 0.006 92` | 1.09:1 |
| `--paper-3` | `#2A2925` | `0.281 0.007 95` | 1.27:1 |
| `--rule` | `#34322E` | `0.318 0.008 85` | 1.44:1 |
| `--ink-3` | `#8F8B81` | `0.637 0.015 89` | 5.43:1 |
| `--ink-2` | `#B5B1A7` | `0.761 0.015 89` | 8.62:1 |
| `--ink` | `#ECE9E1` | `0.934 0.011 90` | 15.20:1 |
| `--accent` | `#E2703F` | `0.671 0.156 43` | 5.82:1 |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | `#141412` | | 5.82:1 |
| `--ok` | `#7FB38A` | `0.719 0.081 151` | 7.66:1 |
| `--warn` | `#D9A93A` | `0.760 0.136 84` | 8.51:1 |
| `--bad` | `#E0705F` | `0.672 0.143 30` | 5.84:1 |

#### Rules for the dark palette

- No pure black. `#000000` turns OLED pixels fully off; when the page scrolls, pixels switching on from off lag behind their neighbors and smear dark content. It also pushes halation around light text to its peak. Keep the darkest surface between OKLCH L 0.16 and 0.22. `#141412` is 0.190.
- No pure white text. `#FFFFFF` on `#141412` is 18.44:1. The canonical `--ink` at 15.20:1 is easier to read for long stretches and still far above 7:1.
- Keep the temperature. The dark neutrals share the light neutrals' hue (about 90), so both themes feel like the same product.
- Spread the surface steps wider. Light surfaces step about 0.03 in L; dark surfaces step about 0.04 to 0.05 (0.190, 0.231, 0.281). Equal L steps look smaller at the dark end, and the contrast ratios confirm it: the light `--paper` to `--paper-3` step is 1.20:1 and the dark one is 1.27:1, which is about the minimum that reads as a separate surface on a dim screen.
- Lighter means closer. Floating layers move up one surface step (2.5).
- Re-pick the accent. The light accent `#B4441C` on `#141412` is 3.32:1 and fails for text. The dark accent `#E2703F` keeps hue (39 to 43) and chroma, raises L from 0.535 to 0.671, and flips `--accent-ink` to dark.
- Calm the status colors. Saturated colors on dark grounds vibrate. The dark status colors raise L to 0.67 to 0.76 and cut chroma by 15% to 20% against their light versions (ok goes from 0.100 to 0.081).
- No glow, ever. Dark mode is where glows creep back in, because a dark page with no shadows can feel flat to a team used to them. The answer is the tone steps and `--rule-strong` borders, not light leaking from edges.

#### Switching themes

Respect the system setting by default and let the user override it. Set `color-scheme` so native controls, scrollbars and the default canvas follow.

```html
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
<script>
  try {
    const t = localStorage.getItem("theme");
    if (t === "light" || t === "dark") document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t;
  } catch (e) {}
</script>
```

```css
:root { color-scheme: light; /* light tokens from the authoring guide */ }

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:not([data-theme="light"]) {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --paper: #141412; --paper-2: #1E1D1A; --paper-3: #2A2925;
    --ink: #ECE9E1;   --ink-2: #B5B1A7;   --ink-3: #8F8B81;
    --rule: #34322E;  --rule-strong: #ECE9E1;
    --accent: #E2703F; --accent-ink: #141412;
    --ok: #7FB38A;    --warn: #D9A93A;    --bad: #E0705F;
    --focus: #ECE9E1;
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  color-scheme: dark;
  /* same values as above */
}
body { background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); }
```

The inline script runs before first paint, so a user who chose dark does not see a flash of light. Keep it in the `head`, before the stylesheet link. The tokens are declared twice (media query and attribute) because the attribute must win in both directions: `data-theme="light"` on a dark system and `data-theme="dark"` on a light one.

#### Borders in dark mode

`--rule` at `#34322E` is 1.44:1 on `--paper`, which is about the same visual weight as the light rule. On `--paper-3` it drops to 1.14:1 and nearly vanishes. Accept that for selected rows, where the tone change itself marks the row, but not for inputs: inputs keep `--ink-3` (5.43:1).

`--rule-strong` in dark mode is `#ECE9E1`, a bright line. On a large dialog that bright frame can dominate the screen. For floating layers larger than about 480px wide, use `--ink-3` (5.43:1) as the border instead; it still clears the 3:1 boundary rule and reads as an edge, not a frame.

#### Images, screenshots, logos and diagrams

- Do not invert or filter photographs. Put a 1px `--rule` border around them so pale photos do not bleed into the page edge.
- Ship dark screenshots of the product for dark mode with `<picture>` and a media query, rather than showing a white screenshot on a dark page.
- Logos need a reversed version. A dark logo on `#141412` disappears.
- Inline SVG icons and diagrams use `currentColor` and the tokens, so they switch themselves. Never hard-code `#000` or `#FFF` in an SVG that ships inline.
- Charts get their own dark palette (2.10).

```html
<picture>
  <source srcset="/img/report-dark.png" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">
  <img src="/img/report-light.png" alt="Monthly report with revenue by region" width="1200" height="760">
</picture>
```

When the site has a manual theme toggle, the `media` attribute follows the system setting and not the toggle. Swap the `src` from the same script that sets `data-theme`, or render both images and hide one with `:root[data-theme="dark"] .only-light { display: none; }`.

#### Testing a dark palette

1. Measure every pairing in the table above against `--paper`, `--paper-2` and `--paper-3`, not only the page.
2. View it at full and at 20% screen brightness. Surface steps that vanish at 20% need a wider L gap.
3. View it on an OLED phone in a dark room. Halation and smear show there first.
4. Turn on forced colors emulation and check that every floating layer still has an edge.
5. Grep for `#000`, `#000000`, `#FFF`, `#FFFFFF`, `black` and `white` in component styles. Each hit should be a token instead.

#### Review checklist for 2.9

- Dark mode has its own measured token set with the same hue temperature as light mode.
- The darkest surface is between OKLCH L 0.16 and 0.22; no `#000`. No `#FFF` text.
- Surface steps are 0.04 to 0.05 apart in L.
- The accent and status colors were re-picked for dark and pass 4.5:1 as text.
- Floating layers move one step lighter; nothing glows.
- `color-scheme` is set, the theme loads before first paint, and images have dark variants or borders.

### 2.10 Data and chart color

Charts are where blue returns through the back door. Every major charting default leads with blue or violet, so a page that bans indigo in its buttons still ships it in its first chart.

#### The defaults and where they lead

| Library | First series color | OKLCH hue |
|---|---|---|
| D3 `schemeCategory10`, matplotlib `tab10` | `#1F77B4` | 245 |
| Tableau 10 | `#4E79A7` | 251 |
| Plotly default | `#636EFA` | 275 |
| Chart.js colors plugin | `#36A2EB` | 243 |
| Recharts documentation examples | `#8884D8` | 285 |
| Google Sheets default | `#4285F4` | 260 |
| matplotlib `viridis` (sequential) | starts at `#440154` | 318 |

The Recharts examples are the most copied chart code in generated React, and their first two strokes, `#8884d8` and `#82ca9d`, show up verbatim in thousands of dashboards. Treat those two hex values as a fingerprint.

#### Categorical palette

Six colors, built from the families in 2.3, with lightness spread on purpose so that series stay apart for readers with color vision deficiency. Measured as the smallest OKLab ΔE between any two colors, under normal vision and under simulated deuteranopia and protanopia (Machado 2009), the light set never drops below 10.4. Two default greens and reds sharing the same lightness can drop to 4 (2.4).

Light mode, on `--paper`:

| Order | Name | Hex | OKLCH | Contrast on `--paper` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Orange | `#D8662A` | `0.639 0.160 45` | 3.29:1 |
| 2 | Graphite | `#27241F` | `0.262 0.010 81` | 14.19:1 |
| 3 | Teal | `#429599` | `0.621 0.080 200` | 3.22:1 |
| 4 | Ochre | `#E0AF3B` | `0.779 0.140 85` | 1.86:1 |
| 5 | Raspberry | `#973462` | `0.481 0.140 355` | 6.46:1 |
| 6 | Olive | `#3F5700` | `0.421 0.107 126` | 7.49:1 |

Dark mode, on `#141412` (smallest ΔE 10.7):

| Order | Name | Hex | OKLCH | Contrast on dark `--paper` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Orange | `#F78955` | `0.740 0.150 45` | 7.61:1 |
| 2 | Stone | `#EFEAE2` | `0.939 0.012 80` | 15.40:1 |
| 3 | Teal | `#64C3C3` | `0.760 0.090 195` | 8.90:1 |
| 4 | Ochre | `#F8CA65` | `0.860 0.130 85` | 11.97:1 |
| 5 | Raspberry | `#C1628A` | `0.620 0.129 355` | 4.73:1 |
| 6 | Olive | `#667F30` | `0.559 0.110 125` | 4.08:1 |

Rules for categorical color:

- Six series at most. A seventh category goes into "Other" in `--ink-3`, or the chart becomes small multiples, one panel per series.
- Assign colors in order and keep the assignment stable. If "Europe" is orange on one chart, it is orange on every chart in the product.
- Light-mode ochre is 1.86:1 against the paper, under the 3:1 floor for graphics. Give ochre bars and areas a 1px `--ink` outline, or use ochre only for large areas that also carry a direct label.
- Do not use status colors as series colors. A green series next to a red series reads as good versus bad.

#### Gray plus one

Most charts answer one question about one series. Draw every series in `--ink-3` and the one that matters in `--accent`. This needs no legend and no categorical palette, and it is the single most effective chart color rule.

```css
.chart .series { stroke: var(--ink-3); stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; }
.chart .series[data-focus] { stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 2.5; }
.chart .series-label { font: 400 12px/1 var(--font-sans); fill: var(--ink-2); }
.chart .series-label[data-focus] { fill: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
```

#### Sequential ramps

For ordered values (density, counts, rates), use a single-hue ramp from the paper toward a dark step of the accent family. Use five classes, not a continuous scale; five stepped colors can be named and read off a legend, a continuous ramp cannot.

| Class | Hex | OKLCH |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (lowest) | `#FEE1D7` | `0.931 0.035 39` |
| 2 | `#F2A48B` | `0.789 0.100 39` |
| 3 | `#D15F38` | `0.620 0.154 39` |
| 4 | `#933511` | `0.459 0.135 39` |
| 5 (highest) | `#4E1C0B` | `0.300 0.080 39` |

L steps are about 0.15 apart, evenly spaced, so each class is as distinct from its neighbor as every other. The ramp avoids `viridis` and `Blues`, the two most common defaults, both of which pass through the banned band.

#### Diverging ramps

For values around a meaningful midpoint (change from last year, above or below target), use two hues that differ in lightness as well as hue, with the midpoint on `--paper-2`. The default `RdBu` (red to blue) puts blue at one end; replace it with teal to orange.

| Class | Hex | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| -3 | `#005356` | Far below |
| -2 | `#34898D` | Below |
| -1 | `#92C2C4` | Slightly below |
| 0 | `#EFECE4` | At midpoint |
| +1 | `#EAAE93` | Slightly above |
| +2 | `#D46E45` | Above |
| +3 | `#983D1D` | Far above |

Which end is "good" depends on the measure. Say it in the legend title ("Change in late deliveries, lower is better"), not with green and red.

#### Legends are swatches, not gradients

A continuous gradient bar under a map is a gradient (2.2). Draw the legend as one swatch per class, with the class range printed under each swatch.

```html
<ol class="legend" aria-label="Late deliveries per 1,000 orders">
  <li><span class="swatch" style="background:#FEE1D7"></span>0 to 4</li>
  <li><span class="swatch" style="background:#F2A48B"></span>5 to 9</li>
  <li><span class="swatch" style="background:#D15F38"></span>10 to 19</li>
  <li><span class="swatch" style="background:#933511"></span>20 to 39</li>
  <li><span class="swatch" style="background:#4E1C0B"></span>40 or more</li>
</ol>
```

```css
.legend { display: flex; gap: 0; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; font: 400 12px/1.3 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink-2); }
.legend li { display: grid; gap: 4px; min-width: 72px; }
.legend .swatch { display: block; height: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule); }
```

#### Label directly

- With four series or fewer, put the label at the end of each line or inside each bar segment, and drop the legend. The eye stops jumping between key and data.
- Label text is `--ink` or `--ink-2`, with a short colored mark beside it. Text in the series color fails contrast for ochre and is hard to read for orange and teal.
- Print the value on the bar when there are fewer than about 12 bars. Gridlines can then go.

#### Chart chrome

- Gridlines: horizontal only, 1px `--rule`. No vertical gridlines on time series.
- Zero baseline: 1px `--ink`.
- Axis text: 12px `--ink-3` on `--paper`, tabular numerals.
- Tooltips: the inverted tooltip from 2.5, no shadow, no blur.
- Areas: a flat fill at the series color with `fill-opacity: 0.12`, or no fill. The gradient fill under a line, from the Recharts area chart example, is banned.

```slop
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="colorUv" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="5%" stopColor="#8884d8" stopOpacity={0.8}/>
    <stop offset="95%" stopColor="#8884d8" stopOpacity={0}/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<Area type="monotone" dataKey="uv" stroke="#8884d8" fill="url(#colorUv)" />
```

```tsx
const series = {
  orange: "var(--chart-1)",
  graphite: "var(--chart-2)",
  teal: "var(--chart-3)",
} as const;

<AreaChart data={rows} margin={{ top: 8, right: 64, bottom: 8, left: 8 }}>
  <CartesianGrid vertical={false} stroke="var(--rule)" />
  <XAxis dataKey="month" tick={{ fill: "var(--ink-3)", fontSize: 12 }} axisLine={{ stroke: "var(--ink)" }} tickLine={false} />
  <YAxis tick={{ fill: "var(--ink-3)", fontSize: 12 }} axisLine={false} tickLine={false} />
  <Area type="linear" dataKey="paid" stroke={series.orange} strokeWidth={2} fill={series.orange} fillOpacity={0.12} isAnimationActive={false} />
</AreaChart>
```

```css
:root {
  --chart-1: #D8662A; --chart-2: #27241F; --chart-3: #429599;
  --chart-4: #E0AF3B; --chart-5: #973462; --chart-6: #3F5700;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --chart-1: #F78955; --chart-2: #EFEAE2; --chart-3: #64C3C3;
  --chart-4: #F8CA65; --chart-5: #C1628A; --chart-6: #667F30;
}
```

`type="linear"` draws the data as measured; `monotone` smooths it and invents values between points. `isAnimationActive={false}` removes the 1500ms default draw-in animation, which runs on every data refresh.

#### Review checklist for 2.10

- No chart color comes from a library default. `#8884d8`, `#82ca9d`, `#1f77b4`, `#636efa` and `#36a2eb` do not appear.
- Categorical series use the six-color set, in a stable order, six at most.
- Sequential and diverging scales are stepped, with swatch legends.
- Series with four or fewer lines are labeled directly.
- Gridlines are horizontal `--rule`; no gradient area fills; no chart animation.
- Chart colors switch with the theme through tokens.

### 2.11 Color in code

The rules in this Part hold only if the code cannot express the banned patterns easily. Remove shadows, gradients, blur and the default palette at the config level, then add a linter and a grep step so anything that slips through fails CI.

#### Token file structure

Keep three layers in one file, in this order:

1. Primitives. Every raw value, named by hue and step: `--orange-700: #B4441C`. Only this layer contains hex values.
2. Roles. What each value is for: `--accent: var(--orange-700)`. Components read only this layer.
3. Themes. Role overrides per theme: `:root[data-theme="dark"] { --accent: var(--orange-500-dark); }`.

```css
/* tokens.css: the only file allowed to contain color literals */
:root {
  /* primitives */
  --stone-50: #F7F5F0;  --stone-100: #EFECE4; --stone-200: #E5E1D6; --stone-300: #D9D5CB;
  --stone-600: #6F6C64; --stone-700: #4A4843; --stone-900: #1A1A18;
  --orange-700: #B4441C;

  /* roles */
  --paper: var(--stone-50);   --paper-2: var(--stone-100); --paper-3: var(--stone-200);
  --rule: var(--stone-300);   --rule-strong: var(--stone-900);
  --ink: var(--stone-900);    --ink-2: var(--stone-700);   --ink-3: var(--stone-600);
  --accent: var(--orange-700); --accent-ink: #FFFFFF;
  --focus: var(--stone-900);
  --radius: 2px;
}
```

#### Tailwind v3: remove the defaults

Override the theme keys (not `extend`) so the default scales vanish, and turn off the plugins that generate shadows, rings, blur and gradients. Tailwind's `ring-*` utilities compile to `box-shadow` declarations, so they go too.

```js
// tailwind.config.js
module.exports = {
  content: ["./src/**/*.{html,js,jsx,ts,tsx,vue,svelte}"],
  theme: {
    colors: {
      transparent: "transparent",
      current: "currentColor",
      paper: { DEFAULT: "var(--paper)", 2: "var(--paper-2)", 3: "var(--paper-3)" },
      ink: { DEFAULT: "var(--ink)", 2: "var(--ink-2)", 3: "var(--ink-3)" },
      rule: { DEFAULT: "var(--rule)", strong: "var(--rule-strong)" },
      accent: { DEFAULT: "var(--accent)", ink: "var(--accent-ink)" },
      ok: "var(--ok)",
      warn: "var(--warn)",
      bad: "var(--bad)",
    },
    borderRadius: { none: "0", DEFAULT: "var(--radius)", full: "9999px" },
    boxShadow: { none: "none" },
    dropShadow: {},
    backgroundImage: {},
    backdropBlur: {},
    blur: {},
    fontFamily: {
      sans: ["IBM Plex Sans", "system-ui", "sans-serif"],
      serif: ["Source Serif 4", "Georgia", "serif"],
      mono: ["IBM Plex Mono", "ui-monospace", "monospace"],
    },
  },
  corePlugins: {
    boxShadowColor: false,
    dropShadow: false,
    backgroundImage: false,
    gradientColorStops: false,
    backdropFilter: false,
    backdropBlur: false,
    blur: false,
    ringWidth: false,
    ringColor: false,
    ringOpacity: false,
    ringOffsetWidth: false,
    ringOffsetColor: false,
  },
};
```

With `colors` replaced, `bg-indigo-600` and `text-gray-500` stop compiling, and an agent that writes them gets unstyled output that a reviewer sees at once. `rounded-full` stays only for avatars and switches; the lint step below checks where it is used.

#### Tailwind v4: the same in CSS

Tailwind v4 reads its theme from CSS. Reset whole namespaces with `initial`, then declare only the tokens.

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-*: initial;
  --shadow-*: initial;
  --inset-shadow-*: initial;
  --drop-shadow-*: initial;
  --text-shadow-*: initial;
  --blur-*: initial;
  --radius-*: initial;

  --color-paper: #F7F5F0;
  --color-paper-2: #EFECE4;
  --color-paper-3: #E5E1D6;
  --color-ink: #1A1A18;
  --color-ink-2: #4A4843;
  --color-ink-3: #6F6C64;
  --color-rule: #D9D5CB;
  --color-accent: #B4441C;
  --radius-sm: 2px;

  --font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Version 4 generates gradient utilities (`bg-linear-to-r`, `bg-radial`, `bg-conic`) and ring utilities without reading the theme, so the reset cannot remove them. The grep step is what catches those.

#### Stylelint rules

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "property-disallowed-list": ["backdrop-filter", "-webkit-backdrop-filter", "text-shadow"],
    "declaration-property-value-disallowed-list": {
      "box-shadow": ["/^(?!none$).+/"],
      "filter": ["/drop-shadow/", "/blur/"],
      "background": ["/gradient/"],
      "background-image": ["/gradient/"],
      "border-image": ["/gradient/"],
      "mask-image": ["/gradient/"],
      "border-radius": ["/^(?:[5-9]|\\d{2,})(?:\\.\\d+)?px/", "/rem/", "/em$/"]
    },
    "function-disallowed-list": ["linear-gradient", "radial-gradient", "conic-gradient", "repeating-linear-gradient", "repeating-radial-gradient"],
    "color-named": "never",
    "color-no-hex": true
  },
  "overrides": [
    { "files": ["src/styles/tokens.css"], "rules": { "color-no-hex": null } }
  ]
}
```

`color-no-hex` everywhere except the token file forces every component to use roles. `border-radius: 50%` stays legal for avatars.

#### Grep commands

Run these in CI over source files. Each must return nothing. Exclude the token file and lint config where noted.

```bash
# box-shadow values other than none, plus Tailwind shadow-* and ring-* utilities
rg -n --pcre2 'box-shadow\s*:(?!\s*none\b)' src/
rg -n '\bshadow-(sm|md|lg|xl|2xl|inner)\b|\bring-[0-9a-z]' src/

# Gradients in CSS and in Tailwind classes (v3 and v4 names)
rg -n '(linear|radial|conic)-gradient' src/
rg -n '\bbg-(gradient|linear|radial|conic)\b|\b(from|via|to)-[a-z]+-[0-9]{2,3}\b' src/

# Blur and glass
rg -n 'backdrop-(blur|filter)|\bblur-(sm|md|lg|xl|2xl|3xl)\b|filter:\s*blur' src/

# Default palette leaks: blue-violet classes and their hex values
rg -n '\b(blue|indigo|violet|purple|fuchsia|sky|slate)-[0-9]{2,3}\b' src/
rg -ni '#(6366f1|4f46e5|8b5cf6|a855f7|3b82f6|2563eb|0f172a|020817|6b7280|8884d8|82ca9d)\b' src/

# Large radius and pills
rg -n '\brounded-(lg|xl|2xl|3xl)\b' src/
rg -n '\brounded-full\b' src/ | rg -v 'avatar|switch|radio'

# Status tells
rg -n 'animate-(pulse|ping)' src/
rg -n '>\s*LIVE\s*<' src/
```

#### A hue check for hex literals

Class names are not the only way blue gets in. A hex value pasted from a mockup slips past every class-based grep. This script flags any hex color whose OKLCH hue falls in the banned band with visible chroma.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Flag hex colors with OKLCH hue 235 to 335 and chroma above 0.02."""
import math, re, sys

HEX = re.compile(r"#([0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{3})\b")

def to_lin(c):
    c /= 255
    return c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4

def oklch(hexstr):
    h = hexstr if len(hexstr) == 6 else "".join(ch * 2 for ch in hexstr)
    r, g, b = (to_lin(int(h[i:i + 2], 16)) for i in (0, 2, 4))
    l = (0.4122214708 * r + 0.5363325363 * g + 0.0514459929 * b) ** (1 / 3)
    m = (0.2119034982 * r + 0.6806995451 * g + 0.1073969566 * b) ** (1 / 3)
    s = (0.0883024619 * r + 0.2817188376 * g + 0.6299787005 * b) ** (1 / 3)
    a = 1.9779984951 * l - 2.4285922050 * m + 0.4505937099 * s
    bb = 0.0259040371 * l + 0.7827717662 * m - 0.8086757660 * s
    return math.hypot(a, bb), math.degrees(math.atan2(bb, a)) % 360

bad = 0
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    for n, line in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
        for m in HEX.finditer(line):
            chroma, hue = oklch(m.group(1))
            if chroma > 0.02 and 235 <= hue <= 335:
                print(f"{path}:{n}: #{m.group(1)} hue {hue:.0f} chroma {chroma:.3f}")
                bad += 1
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
```

Run it as `python3 scripts/hue_check.py $(git ls-files '*.css' '*.tsx' '*.html' '*.svg')`. The chroma floor of 0.02 lets near-neutral grays through (Newsprint's paper at chroma 0.003) and still catches Tailwind `gray-500` (`#6B7280`, 0.023) and the middle steps of `slate` (0.035 to 0.041), along with every blue and indigo.

#### Agent instructions

When an AI agent writes UI code for a project, add the rules to the instruction file it reads (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules` or the equivalent) in plain, checkable form:

```text
Color and depth rules for this repo:
- Colors come from CSS variables in src/styles/tokens.css. Never write a hex value or a Tailwind palette class in a component.
- One accent: var(--accent). No blue, indigo, violet or purple anywhere.
- No box-shadow except none. No ring utilities. Focus is outline 2px solid var(--focus), offset 2px.
- No gradients of any kind. No backdrop-filter. No blur. No glow. No text-shadow.
- Border radius is var(--radius) (2px). No rounded-lg or larger. rounded-full only on avatars and switches.
- Depth: borders (1px var(--rule), var(--rule-strong) for floating layers) and surface tones (--paper, --paper-2, --paper-3).
- Status: word plus icon plus color. No pulsing dots, no LIVE pills.
- Run npm run lint:color before finishing. It must exit 0.
```

#### Review checklist for 2.11

- Hex values exist only in the token file.
- The Tailwind theme replaces `colors`, `boxShadow`, `backgroundImage` and `borderRadius` instead of extending them; ring and gradient plugins are off (v3) or caught by grep (v4).
- Stylelint blocks shadows, gradients, blur and large radii.
- The grep commands and the hue check run in CI and exit 0.
- The agent instruction file lists the color rules in checkable form.

### 2.12 Review checklist for Part 2

Run this list on every screen before it ships. The chapter checklists above hold the detail.

#### Palette and status

- Neutrals have a named hue and chroma under 0.012; surface steps are 0.025 to 0.035 apart in OKLCH L (0.04 to 0.05 in dark mode).
- One accent, OKLCH hue outside 235 to 335, under 10% of the screen; bright accents split into fill and text tokens.
- Every shipped text pairing passes 4.5:1 on each surface it sits on; control boundaries pass 3:1; `--ink-3` appears only on `--paper`.
- Three status hues, each shown with a word and a distinct icon shape. No pulsing dots, no LIVE pill. Deltas colored by meaning.

#### Effects and depth

- No gradients of any kind or hue, no blur, glass, glow, `text-shadow`, noise, neon, spotlight, tilt or shimmer.
- `box-shadow: none` everywhere; no `shadow-*` or `ring-*` classes.
- Depth comes from tone steps, borders, overlap, spacing and inversion. Floating layers are opaque with a 1px `--rule-strong` border.
- Hover changes a border or tone in 120ms or less; selection combines tone, edge and icon; every layer edge survives forced colors mode.

#### Borders and radius

- Borders are 1px or 2px in token colors (3px double for grand totals, 4px for one masthead rule); never translucent; never more than two bordered containers deep.
- One radius, 2px or 0. Circles only for avatars, radios, switches, swatches and data marks.

#### Dark mode and charts

- A separate measured dark token set; darkest surface at L 0.16 to 0.22; no `#000` surfaces, no `#FFF` text; `color-scheme` set before first paint.
- Charts use the six-color set or gray plus one, stepped ramps with swatch legends, direct labels, and no library default colors.

#### Code

- Hex values live only in the token file; Tailwind theme keys are replaced, not extended.
- Stylelint, the grep commands and the hue check exit 0 in CI, and the fingerprint scan from 2.1 finds zero tells.

## Part 3. Type, Space, Layout, Icons and Motion

This Part sets the physical rules of a page: which faces, which sizes, how much space, where things sit, which icons, which images, what moves and for how long. Every value here matches the canonical tokens in the authoring rules. When a number in a later Part disagrees with a number here, this Part wins for type, space and motion.

A generated interface is easy to spot from across the room because it is assembled from defaults: Inter at `font-extrabold`, `tracking-tight` on every heading, `py-24` on every section, `max-w-7xl mx-auto` around everything, three cards with an icon in an indigo rounded square, and a fade-up on scroll. None of those choices is wrong in isolation. Together they are a fingerprint. The chapters below replace each default with a decision and a number.

### 3.1 Typefaces

#### Why the default face reads as generated

Inter is a good typeface. The problem is frequency. `create-next-app` loaded Inter through `next/font/google` in its starter `layout.tsx` for several major versions, shadcn/ui examples render in it, most Figma UI kits ship with it, and code generators reach for it because it is the most common face in their training data. When a page uses Inter at 400 for body, Inter at 800 for a 72px headline and Inter at 500 for buttons, a reader who has seen a hundred such pages recognizes the template before reading a word.

The swap to the next most popular face does not fix it. Geist (the newer `create-next-app` default), Space Grotesk (the face of a thousand crypto and AI landing pages), Satoshi, General Sans and Clash Display from Fontshare, Manrope, Plus Jakarta Sans and DM Sans are the second tier of the same fingerprint. Choosing one of them because a template did is the same non-decision.

The second tell is the giant gradient headline:

```slop
<h1 class="text-6xl md:text-7xl font-extrabold tracking-tighter
           bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500
           bg-clip-text text-transparent">
  Build faster. Ship smarter.
</h1>
```

Four defaults stack here: the extrabold weight, the negative tracking pulled from Tailwind's `tracking-tighter` (-0.05em), the clipped gradient fill, and a two-fragment slogan. Replace all four:

```html
<h1 class="display">Payroll for teams of 5 to 200, filed in every US state</h1>
```

```css
.display {
  font-family: var(--font-sans);
  font-size: 56px;
  line-height: 1.15;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  color: var(--ink);
  max-width: 20ch;
  text-wrap: balance;
}
```

#### Choosing a face

Pick a face for reasons you can write down. Check these properties before anything else, in this order:

1. **Glyph distinction.** Type `Il1 O0 rn m` at 14px. Capital I, lowercase l and the numeral 1 must differ. In product UI people read invoice numbers, API keys and coupon codes, so ambiguous glyphs cause support tickets.
2. **Figures.** The face needs tabular lining figures (`tnum`, `lnum` OpenType features). Without them, numbers in tables and timers wobble horizontally as they change.
3. **Language coverage.** If the product ships in Polish, Vietnamese or Turkish, the face needs those accents drawn, not synthesized. Check the character set before falling in love with a specimen.
4. **Weights you need, and no more.** Two weights cover almost all UI: 400 and 600. A third (500) is useful for button labels and table headers in dense UIs.
5. **x-height and width at 14px.** UI text is mostly 14px and 16px. A face with a small x-height (Garamond-style serifs, many geometric sans) reads small at those sizes and forces you to bump everything up a step.
6. **License.** SIL Open Font License (OFL) faces can be self-hosted and subset freely. Commercial faces need a web license sized to page views; read it before shipping.

#### Named alternatives

These are faces with a clear character, decent figures and broad coverage. None of them is a secret; they are simply less saturated than the template defaults.

Sans for UI and body:

- **IBM Plex Sans** (OFL). Slightly mechanical, distinct `l` with a tail, tabular figures, nine weights, Greek and Cyrillic, plus Plex Mono and Plex Serif in the same family. This handbook's canonical sans.
- **Source Sans 3** (OFL). Humanist, compact, very readable at 14px. Pairs with Source Serif 4 and Source Code Pro.
- **Public Sans** (OFL). Neutral, built for US government services, solid figures.
- **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (OFL). Drawn by the Braille Institute for low-vision readers. Exaggerated letter distinctions. Pick it when legibility is the brief.
- **Instrument Sans**, **Work Sans**, **Libre Franklin** (OFL). Each has more personality than Inter at display sizes.
- Commercial, when there is budget: Söhne, Untitled Sans, GT America, Graphik, ABC Diatype, Founders Grotesk.

Serif for long-form reading, docs and editorial headings:

- **Source Serif 4** (OFL). Has an optical size axis (`opsz`), so the same file draws sturdier shapes at 14px and finer ones at 56px. This handbook's canonical serif.
- **Literata** (OFL). Drawn for e-book reading, also has `opsz`.
- **Newsreader** (OFL). Editorial, with optical sizes.
- **Charter**. Ships with macOS and iOS as a system font; Bitstream Charter is free elsewhere. Sturdy at small sizes.
- **Spectral**, **Crimson Pro**, **EB Garamond** (OFL). Bookish. EB Garamond needs 18px or larger.

Monospace for code, IDs and fixed-width data:

- **IBM Plex Mono**, **JetBrains Mono**, **Source Code Pro**, **Iosevka** (all OFL). Berkeley Mono if there is budget.

#### Pairings that work

Pair faces with a job split, not for decoration. One face does UI, at most one more does long reading, and mono does code. Three families is the ceiling.

| Product | UI and headings | Long-form body | Code and IDs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Developer tool, dashboard | IBM Plex Sans | IBM Plex Sans | IBM Plex Mono |
| Docs site, knowledge base | IBM Plex Sans | Source Serif 4 at 18px | IBM Plex Mono |
| Publishing, essays | Source Serif 4 (headings 600) | Source Serif 4 | Source Code Pro |
| Government, health, forms | Public Sans or Atkinson Hyperlegible Next | same | system mono |
| Internal tool, zero budget | system UI stack | system UI stack | system mono stack |

Rules for pairing:

- Superfamilies (Plex, Source) pair without effort because the vertical metrics and figure styles were drawn together.
- Do not pair two sans faces. Inter for body and Space Grotesk for headings looks like two templates merged.
- Do not set UI chrome in a serif. Buttons, tabs, table headers and form labels stay in the sans.
- If you add a serif for headings only, use it at 32px and above. Serif headings at 21px next to sans body text look like a mistake.

#### System font stacks

A system stack costs zero bytes and zero layout shift. For internal tools, admin panels and anything behind a login where brand voice does not matter, use it and stop thinking about fonts.

```css
:root {
  --font-system: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto,
                 "Helvetica Neue", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif;
  --font-system-mono: ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", "Cascadia Code",
                      "Source Code Pro", Menlo, Consolas,
                      "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace;
  /* Serif stacks that need no download */
  --font-system-serif-transitional: Charter, "Bitstream Charter",
                                    "Sitka Text", Cambria, serif;
  --font-system-serif-oldstyle: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype",
                                "URW Palladio L", P052, serif;
}
```

Facts about the system stack you need to plan around:

- `system-ui` resolves to San Francisco on Apple platforms, Segoe UI on Windows, Roboto or Noto Sans on Android and whatever the desktop sets on Linux. Your layout must tolerate width differences of about 5 to 8 percent between them. Never size a button to fit its label exactly.
- On Windows, Segoe UI's figures are proportional by default; add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever numbers align.
- Tailwind's default `font-sans` appends `"Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji"` to the stack. Remove them. This handbook bans emoji in the interface, and the emoji fonts in the stack only matter if you allow them.

#### The canonical font tokens

Use these three tokens everywhere. Never write a family name directly in a component.

```css
:root {
  --font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --font-serif: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  --font-mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", Menlo, monospace;
}

html {
  font-family: var(--font-sans);
  font-size: 100%;          /* respect the reader's browser setting */
  font-synthesis: none;     /* no faux bold or faux italic */
  -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
  text-size-adjust: 100%;
}

code, kbd, samp, pre { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.875em; }
.prose { font-family: var(--font-serif); }
```

Wire the same tokens into Tailwind so utility classes cannot drift:

```js
// tailwind.config.js (v3)
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    fontFamily: {
      sans: ["var(--font-sans)"],
      serif: ["var(--font-serif)"],
      mono: ["var(--font-mono)"],
    },
  },
};
```

```css
/* Tailwind v4: tokens live in CSS */
@theme {
  --font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --font-serif: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
  --font-mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", Menlo, monospace;
}
```

`font-size: 100%` on `html` matters. Setting `html { font-size: 62.5% }` so that 1rem equals 10px breaks third-party components that assume 16px and it fights readers who raised their default size. Keep the root at the browser default and write rem values that map to the scale (0.875rem is 14px).

`font-synthesis: none` matters too. If you load only 400 and 600, a stray `font-bold` (700) makes the browser smear the 600 outlines into a fake bold. With synthesis off, it renders the nearest real weight instead.

#### Loading fonts without layout shift

A web font that arrives late causes two failures: invisible text (FOIT) while it loads, then a reflow when it replaces the fallback because the two faces have different widths and vertical metrics. Both are visible to users and the reflow counts toward Cumulative Layout Shift. Fix both.

Rules:

1. **Self-host WOFF2.** Do not hotlink a font CDN in production. Third-party font requests add a DNS lookup and a TLS handshake on the critical path, and some EU regulators have ruled that loading Google Fonts from Google's servers leaks visitor IP addresses. `next/font` and Fontsource both self-host at build time.
2. **Subset.** Ship the Latin subset by default and split other scripts with `unicode-range` so they load only when the page uses them. A static Latin subset of one weight is typically 15 to 30 KB as WOFF2. A full multilingual file can be 150 KB or more.
3. **Preload what is above the fold, and only that.** Usually one or two files: body 400 and heading 600. Every preload competes with the CSS and the hero image.
4. **Pick `font-display` on purpose.** `swap` shows fallback text immediately and swaps when the font arrives. `optional` gives the font about 100ms; if it misses, the page keeps the fallback for that view and the font is cached for the next one. Use `optional` for body text on content sites where a swap mid-read is worse than a fallback. Use `swap` with metric overrides (below) everywhere else. Never use `block`.
5. **Match fallback metrics.** Declare a fallback face built from a local system font with `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override` and `line-gap-override`, so the fallback occupies the same box as the web font. The swap then changes letter shapes but moves nothing.

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "IBM Plex Sans";
  src: url("/fonts/plex-sans-400-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
  unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6,
                 U+02DA, U+02DC, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2212, U+FEFF;
}

@font-face {
  font-family: "IBM Plex Sans";
  src: url("/fonts/plex-sans-600-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 600;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
  unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6,
                 U+02DA, U+02DC, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2212, U+FEFF;
}

/* Metric-matched fallback. Generate these four numbers with a tool
   (Capsize metrics, fontaine, or next/font's adjustFontFallback).
   The values below show the shape of the rule; measure your own files. */
@font-face {
  font-family: "IBM Plex Sans Fallback";
  src: local("Arial");
  size-adjust: 101.5%;
  ascent-override: 101%;
  descent-override: 27%;
  line-gap-override: 0%;
}

:root {
  --font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", "IBM Plex Sans Fallback", system-ui,
               -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
}
```

Preload the two files in the document head. The `crossorigin` attribute is required even for same-origin fonts; without it the browser fetches the file twice.

```html
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/plex-sans-400-latin.woff2"
      as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/plex-sans-600-latin.woff2"
      as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
```

In Next.js, `next/font` does the subsetting, self-hosting, preloading and fallback metrics for you. Use it and point it at the canonical variable:

```tsx
// app/fonts.ts
import { IBM_Plex_Sans, IBM_Plex_Mono, Source_Serif_4 } from "next/font/google";

export const sans = IBM_Plex_Sans({
  subsets: ["latin"],
  weight: ["400", "600"],
  display: "swap",
  variable: "--font-plex-sans",
});

export const mono = IBM_Plex_Mono({
  subsets: ["latin"],
  weight: ["400"],
  display: "swap",
  variable: "--font-plex-mono",
});

export const serif = Source_Serif_4({
  subsets: ["latin"],
  weight: ["400", "600"],
  style: ["normal", "italic"],
  display: "swap",
  variable: "--font-source-serif",
  preload: false, // only docs pages use it
});
```

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { sans, mono, serif } from "./fonts";
import "./globals.css";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className={`${sans.variable} ${mono.variable} ${serif.variable}`}>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```css
/* globals.css: the canonical tokens read from next/font's variables */
:root {
  --font-sans: var(--font-plex-sans), system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --font-mono: var(--font-plex-mono), ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", Menlo, monospace;
  --font-serif: var(--font-source-serif), Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
}
```

Check the result in the browser: open DevTools, throttle to Slow 4G, reload, and watch the hero. If any line rewraps when the font arrives, the fallback metrics are wrong.

#### Weights to ship

| Face | Ship | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sans | 400, 600 | Body and UI at 400; headings, button labels, table headers, emphasis at 600 |
| Sans (dense apps) | add 500 | Button labels and nav items when 600 is too loud at 14px |
| Serif (docs, essays) | 400, 400 italic, 600 | Body, emphasis, headings |
| Mono | 400 | Code, IDs, keyboard keys |

Hard limits:

- At most five font files on any page, and at most two preloaded.
- Never ship 100, 200 or 300 for text. Thin weights at 14px to 16px on a light background fall below legible stroke contrast on non-Retina screens, and `font-light text-gray-500` body copy is a common template tell.
- Never ship 800 or 900. `font-extrabold` and `font-black` headlines are the clearest single marker of a generated landing page. Size and space carry hierarchy; weight beyond 600 shouts.
- Italic only for the serif in long-form text. UI rarely needs italic; when it does (a variable name in a sentence, a book title), the browser's synthesized italic is turned off, so either ship the file or use a different signal.

A variable font file (one file, all weights) is worth it when you need three or more weights of the same style, or an optical size axis. For two weights, two static subsets are usually smaller than one variable file. Check the byte counts; do not assume.

#### Failure cases

```slop
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@100;200;300;400;500;600;700;800;900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<body class="font-sans antialiased">
  <h1 class="text-7xl font-black tracking-tighter">The future of work</h1>
  <p class="text-lg font-light text-gray-500">Experience seamless collaboration.</p>
```

Nine weights requested from a third-party origin, a 900-weight headline with -0.05em tracking, light gray body text at 300. Every choice is a framework default or a copied snippet.

```slop
body { font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; }
h1, h2, h3 { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; }
.hero-title { font-family: 'Clash Display'; }
```

Three display-oriented sans faces with no job split and no fallback stack. If any file fails to load, the browser falls back to the generic family with entirely different metrics.

```css
/* Fixed: one family, two weights, a real fallback stack */
body { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-weight: 400; }
h1, h2, h3 { font-weight: 600; }
```

### 3.2 Type scale and hierarchy

#### The canonical scale

Nine sizes, in pixels: 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 32, 40, 56. Body is 16. Nothing else. No 13px, no 15px, no 20px, no 36px, no 48px, no 60px, no 72px. If a design needs a size that is not on the list, the design needs another look, not another size.

Each size has a job:

| Token | px | rem | Line height (px) | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-12` | 12 | 0.75 | 16 | Captions, timestamps, uppercase labels, badges, footnotes |
| `--text-14` | 14 | 0.875 | 20 | Secondary UI text, table cells, form help, nav items in dense apps |
| `--text-16` | 16 | 1 | 24 | Body text, form inputs, buttons, default UI |
| `--text-18` | 18 | 1.125 | 28 | Long-form body (docs, articles), lead paragraph |
| `--text-21` | 21 | 1.3125 | 28 | h4, card titles, dialog titles |
| `--text-24` | 24 | 1.5 | 32 | h3, page titles inside an app |
| `--text-32` | 32 | 2 | 40 | h2, section headings on marketing and docs pages |
| `--text-40` | 40 | 2.5 | 48 | h1 on docs and app landing screens; page h1 on mobile |
| `--text-56` | 56 | 3.5 | 64 | Display: one per page at most, desktop marketing h1 only |

```css
:root {
  --text-12: 0.75rem;   --lh-12: 1rem;
  --text-14: 0.875rem;  --lh-14: 1.25rem;
  --text-16: 1rem;      --lh-16: 1.5rem;
  --text-18: 1.125rem;  --lh-18: 1.75rem;
  --text-21: 1.3125rem; --lh-21: 1.75rem;
  --text-24: 1.5rem;    --lh-24: 2rem;
  --text-32: 2rem;      --lh-32: 2.5rem;
  --text-40: 2.5rem;    --lh-40: 3rem;
  --text-56: 3.5rem;    --lh-56: 4rem;
}

body { font-size: var(--text-16); line-height: var(--lh-16); color: var(--ink); }
h1 { font-size: var(--text-40); line-height: var(--lh-40); font-weight: 600; }
h2 { font-size: var(--text-32); line-height: var(--lh-32); font-weight: 600; }
h3 { font-size: var(--text-24); line-height: var(--lh-24); font-weight: 600; }
h4 { font-size: var(--text-21); line-height: var(--lh-21); font-weight: 600; }
small, .caption { font-size: var(--text-12); line-height: var(--lh-12); }
```

Every line height lands on a multiple of 4px, so text blocks sit on the same 4px grid as the spacing scale in 3.4. The ratios fall out of that: 1.5 at 16px, about 1.43 at 14px, 1.33 at 12px, 1.25 at 24px and 32px, 1.2 at 40px, about 1.14 at 56px. Body runs at 1.5; headings run between 1.15 and 1.25, as the canonical tokens require. Where a ratio sits a hair outside, the 4px grid wins.

To restrict Tailwind to the scale, replace the theme instead of extending it, so `text-5xl` and its relatives stop existing:

```js
// tailwind.config.js (v3): replace, do not extend
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    fontSize: {
      12: ["0.75rem", { lineHeight: "1rem" }],
      14: ["0.875rem", { lineHeight: "1.25rem" }],
      16: ["1rem", { lineHeight: "1.5rem" }],
      18: ["1.125rem", { lineHeight: "1.75rem" }],
      21: ["1.3125rem", { lineHeight: "1.75rem" }],
      24: ["1.5rem", { lineHeight: "2rem" }],
      32: ["2rem", { lineHeight: "2.5rem", letterSpacing: "-0.01em" }],
      40: ["2.5rem", { lineHeight: "3rem", letterSpacing: "-0.01em" }],
      56: ["3.5rem", { lineHeight: "4rem", letterSpacing: "-0.015em" }],
    },
  },
};
```

Now `text-16` and `text-32` are the only spellings, and a reviewer sees the pixel value in the class name.

#### Hierarchy with few levers

Hierarchy comes from four levers, used in this order: size, weight, space, color. Use the fewest that make the order unambiguous.

- Adjacent heading levels differ by at least one scale step and usually two. h2 at 32 over h3 at 24 reads as two levels. h2 at 24 over h3 at 21 does not.
- Headings are 600. Body is 400. Do not mix 500, 600 and 700 among headings to fake extra levels.
- A heading sits closer to the text it introduces than to the text above it (space above about twice the space below; see 3.4).
- Color is the last lever. `--ink` for headings and body, `--ink-2` for secondary text, `--ink-3` for metadata. Never color a heading with the accent to make it important.
- Keep the visual level independent from the HTML level. A sidebar's "Filters" heading is an `h2` for the outline but may render at 14px 600. Use classes for looks and elements for structure.

```html
<aside aria-labelledby="filters-h">
  <h2 id="filters-h" class="label">Filters</h2>
  ...
</aside>
```

```css
.label {
  font-size: var(--text-14);
  line-height: var(--lh-14);
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--ink);
}
```

A complete app screen often needs only four sizes: 24 for the page title, 16 for body and controls, 14 for tables and secondary text, 12 for metadata. If a single screen uses seven sizes, collapse it.

#### Letter spacing

Tailwind's `tracking-tight` is -0.025em and `tracking-tighter` is -0.05em. Generated pages apply one of them to every heading and sometimes to body text, because the Tailwind UI hero examples do. At 16px, -0.025em removes 0.4px between every pair of letters, which closes counters and makes `rn` read as `m`.

The rules:

| Size | letter-spacing |
| --- | --- |
| 12px uppercase labels | 0.06em |
| 12px to 21px, sentence case | 0 |
| 24px | 0 to -0.005em |
| 32px and 40px | -0.01em |
| 56px | -0.015em, never past -0.02em |
| Monospace at any size | 0 |

Large type needs a little negative tracking because fonts are spaced for text sizes, and the gaps grow optically as size grows. A face with optical sizes (Source Serif 4 with `font-optical-sizing: auto`) already corrects for this, so leave its tracking at 0. Test negative tracking against the actual glyphs: at 56px, -0.015em is 0.84px, which is enough.

```slop
<h2 class="text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight">Everything you need</h2>
<p class="mt-6 text-lg leading-8 tracking-tight text-gray-600">...</p>
```

```css
h2 { font-size: var(--text-32); line-height: var(--lh-32); letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
p  { letter-spacing: 0; }
```

#### Measure

Prose runs at most 66ch wide. The comfortable range is 45 to 75 characters per line; 66 is the classic target. The `ch` unit is the advance width of the digit 0, and most lowercase letters are narrower than a zero, so `66ch` usually fits somewhat more than 66 average characters. For long reading, that slight overshoot is fine; do not go wider.

Apply the measure to the text element, not to the page container. A table or a code block in the same column may use the full width.

```css
.prose > :where(p, ul, ol, blockquote, h2, h3, h4) { max-width: 66ch; }
.prose > :where(pre, table, figure) { max-width: 100%; }

/* Headings get a narrower measure so they break into balanced lines */
.prose h1, .prose h2 { max-width: 24ch; text-wrap: balance; }
```

Failure cases:

- Body text running the full 1280px container: about 180 characters per line at 16px. Readers lose their place on the return sweep.
- Centered paragraphs constrained to `max-w-2xl` (672px) under a centered hero: the measure is fine, the ragged left edge is not (see 3.3).
- A two-column layout where each column is 30ch: fine for a sidebar list, too narrow for paragraphs, and it triggers rivers of space if justified.

#### Heading sizes on landing pages

The landing page h1 is 40px on narrow screens and 56px on wide ones. Nothing larger. The 72px, 96px and 128px headlines (`text-7xl`, `text-8xl`, `text-9xl`) on generated landing pages exist because the hero has nothing to say, so the type has to fill the space. A headline with real content needs fewer pixels.

The copy pattern matters as much as the size. The generated hero is two to four words plus a buzzword:

```slop
<h1 class="text-7xl font-extrabold">Email, Reimagined.</h1>
<h1 class="text-8xl font-bold">The Future of Finance</h1>
<h1 class="text-7xl">Work smarter, not harder.</h1>
```

Write a sentence that names what the product does and for whom, 6 to 14 words, and set it at the scale's display size with a narrow measure so it breaks into two or three balanced lines:

```html
<header class="hero">
  <h1>Shared inboxes for support teams that answer in more than one language</h1>
  <p class="lead">Route by language, translate replies in place, and keep one thread
     per customer. Works with Gmail and Outlook.</p>
</header>
```

```css
.hero h1 {
  font-size: clamp(var(--text-40), 2rem + 2vw, var(--text-56));
  line-height: 1.15;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  max-width: 22ch;
  text-wrap: balance;
}
.hero .lead {
  font-size: var(--text-18);
  line-height: var(--lh-18);
  color: var(--ink-2);
  max-width: 52ch;
  margin-top: 16px;
}
```

About the `clamp()`: the middle term mixes `rem` and `vw` on purpose. A size made only of `vw` does not grow when the reader zooms the page, which fails WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text). Anchoring to rem keeps zoom working. The two ends are scale values, so the fluid size never lands outside the scale at the extremes.

Only the h1 is fluid. h2 and below use fixed scale values with one breakpoint, if any. A page where every heading uses its own `clamp()` produces sizes like 27.4px that belong to no scale.

#### Numerals

Numbers have their own typography. Three OpenType features cover nearly every case:

- `tabular-nums`: every digit has the same width. Use in tables, prices that update, timers, counters, version lists, anything stacked vertically or changing in place.
- `lining-nums`: digits sit on the baseline at cap height. Default in most sans faces. Use in UI.
- `oldstyle-nums`: digits with ascenders and descenders that sit like lowercase letters. Use in serif long-form prose so years and numbers in a sentence do not shout. Source Serif 4 and Literata support them.

Plus `slashed-zero` for IDs, codes and keys, where O and 0 must not be confused.

```css
table, .num, time, .price, .duration { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; }
.prose { font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums proportional-nums; }
.prose table { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; }
.id, .api-key, .order-number { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero; }

td.num, th.num { text-align: right; }
```

Right-align numeric columns so the place values line up, and align the column header to match. Keep the same number of decimals down a column: `12.50`, `8.00`, `130.25`, not `12.5`, `8`, `130.25`.

If a face lacks `tnum`, `font-variant-numeric` silently does nothing. Check in the browser: type `1111` over `8888` in a table cell and compare widths.

#### Small caps

Real small caps are capitals drawn at about x-height with stroke weights matched to the lowercase. Use them for acronyms in running serif text (NASA, HTML, API) so a sentence full of acronyms does not look like shouting.

```css
.prose abbr { font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
```

Use them only when the face contains the `smcp` and `c2sc` features. Source Serif 4 does. Many sans faces do not. When the feature is missing, the browser synthesizes small caps by shrinking full capitals, which makes thin, spindly letters that look broken next to the lowercase. In that case, leave the acronyms as plain capitals.

#### Uppercase labels

Uppercase text is a tool for short labels, not a voice. Tailwind UI's feature sections open with a small uppercase "eyebrow" in the accent color above every heading (`text-base font-semibold leading-7 text-indigo-600` reading "Deploy faster"), and generated pages copy it onto every section. One eyebrow on one page is a choice. Six is a template.

Rules for uppercase:

- 12px only, weight 500 or 600, `letter-spacing: 0.06em`, color `--ink-2` or `--ink-3`. Never the accent.
- Three words at most. Never a sentence, never a heading above 14px, never body copy, never a button in a form.
- Uppercase via CSS `text-transform`, with the source text in sentence case. Some screen readers spell out text typed in capitals letter by letter, and copy-paste should give the reader normal text.
- Good uses: table column headers in dense data tables, a section label in a sidebar group, metadata keys in a definition list, the label on a keyboard shortcut.

```css
.overline {
  font-size: var(--text-12);
  line-height: var(--lh-12);
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ink-3);
}
```

```html
<dl class="meta">
  <div><dt class="overline">Region</dt><dd>eu-west-1</dd></div>
  <div><dt class="overline">Created</dt><dd><time datetime="2026-03-14">14 Mar 2026</time></dd></div>
</dl>
```

```slop
<p class="text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-widest text-indigo-600">Why choose us</p>
<h2 class="mt-2 text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight">Everything you need to scale</h2>
```

`tracking-widest` is 0.1em, the accent color makes the label compete with the heading, and the label says nothing the heading does not.

#### Weight and color for emphasis

- Inside a paragraph, emphasis is `<em>` (italic in serif text) or `<strong>` at 600. One or two per paragraph.
- Do not bold a key phrase in every paragraph. Generated copy does this so skimmers find the "point", and the result is a page where nothing stands out.
- Do not color words in a sentence. A headline with one word in the accent color (`<span class="text-indigo-600">faster</span>`) is a template pattern.
- Secondary text goes to `--ink-2` at the same size, or one step down to 14px. Not both plus lighter weight.

#### Failure cases in one block

```slop
<section class="py-24 text-center">
  <p class="text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-indigo-600">Features</p>
  <h2 class="mt-2 text-5xl font-extrabold tracking-tight text-gray-900">
    Supercharge your <span class="text-indigo-600">workflow</span>
  </h2>
  <p class="mx-auto mt-6 max-w-2xl text-xl leading-8 text-gray-500">
    Our platform helps you do more with less, faster than ever before.
  </p>
</section>
```

Count the defaults: accent eyebrow, 48px extrabold with negative tracking, an accent-colored word, centered 20px gray lead, 96px vertical padding. The fix is not a new combination of the same utilities. It is a heading that states something, at a scale size, left-aligned on the page's edge:

```html
<section class="section">
  <h2>Approvals, budgets and receipts in the same place</h2>
  <p>Managers approve from the email notification. Finance sees the budget
     impact before the money moves.</p>
</section>
```

```css
.section h2 { font-size: var(--text-32); line-height: var(--lh-32); letter-spacing: -0.01em; max-width: 24ch; }
.section p  { font-size: var(--text-18); line-height: var(--lh-18); color: var(--ink-2); max-width: 60ch; margin-top: 16px; }
```

### 3.3 Text details

#### Alignment

Paragraphs are left-aligned (`text-align: start`, which flips correctly for right-to-left languages). The left edge is where the eye returns after every line; a ragged left edge makes every return a search.

Centered text is allowed in exactly these places:

- A single line of two to eight words that stands alone: an empty-state title, a short confirmation message in a narrow dialog, a figure caption under a centered image.
- Labels inside buttons, tabs and badges.
- Numbers in a cell when the column is a short status or icon column.

Centered text is not allowed for paragraphs, for lists, for anything over two lines, or for section headings that sit above left-aligned content. The centered landing page (centered eyebrow, centered h1, centered 20px gray paragraph, two centered buttons, centered logo row) is the most common generated layout on the web, and it comes straight from the Tailwind UI and shadcn hero blocks. Chapter 3.5 covers the layout fix; the text fix is to put the headline and the paragraph on the same left edge as everything below them.

```slop
<div class="mx-auto max-w-2xl text-center">
  <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold">Trusted by thousands</h2>
  <p class="mt-4 text-lg text-gray-600">Teams of every size rely on our platform to get more
  done every day, with features designed to help them collaborate and grow.</p>
</div>
```

Do not justify text on the web unless the column also hyphenates and is at least 50ch wide. Browser justification works line by line, not paragraph by paragraph, so without hyphenation it opens gaps between words ("rivers") that are worse than a ragged right edge.

#### Widows, orphans and balanced lines

A single short word alone on the last line of a heading looks like a mistake. Two CSS properties fix most cases:

```css
h1, h2, h3, h4, .card-title, figcaption { text-wrap: balance; }
p, li, dd { text-wrap: pretty; }
```

- `text-wrap: balance` spreads a heading across lines of similar length. Chromium limits balancing to blocks of six lines or fewer, which covers every heading you should write. Supported in Chromium, Firefox and Safari.
- `text-wrap: pretty` lets the browser spend more effort on paragraph endings, mainly to avoid a one-word last line. Supported in Chromium and recent Safari; elsewhere it falls back to normal wrapping, which is harmless.

For short strings where a specific pair must stay together, use a non-breaking space (`&nbsp;`, U+00A0):

- Between a number and its unit: `16&nbsp;GB`, `30&nbsp;min`, `4.2&nbsp;MB`.
- Between a title and a name, an initial and a surname: `Dr.&nbsp;Okafor`.
- Between the last two words of a button label that wraps in a narrow layout.

Do not paste `&nbsp;` into every paragraph to fight widows by hand. Rewriting a sentence is cheaper than maintaining manual breaks across breakpoints.

#### Hyphenation and overflow

Turn on hyphenation for narrow columns of prose: sidebars, multi-column text under 40ch, mobile layouts of long-form articles. It requires a correct `lang` attribute, because the browser uses the language's dictionary.

```html
<html lang="en">
```

```css
.prose { hyphens: manual; }
@media (max-width: 30em) {
  .prose p { hyphens: auto; hyphenate-limit-chars: 7 3 3; }
}
h1, h2, h3, h4, a, code, .no-hyphens { hyphens: manual; }
```

`hyphenate-limit-chars: 7 3 3` means only words of seven or more letters are hyphenated, with at least three letters before and after the break. Without it, the browser can split "into" as "in-to".

Never hyphenate headings, links or code. For strings that cannot break naturally (URLs, hashes, email addresses, file paths), allow breaks anywhere instead of letting them overflow the container:

```css
.prose a, .prose code, td, .breakable { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
```

Avoid `word-break: break-all` on body text; it breaks ordinary words at arbitrary letters even when a normal break exists. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` only breaks inside a word when the word would otherwise overflow.

#### Quotes and apostrophes

Use typographic quotes in all interface copy and prose:

| Character | Name | Code point | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ’ | right single quote | U+2019 | apostrophes: don’t, it’s, the ’90s |
| ‘ ’ | single quotes | U+2018, U+2019 | quotes inside quotes |
| “ ” | double quotes | U+201C, U+201D | quotations |
| ′ ″ | prime, double prime | U+2032, U+2033 | feet and inches, minutes and seconds of arc |

Straight quotes (`'` and `"`) belong only in code, in values the user will type or paste, and in monospace UI such as a terminal. Write them directly in source as UTF-8; do not rely on a Markdown processor to curl them, because it gets apostrophes before numerals and after closing tags wrong.

For quotations rendered with `<q>`, let CSS supply the marks per language:

```css
q { quotes: "\201C" "\201D" "\2018" "\2019"; }
:lang(fr) q { quotes: "\00AB\00A0" "\00A0\00BB"; }
:lang(de) q { quotes: "\201E" "\201C" "\201A" "\2018"; }
```

`hanging-punctuation: first` pulls an opening quote mark into the margin so the letters align with the paragraph edge. Only Safari supports it; set it anyway, it degrades to normal setting.

#### Ellipsis

Use the single ellipsis character (…, U+2026), not three periods. In UI it has two jobs:

- **A continuing state**: `Saving…`, `Uploading 3 of 12…`, `Connecting…`. The action is in progress.
- **An action that needs more input before it runs**: a menu item `Rename…` or `Export as…` opens a dialog. A menu item without the ellipsis acts immediately. This is the macOS and Windows convention, and power users rely on it.

Do not use an ellipsis for drama in headings or marketing copy ("And then… everything changed"). Do not end a button label that runs immediately with one.

Truncation uses CSS, and the full text must stay reachable:

```css
.truncate {
  overflow: hidden;
  white-space: nowrap;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  min-width: 0;            /* required inside flex and grid items */
}
.clamp-2 {
  display: -webkit-box;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
  line-clamp: 2;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

```html
<td class="truncate" title="Q3 2026 vendor reconciliation, EMEA, final.xlsx">
  Q3 2026 vendor reconciliation, EMEA, final.xlsx
</td>
```

The `title` attribute is a weak fallback (no touch access, no keyboard access). Where truncated text matters, link to the full record or expand on click. Truncate from the middle for file names and paths, where the end carries the meaning: `invoice-2026-…-final.pdf`. That needs JavaScript or server-side shortening; CSS only truncates the end.

#### Numbers, units and math signs

- Thousands separators via `Intl.NumberFormat`, never hand-built strings. `12,480` in en-US, `12.480` in de-DE, `12 480` in fr-FR (a narrow no-break space).
