- A non-breaking space between number and unit: `250&nbsp;ms`, `16&nbsp;GB`, `3&nbsp;users`. Percent attaches in English (`12%`) and takes a space in French and German.
- A true minus sign (−, U+2212) for negative numbers in tables and financial figures. The hyphen is shorter and sits lower. `Intl.NumberFormat` outputs a hyphen-minus in most locales; replace it where alignment matters.
- The multiplication sign (×, U+00D7) for dimensions: `1920 × 1080`, `2×` zoom.
- Ranges: write `10 to 20` in prose. In tables and compact UI, `10-20` with a plain hyphen. This handbook does not use the en dash glyph.
- Same precision down a column, same unit down a column, unit in the column header when every row shares it: `Size (MB)` heading, bare numbers in cells.
- Abbreviate large numbers only where space forces it, and keep one decimal: `1.2k`, `48.6M`. Use the compact formatter so the suffix is localized.

```ts
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" });
money.format(-1234.5);         // "-€1,234.50"

const compact = new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { notation: "compact", maximumFractionDigits: 1 });
compact.format(48_620_000);    // "48.6M"

const pct = new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 });
pct.format(0.1234);            // "12.3%"

// Replace hyphen-minus with U+2212 for tabular display
export const tableNumber = (s: string) => s.replace(/^-/, "−");
```

#### Dates and times

- Use an unambiguous human format: `14 Mar 2026` or `Mar 14, 2026`, matching the locale. Never `03/04/2026`, which is March 4 in the US and 3 April almost everywhere else.
- Wrap every date in `<time datetime>` with the ISO 8601 value. It gives screen readers, scrapers and translation tools the exact value.
- Relative times (`5 min ago`, `yesterday`) for events in the last 7 days in feeds and activity logs. Switch to the absolute date after that. Always expose the absolute timestamp on hover and focus.
- Show the time zone whenever two people might read the same time differently: scheduled jobs, deadlines, meeting times. `09:00 CET`, or the reader's own zone with the abbreviation.
- 24-hour or 12-hour follows the locale; let `Intl.DateTimeFormat` decide.
- Durations in tabular numerals: `02:14:09` for a running timer, `2 h 14 min` for a static value.

```tsx
const rtf = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("en", { numeric: "auto" });
const abs = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" });

export function When({ iso }: { iso: string }) {
  const d = new Date(iso);
  const mins = Math.round((d.getTime() - Date.now()) / 60000);
  const label =
    Math.abs(mins) < 60 ? rtf.format(mins, "minute")
    : Math.abs(mins) < 1440 ? rtf.format(Math.round(mins / 60), "hour")
    : Math.abs(mins) < 10080 ? rtf.format(Math.round(mins / 1440), "day")
    : abs.format(d);
  return <time dateTime={iso} title={abs.format(d)}>{label}</time>;
}
```

#### Links

Links in running text are underlined. Color alone does not identify a link for readers with color vision deficiency, and WCAG 1.4.1 requires a non-color cue. The underline is the cue that everyone already knows.

```css
a {
  color: inherit;
  text-decoration-line: underline;
  text-decoration-thickness: 1px;
  text-underline-offset: 0.2em;
  text-decoration-color: var(--ink-3);
}
a:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-decoration-color: currentColor; }
a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; text-decoration: none; }
.prose a:visited { text-decoration-color: var(--ink-2); }

/* Links inside nav, tabs and button groups: position already says "clickable" */
nav a, .tabs a, a.button { text-decoration: none; }
```

Rules:

- Link text says where it goes. "Read the billing docs", not "click here" or "learn more". Screen reader users jump through a list of links out of context.
- One link per destination per paragraph.
- Do not open links in a new tab by default. If you must (a help link inside a half-filled form), say so in the text: `Billing docs (opens in new tab)`.
- Do not use the accent color plus no underline plus a hover underline. It fails 1.4.1 unless the link color has 3:1 contrast against the surrounding text, and the canonical accent does not reach that against `--ink`.
- External link icons are optional; if you use one, use the icon set's arrow-up-right at 12px, `aria-hidden`, after the text.

#### No text gradients

Text filled with a gradient (`bg-clip-text text-transparent bg-gradient-to-r`) is banned. It is the single most recognizable mark of a generated hero, and it also fails in practice:

- Contrast cannot be checked: part of every letter sits on a light stop and part on a dark one, and automated checkers report a pass or fail at random.
- Selection highlights render oddly, because the text color is transparent.
- The text disappears when the background image fails to paint: in some print modes, in reader views and in email clients that strip backgrounds.

Use `--ink` for headings. If a single headline must carry the brand color, set the whole heading in `--accent`, check that it reaches 4.5:1 (the canonical accent is 5.1:1 on `--paper`), and do it once in the product.

```slop
<span class="bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-600 to-violet-600 bg-clip-text text-transparent">AI-powered</span>
```

#### Lists and bullets

Lists use real list markup and plain markers. Emoji bullets (a rocket, a lightning bolt, a check mark emoji at the start of each line) are banned, as are the check-mark lines in pricing tables rendered as emoji.

```slop
- :rocket: Blazing fast builds
- :zap: Lightning deploys
- :lock: Enterprise-grade security
- :sparkles: AI-powered insights
```

Each marker is an OS emoji glyph that renders differently on Apple, Google and Microsoft systems, ignores your color tokens, is read aloud by screen readers (the listener hears "rocket" before the feature name), and repeats what the words say.

```css
.prose ul { list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 1.25em; }
.prose ul ::marker { color: var(--ink-3); }
.prose ol { list-style: decimal; padding-inline-start: 1.5em; }
.prose ol ::marker { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink-2); }
.prose li + li { margin-top: 8px; }

/* A dash marker, if the brand wants something quieter than a disc */
.dash-list { list-style-type: "-  "; }
```

For a feature list where each row has a yes or no, use a table with an SVG check icon plus visually hidden text (see 3.7), not a column of emoji.

#### Case

- Sentence case for headings, buttons, menu items, tab labels and table headers: `Create invoice`, `Billing settings`. Title Case (`Get Started Today`, `Unlock Your Potential`) is a marketing-template tell and slows reading.
- Proper nouns and product names keep their own capitalization.
- No all-caps headings (see uppercase label rules in 3.2).

### 3.4 Spacing system

#### The canonical scale

Ten values, in pixels: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Every margin, padding and gap is one of them. No 5, 6, 10, 14, 18, 20, 40, 56, 80.

```css
:root {
  --space-4: 4px;
  --space-8: 8px;
  --space-12: 12px;
  --space-16: 16px;
  --space-24: 24px;
  --space-32: 32px;
  --space-48: 48px;
  --space-64: 64px;
  --space-96: 96px;
  --space-128: 128px;
}
```

Naming the tokens by their pixel value means a reviewer reads `--space-24` and knows the number. Abstract names (`--space-md`, `--space-lg`) hide the value and invite arguments about what "medium" means.

Tailwind's default spacing scale already contains these values. Use only the matching keys and remove the rest from the theme so stray values fail the build:

| Canonical px | Tailwind key | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 1 | `gap-1` |
| 8 | 2 | `p-2` |
| 12 | 3 | `px-3` |
| 16 | 4 | `p-4` |
| 24 | 6 | `gap-6` |
| 32 | 8 | `mt-8` |
| 48 | 12 | `py-12` |
| 64 | 16 | `mt-16` |
| 96 | 24 | `py-24` (only where 3.4 says so) |
| 128 | 32 | `mt-32` |

```js
// tailwind.config.js (v3): replace spacing so p-5, gap-7, mt-10 stop existing
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    spacing: {
      0: "0", px: "1px",
      1: "4px", 2: "8px", 3: "12px", 4: "16px", 6: "24px",
      8: "32px", 12: "48px", 16: "64px", 24: "96px", 32: "128px",
    },
  },
};
```

Arbitrary values (`p-[13px]`, `mt-[72px]`) are banned in review. Each one is a decision that did not get made.

#### Inner space is smaller than outer space

Spacing is how a reader groups things. Elements that belong together sit closer than elements that do not. This is the proximity rule, and every layout decision in this chapter derives from it.

A working ladder:

| Relationship | Space |
| --- | --- |
| Icon to its label, label to its value inline | 4 to 8 |
| Form label to its input; heading to its first paragraph | 8 |
| Paragraph to paragraph; list item to list item in UI | 12 to 16 |
| Field to field in a form; card padding | 16 to 24 |
| Group of fields to the next group; subsection to subsection | 32 to 48 |
| Section to section within a page | 48 to 96 |
| Major topic change on a long page; hero to first section | 96 to 128 |

Check every screen against this ladder. The most common failure is equal space everywhere: a form where the label sits 16px above its input and the next label sits 16px below the input, so labels float halfway between two fields. Halve the label gap and double the field gap.

```css
.field { display: grid; gap: var(--space-8); }
.form  { display: grid; gap: var(--space-24); }
.form fieldset + fieldset { margin-top: var(--space-48); }
```

#### Spacing as the main grouping tool

Generated interfaces group with containers: a card with a border, a radius and a shadow around every block, then a card inside the card. Space does the same work with less ink. Reach for space first, a 1px rule second, a tonal surface (`--paper-2`) third, and a bordered panel only when the group must look movable, selectable or separate from the page.

```slop
<div class="rounded-2xl bg-white p-8 shadow-lg">
  <div class="rounded-xl border p-6 shadow-sm">
    <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold">Notifications</h3>
    <div class="mt-4 rounded-lg bg-gray-50 p-4">
      <div class="rounded-md border bg-white p-3">Email me when an invoice is paid</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Four nested surfaces for one checkbox. Each wrapper adds padding, so the actual control ends up 76px from the page edge.

```html
<section class="settings-group" aria-labelledby="notif-h">
  <h2 id="notif-h">Notifications</h2>
  <p class="help">Sent to finance@acme.example</p>
  <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" checked> Email me when an invoice is paid</label>
  <label class="check"><input type="checkbox"> Email me when a payment fails</label>
</section>
```

```css
.settings-group { display: grid; gap: var(--space-12); padding-block: var(--space-32); border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.settings-group h2 { font-size: var(--text-18); line-height: var(--lh-18); }
.settings-group .help { color: var(--ink-2); font-size: var(--text-14); margin-top: calc(var(--space-8) * -1); }
```

One rule separates the groups; space separates everything inside them.

#### Vertical rhythm

Line heights from 3.2 are all multiples of 4px. Keep margins on the same 4px grid and the page aligns without a baseline grid tool.

Headings get more space above than below, about two to one, so each heading visibly belongs to the text that follows it:

```css
.prose > * + * { margin-top: var(--space-16); }
.prose > h2 { margin-top: var(--space-48); }
.prose > h3 { margin-top: var(--space-32); }
.prose > h2 + *, .prose > h3 + * { margin-top: var(--space-12); }
.prose > :where(pre, table, figure) { margin-block: var(--space-24); }
```

The `* + *` selector (the "flow" or "owl" pattern) sets space between siblings only, so the first and last children never add stray space at the edges of the container. Use it instead of `mb-4` on every element, which leaves a trailing margin inside every box.

For component layouts, prefer `gap` on a flex or grid parent over margins on children. `gap` never collapses, never leaks out of the container, and moves with reordering.

#### Section spacing on marketing pages

`py-24 sm:py-32` is the vertical padding on nearly every section block in Tailwind UI, and generated pages apply it to every section regardless of content. The page becomes a stack of equal slabs with 96px to 128px of air between each, and the rhythm says "these sections are unrelated and equally important", which is almost never true.

Vary section spacing by relationship:

- 128px after the hero, before the first content section.
- 48 to 64px between sections that continue the same topic (a feature and its detail, a pricing table and its FAQ).
- 96px at a real change of topic.
- A 1px `--rule` line with 48px on either side works better than 128px of empty space when the sections are dense.
- The last section before the footer gets 96px, the footer itself 48px of padding.

Do not alternate full-bleed background colors (`bg-white`, `bg-gray-50`, `bg-white`) on every other section to separate them. That pattern exists because equal padding failed to group anything. Change background only for a section that really is different: a code sample panel on `--paper-2`, the footer.

```css
.page > section { padding-block: var(--space-64); }
.page > .hero { padding-block: var(--space-96) var(--space-128); }
.page > section.continues { padding-top: var(--space-24); }
.page > section.new-topic { padding-top: var(--space-96); border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
```

#### Density

Pick a density per product and per surface, then set it with tokens, not with one-off padding.

| Density | Row height | Text | Cell padding | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compact | 32px | 14px | 4px 8px | Trading, logs, spreadsheets, admin tables with 50+ rows |
| Default | 40px | 14 to 16px | 8px 12px | Most app screens, settings, lists |
| Comfortable | 48px | 16px | 12px 16px | Touch-first apps, consumer forms, onboarding |

A tool people use for hours is a compact-to-default product. Generated dashboards ship comfortable density everywhere (`p-6` cards, `py-4` table cells, 64px rows) because the template was designed for a screenshot, not for a person scanning 400 rows. Fewer rows on screen means more scrolling and less comparison.

```css
:root {
  --row-h: 40px;
  --cell-py: var(--space-8);
  --cell-px: var(--space-12);
}
[data-density="compact"] {
  --row-h: 32px;
  --cell-py: var(--space-4);
  --cell-px: var(--space-8);
}
[data-density="comfortable"] {
  --row-h: 48px;
  --cell-py: var(--space-12);
  --cell-px: var(--space-16);
}
@media (pointer: coarse) {
  :root:not([data-density="compact"]) { --row-h: 48px; }
}

td, th { padding: var(--cell-py) var(--cell-px); height: var(--row-h); }
```

Let the reader switch density in data-heavy products, and remember the choice.

#### Padding inside controls

- Buttons: 8px vertical by 16px horizontal at 16px text gives a 40px button; 12px by 16px for 48px touch. When the button has a leading icon, reduce the padding on the icon side to 12px so the icon and text look centered as a unit.
- Inputs: same height as buttons in the same row. A 40px input next to a 36px button is the most common misalignment in generated forms.
- Badges: 0 by 8px at 12px text, 20px tall.
- Cards: 16px or 24px padding. 32px padding around a single line of text wastes space and reads as template.

#### Failure cases

```slop
<div class="space-y-8">
  <div class="mb-6 mt-10 px-7 py-5">...</div>
  <div class="mt-[18px] p-[22px]">...</div>
</div>
```

Off-scale values everywhere, margins on children fighting `space-y` on the parent. Every value is a guess.

### 3.5 Layout and grid

#### The two generated layouts

Almost every generated landing page and dashboard is built from two layouts.

**The centered stack.** Every block is centered in a `max-w-7xl mx-auto` container, and inside it, every heading and paragraph is centered too:

```slop
[ centered pill: "New: AI features" ]
[ centered h1, 72px, gradient ]
[ centered gray paragraph, max-w-2xl ]
[ two centered buttons: "Get started" (indigo) + "Learn more ->" (ghost) ]
[ centered row of six grayscale logos: "Trusted by teams at" ]
[ centered eyebrow + h2 + paragraph ]
[ three equal cards ]
[ centered testimonial with avatar ]
[ centered CTA panel with gradient ]
```

The eye has no edge to follow, every block has the same weight, and the reader scrolls past a column of headlines without a reason to stop.

**The three equal cards.** `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-8`, each card with an icon in a colored square, a bold title and two lines of gray text. Real features are rarely three and rarely equal. The grid forces the copy to fit the shape: three benefits padded to equal length, or six squeezed into two rows of three.

The fix for both is the same: decide what the most important item is, give it more space, and align everything to one left edge.

#### Alignment to a shared left edge

Pick one left edge per page, or per column, and start everything there: the logo, the h1, the paragraph, the primary button, the screenshot, the section headings, the table. When a reader's eye drops from the headline, it lands on the start of the next line without searching.

```css
.page {
  --edge: max(var(--space-16), (100vw - 1200px) / 2);
  padding-inline: var(--edge);
}
```

Concrete checks:

- Draw a vertical line at the left edge of the h1. The paragraph, the buttons and the next section heading touch it.
- Icons in lists and nav hang outside the text edge, or the text column starts after the icon column consistently. Do not mix the two.
- Card text does not start 32px in from the page edge when the surrounding text starts at 0. Either the card border sits on the edge and the padding is visible as a deliberate inset, or there is no card.

#### Asymmetric grids

Split layouts unevenly. An uneven split states which side matters.

| Split (of 12) | Use |
| --- | --- |
| 4 / 8 | Section label and summary on the left, content on the right (docs, settings, feature detail) |
| 5 / 7 | Text and a screenshot, text side smaller |
| 3 / 9 | Sidebar nav and main content |
| 8 / 4 | Article and a narrow aside (metadata, table of contents) |
| 6 / 6 | Only for two things that are equivalent: before and after, two plans |

```css
.grid-12 {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr));
  column-gap: var(--space-24);
  row-gap: var(--space-48);
}
@media (min-width: 64em) { .grid-12 { column-gap: var(--space-32); } }

.span-4 { grid-column: span 4; }
.span-5 { grid-column: span 5; }
.span-7 { grid-column: span 7; }
.span-8 { grid-column: span 8; }

@media (max-width: 47.99em) {
  .grid-12 > * { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
}
```

Use `minmax(0, 1fr)`, not `1fr`. A plain `1fr` track has a minimum of `auto`, which is the min-content width of its contents, so one long URL or code line makes its column wider than its siblings and pushes the page into horizontal scroll.

A feature section rebuilt with a 4 / 8 split, replacing the three cards:

```html
<section class="grid-12 feature">
  <div class="span-4">
    <h2>Reconciliation</h2>
    <p>Matches bank lines to invoices every morning at 06:00 in your time zone.</p>
  </div>
  <dl class="span-8 facts">
    <div><dt>Match rate</dt><dd>94% of lines match without review in the first month</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Rules</dt><dd>Match on amount, reference, IBAN or a regex you write</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Exceptions</dt><dd>Unmatched lines land in a queue with the three closest invoices</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Banks</dt><dd>2,400 banks through Open Banking; CSV and CAMT.053 for the rest</dd></div>
  </dl>
</section>
```

```css
.feature h2 { font-size: var(--text-24); line-height: var(--lh-24); }
.facts { display: grid; gap: 0; }
.facts > div {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 160px minmax(0, 1fr);
  gap: var(--space-16);
  padding-block: var(--space-16);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
.facts dt { font-weight: 600; }
.facts dd { color: var(--ink-2); }
```

Four facts instead of three, uneven lengths allowed, numbers where the template had adjectives.

Other replacements for the three-card row:

- **One large, two small.** The main feature spans 8 columns with a real screenshot; two secondary features stack in the remaining 4.
- **A comparison table.** If the features differ along the same dimensions, a table is clearer than cards.
- **An annotated screenshot.** One product image with three to five numbered callouts and a list below.
- **A plain list.** Headings at 21px with one paragraph each, in a single 66ch column. Unglamorous and fast to read.

#### Content-out layout with named lines

For pages that mix prose with wider elements (docs, articles, changelogs), define the columns once with named grid lines and let each child choose its width. This replaces nested `max-w-*` containers.

```css
.content-grid {
  --gutter: var(--space-16);
  --prose: 66ch;
  --wide: 960px;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns:
    [full-start] minmax(var(--gutter), 1fr)
    [wide-start] minmax(0, calc((var(--wide) - var(--prose)) / 2))
    [content-start] min(var(--prose), 100% - var(--gutter) * 2)
    [content-end] minmax(0, calc((var(--wide) - var(--prose)) / 2))
    [wide-end] minmax(var(--gutter), 1fr)
    [full-end];
}
.content-grid > * { grid-column: content; }
.content-grid > .wide { grid-column: wide; }
.content-grid > .full { grid-column: full; }
```

```html
<article class="content-grid">
  <h1>Migrating from v2 to v3</h1>
  <p>Version 3 changes how webhooks are signed. Plan for about 30 minutes per service.</p>
  <pre class="wide"><code>...</code></pre>
  <figure class="full"><img src="/img/v3-dashboard.png" alt="..." width="2400" height="1350"></figure>
  <p>Next, rotate the signing secret.</p>
</article>
```

Prose stays at 66ch; code blocks and tables break out to 960px; screenshots can go edge to edge. Everything shares the same left edge for its width class, and no element needs its own container.

#### Sidebars

Application shells use a fixed-width sidebar and a fluid main area:

```css
.shell {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 248px minmax(0, 1fr);
  min-height: 100dvh;
}
.shell > nav {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  height: 100dvh;
  overflow-y: auto;
  border-right: 1px solid var(--rule);
  background: var(--paper-2);
  padding: var(--space-16) var(--space-12);
}
.shell > main { padding: var(--space-24) var(--space-32); }

@media (max-width: 63.99em) {
  .shell { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
  .shell > nav { position: static; height: auto; border-right: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
}
```

- Sidebar width 240 to 280px. Narrower truncates labels; wider steals table columns.
- The sidebar is separated by a 1px rule and a tonal step to `--paper-2`, never by a shadow.
- A collapsible icon-only rail (56px) is fine for products with ten or more destinations used all day. For fewer, keep labels visible.

For a sidebar that sits beside content only when there is room, without a media query, use the intrinsic pattern:

```css
.with-sidebar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-32); }
.with-sidebar > .side { flex-basis: 240px; flex-grow: 1; }
.with-sidebar > .main { flex-basis: 0; flex-grow: 999; min-inline-size: 60%; }
```

When the main area would drop below 60 percent of the container, the sidebar wraps above it.

#### Max widths

| Content | Max width |
| --- | --- |
| Prose paragraphs | 66ch |
| Headings | 20 to 24ch |
| Forms (single column) | 480 to 560px |
| Dialogs | 480px for confirmations, 640px for forms |
| Marketing page container | 1200 to 1280px |
| Docs page with sidebar and table of contents | 1440px |
| Data tables, dashboards, editors | none: use the window |

`max-w-7xl mx-auto` (1280px) around a data table on a 2560px monitor leaves half the screen blank while the table truncates its columns. Application screens fill the viewport; only their text blocks get a measure.

#### CSS grid recipes

A responsive card grid that never produces a lonely half-width card and never needs a breakpoint:

```css
.auto-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(280px, 100%), 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-24);
}
```

`auto-fill` keeps empty tracks so a row of two cards on a wide screen stays card-sized; `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks and stretches two cards across the row. Use `auto-fill` for collections of items, `auto-fit` only when the items should fill the row.

Aligned internals across cards with subgrid, so titles, bodies and footers line up row by row even when text lengths differ:

```css
.cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(280px, 100%), 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-24);
}
.card {
  display: grid;
  grid-row: span 3;
  grid-template-rows: subgrid;
  row-gap: var(--space-8);
  padding: var(--space-16);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
```

Label and value rows aligned on their text baselines (the label is 12px, the value 16px; centering them makes the label float):

```css
.stat-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: var(--space-8); }
.stat-row .value { font-size: var(--text-24); line-height: var(--lh-24); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.stat-row .label { font-size: var(--text-12); color: var(--ink-3); }
```

A page frame with header, main and footer where the footer stays at the bottom on short pages:

```css
body { min-height: 100dvh; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto; }
```

#### Container queries

A component should respond to the space it is given, not to the window. A table cell, a sidebar and a main column can all hold the same component at different widths.

```css
.invoice-summary { container-type: inline-size; container-name: summary; }

.invoice-summary .body { display: grid; gap: var(--space-12); }

@container summary (min-width: 480px) {
  .invoice-summary .body { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto; align-items: baseline; }
}
@container summary (min-width: 720px) {
  .invoice-summary .body { grid-template-columns: 200px minmax(0, 1fr) auto; }
}
```

- Put `container-type: inline-size` on a wrapper, not on the element you style; an element cannot query itself.
- Use container queries for components and media queries for page structure.
- Container query units (`cqi`) are available for sizes that scale with the container, but keep text on the type scale; do not set `font-size: 4cqi`.

#### Failure cases

```slop
<section class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-6 py-24 text-center">
  <h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Features</h2>
  <div class="mt-16 grid grid-cols-1 gap-8 md:grid-cols-3">
    <div class="rounded-2xl p-8 shadow-lg">...</div>
    <div class="rounded-2xl p-8 shadow-lg">...</div>
    <div class="rounded-2xl p-8 shadow-lg">...</div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```slop
<main class="mx-auto max-w-7xl">
  <div class="grid grid-cols-4 gap-6">
    <!-- four KPI cards, each with a big number, a green "+12.5%" pill and a sparkline -->
  </div>
</main>
```

The second is the generated dashboard: four equal KPI cards across the top whether the product has four important numbers or one. Put the one number that drives decisions at the left with more space, and move the rest into a compact row or a table.

### 3.6 Responsive behavior

#### Breakpoints come from content

Set a breakpoint where the content breaks, not where a device sits. Open the page, drag the window from 320px to 1920px, and add a breakpoint only where something fails: a line passes 75 characters, a column drops under 280px, a table starts to scroll, a nav row wraps into two lines.

The usual result is two or three breakpoints, not five. Generated code ships Tailwind's whole ladder (`sm:` 640, `md:` 768, `lg:` 1024, `xl:` 1280, `2xl:` 1536) on every element, with a different font size, padding and column count at each step, and nobody has looked at the page at 900px.

Write breakpoints in `em`, not `px`. An `em` media query scales with the reader's default font size, so someone who set 20px in the browser gets the narrow layout earlier, which is what they need.

```css
/* 48em = 768px at the default 16px; 64em = 1024px */
@media (min-width: 48em) { ... }
@media (min-width: 64em) { ... }
```

Name the breakpoints by what changes, in a comment or a custom media name, not by device:

```css
/* two-column: text column + aside fit side by side at 66ch + 280px + gaps */
@media (min-width: 64em) { .article { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 66ch) 280px; } }
```

#### Mobile-first rules

- Base styles are the narrow layout. `min-width` queries add columns and space as the window grows. A page built desktop-first with `max-width` overrides collects contradictory rules for every component.
- The page works at 320 CSS pixels wide with no horizontal page scroll. That is the WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow) target, and it is also what 1280px looks like at 400 percent zoom. Only data tables, code blocks and maps may scroll sideways, inside their own container.
- Body text stays at 16px on phones. Do not shrink it to fit more; reflow instead.
- Inputs are at least 16px. iOS Safari zooms the page when focusing an input with a smaller font size, then leaves the reader zoomed in.
- Gutters are 16px at the narrow end and grow to 24px or 32px. Never 0.
- Use `100dvh` for full-height layouts. `100vh` on mobile browsers is the height with the toolbars hidden, so a `h-screen` hero hides its bottom 60 to 100px behind the address bar.
- For layouts that reach the screen edges on notched phones, add `viewport-fit=cover` and pad with safe-area insets.

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
```

```css
.app-header { padding-inline: max(var(--space-16), env(safe-area-inset-left)) max(var(--space-16), env(safe-area-inset-right)); }
.bottom-bar { padding-bottom: max(var(--space-8), env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }
```

Never set `maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no` in the viewport tag. It blocks pinch zoom for readers who need it.

#### Touch targets

| Standard | Minimum |
| --- | --- |
| WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA | 24 by 24 CSS px, or enough spacing that a 24px circle around it touches no other target |
| WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size, level AAA | 44 by 44 CSS px |
| Apple Human Interface Guidelines | 44 by 44 pt |
| Material Design | 48 by 48 dp |

The rule in this handbook: every interactive element is at least 44 by 44px on touch devices and at least 24 by 24px everywhere. The visible element can be smaller than the hit area. A 20px icon button gets 12px of padding; a dense table row link gets an enlarged hit area with a pseudo-element.

```css
.icon-button {
  display: inline-grid;
  place-items: center;
  min-width: 44px;
  min-height: 44px;
  padding: 12px;
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--ink-2);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
}
@media (pointer: fine) {
  .icon-button { min-width: 32px; min-height: 32px; padding: 6px; }
}

/* Extend the hit area of a small link without changing the layout */
.row-link { position: relative; }
.row-link::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -10px -4px; }
```

The 6px padding in the fine-pointer rule is the one place a non-scale value is allowed: it centers a 20px icon in a 32px box. Keep it inside the component.

Adjacent targets need space between them, 8px at least. Two 44px buttons touching edge to edge cause mis-taps at the shared border.

#### Hover is optional

Touch screens have no hover. Anything revealed only on hover (row actions, card buttons, tooltips holding the only label) is invisible to a phone user and to keyboard users unless focus reveals it too.

```css
.row-actions { opacity: 1; }
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .row .row-actions { opacity: 0; }
  .row:hover .row-actions,
  .row:focus-within .row-actions { opacity: 1; }
}
```

Hide on hover-capable devices only, and always reveal on `:focus-within`.

#### Tables on small screens

A data table is the hardest element to make responsive, and the generated answer (turn every row into a card below 768px) is usually wrong: it destroys comparison down a column, which is the reason the data was in a table.

Choose by the number of columns and the task:

1. **Two to four columns, short values.** The table fits at 320px. Reduce cell padding to `4px 8px` and the text to 14px. Done.
2. **Five or more columns, comparison matters.** Keep the table, scroll it horizontally inside its own container, and stick the first column so each row keeps its label.
3. **Many columns, each row read alone (a contacts list, an orders list).** Show two or three priority columns and link each row to a detail view. A column picker lets the reader choose which columns stay.
4. **Key-value records.** Render as a definition list on narrow screens. This is the only case where the card reflow is right.

```html
<div class="table-scroll" role="region" aria-labelledby="orders-cap" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-cap">Orders, last 30 days</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Order</th><th scope="col">Customer</th><th scope="col" class="num">Total</th>
          <th scope="col">Status</th><th scope="col">Placed</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th scope="row">#10482</th><td>Halvorsen AS</td><td class="num">1,240.00</td>
          <td>Shipped</td><td><time datetime="2026-03-12">12 Mar</time></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

```css
.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%; border: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.table-scroll:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.table-scroll table { border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0; min-width: 640px; width: 100%; }
.table-scroll :where(th, td) { padding: var(--cell-py) var(--cell-px); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); white-space: nowrap; }
.table-scroll thead th { background: var(--paper-2); text-align: left; }
.table-scroll tbody th[scope="row"],
.table-scroll thead th:first-child {
  position: sticky;
  left: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  border-right: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
.table-scroll thead th:first-child { background: var(--paper-2); z-index: 1; }
```

The `tabindex="0"`, the `role="region"` and the label make the scroll container reachable and announced for keyboard users, who otherwise cannot scroll it. The sticky first column needs an opaque background or the scrolled cells show through. The separator is a 1px rule, not a fading edge.

#### Navigation collapse without hamburger theater

The generated mobile nav: a hamburger icon that morphs into an X with a 300ms rotation, a full-height drawer that slides in from the right over a blurred backdrop, and links that fade in one by one with a 50ms stagger. Each step delays the reader by animation time and adds code that breaks focus management.

Rules:

- **Five or fewer top-level links: do not collapse.** Let them wrap onto a second row, or scroll the row horizontally with the current item scrolled into view. Most marketing sites have four links plus a sign-in.
- **App with three to five primary destinations: use a bottom bar** on phones, with icon plus text label for each item, 56px tall plus the safe-area inset.
- **More than that: one disclosure button labeled "Menu"** (a text label; a three-line icon is optional next to it), which opens a plain list directly below the header and pushes the page down. No overlay, no drawer, no stagger, no blur.
- The button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.
- The open and close transition is 0 to 150ms, opacity only, or none.

```html
<header class="site-header">
  <a href="/" class="wordmark">Ledgerline</a>
  <button class="menu-button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="site-nav">Menu</button>
  <nav id="site-nav" class="site-nav" aria-label="Main">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="/product">Product</a></li>
      <li><a href="/pricing">Pricing</a></li>
      <li><a href="/docs">Docs</a></li>
      <li><a href="/changelog">Changelog</a></li>
      <li><a href="/login">Sign in</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</header>
```

```css
.site-header { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-16); padding: var(--space-12) var(--space-16); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.menu-button { margin-left: auto; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 var(--space-12); border: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--paper); border-radius: var(--radius); font: inherit; }
.site-nav { flex-basis: 100%; }
.site-nav[data-open="false"] { display: none; }
.site-nav ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
.site-nav a { display: block; padding: var(--space-12) 0; min-height: 44px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); text-decoration: none; }

@media (min-width: 48em) {
  .menu-button { display: none; }
  .site-nav, .site-nav[data-open="false"] { display: block; flex-basis: auto; margin-left: auto; }
  .site-nav ul { display: flex; gap: var(--space-24); }
  .site-nav a { border-top: 0; padding: var(--space-8) 0; }
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

export function useMenu() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return;
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === "Escape") { setOpen(false); buttonRef.current?.focus(); }
    };
    document.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
    return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
  }, [open]);
  return {
    buttonProps: { ref: buttonRef, "aria-expanded": open, onClick: () => setOpen(o => !o) },
    navProps: { "data-open": String(open) },
  };
}
```

Without JavaScript the nav should still be reachable. Either render it open by default and let the script hide it, or use a `<details>` element as the disclosure.

#### Images and media across sizes

- Every `<img>` has `width` and `height` attributes. The browser reserves the box before the file arrives.
- `max-width: 100%; height: auto;` on all images globally.
- Serve sizes with `srcset` and `sizes` so a phone does not download a 2400px screenshot (details in 3.8).
- Videos and embeds use `aspect-ratio` on a wrapper instead of the padding-top hack.

#### Failure cases

```slop
<h1 class="text-4xl sm:text-5xl md:text-6xl lg:text-7xl xl:text-8xl">...</h1>
<div class="px-4 sm:px-6 md:px-8 lg:px-12 xl:px-16 2xl:px-24">...</div>
<div class="hidden md:block">Important pricing details</div>
```

Five font sizes and six paddings nobody reviewed, and content that exists only on desktop. If something is important on desktop, it is important on a phone; reflow it instead of hiding it.

### 3.7 Icons

#### One set, configured once

Use one SVG icon set across the product. Mixing sets is visible even to people who cannot name the cause: stroke weights, corner radii, end caps and optical sizes all differ.

Sets that work at the canonical spec (stroke 1.5px, 16 or 20px):

- **Lucide**: 24px grid, default stroke 2. Set `strokeWidth={1.5}` and `absoluteStrokeWidth` so the rendered stroke stays 1.5px when scaled down to 16 or 20px.
- **Heroicons outline**: 24px grid, stroke 1.5. There is also a 20px solid and 16px micro set; do not mix outline and solid in one interface except for selected states.
- **Phosphor**, regular weight: 256 unit grid; the regular weight renders close to 1.5px at 20px.
- **Tabler Icons**: 24px grid, default stroke 2; set the stroke to 1.5.
- **IBM Carbon icons**: drawn natively at 16, 20, 24 and 32px, solid shapes rather than strokes. Pair with Plex. If you choose Carbon, the stroke rule becomes "use the 16 and 20 masters".

Wrap the set in one component so size and stroke are decided in one place:

```tsx
import type { LucideIcon } from "lucide-react";

type Props = { icon: LucideIcon; size?: 16 | 20; label?: string };

export function Icon({ icon: Glyph, size = 16, label }: Props) {
  return (
    <Glyph
      width={size}
      height={size}
      strokeWidth={1.5}
      absoluteStrokeWidth
      aria-hidden={label ? undefined : true}
      aria-label={label}
      role={label ? "img" : undefined}
      focusable="false"
      className="icon"
    />
  );
}
```

Without a framework, use a sprite file and reference symbols:

```html
<svg class="icon" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
  <use href="/icons.svg#download"></use>
</svg>
```

```css
.icon {
  width: 16px;
  height: 16px;
  flex: none;
  stroke: currentColor;
  stroke-width: 1.5;
  fill: none;
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
}
.icon path, .icon circle, .icon line, .icon rect { vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; }
.icon--20 { width: 20px; height: 20px; }
```

`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` keeps the stroke at 1.5 screen pixels regardless of the viewBox scale, which is what `absoluteStrokeWidth` does in Lucide.

#### Sizes

| Icon | Next to text at | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16px | 12 to 16px | Inline in text, buttons at 14 to 16px, table cells, menu items, form field adornments |
| 20px | 16 to 21px | Toolbar and icon-only buttons, sidebar nav, page header actions, empty states |

Two sizes. Never 24px icons beside 14px labels, never 32px or 48px decorative icons in a feature grid. An empty state that needs a picture needs a screenshot or nothing, not a 64px icon.

Color comes from `currentColor`. Icons take the text color of their context: `--ink-2` in toolbars and nav, `--ink` when active, the semantic color only when the icon carries status beside a text label.

#### Alignment with text

Inside a button, nav item or menu row, use flex and center the icon on the text line:

```css
.button, .nav-item, .menu-item {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-8);
}
```

Inline in a sentence, the icon must sit on the text, not float above the baseline. A 1em icon with a small negative vertical offset lines up with lowercase and capital letters in most faces:

```css
.inline-icon { width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.125em; }
```

For pixel accuracy against the cap height, browsers that support the `cap` unit can center on it:

```css
@supports (height: 1cap) {
  .inline-icon { vertical-align: calc((1cap - 1em) / 2); }
}
```

Check alignment visually at 200 percent zoom. Most icon sets put the drawing in a 24 unit box with 2 units of padding, so an icon that looks one pixel too high usually is.

In lists with leading icons, align text lines to each other, not to the icon. Give the icon a fixed column and let wrapped lines start under the first word:

```css
.icon-list li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16px minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: var(--space-8); align-items: start; }
.icon-list .icon { margin-top: 4px; } /* (24px line - 16px icon) / 2 */
```

#### Accessible names

- **Decorative icon next to a text label**: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. The text is the name. Without `aria-hidden`, some screen readers announce "image" or read the SVG's title, doubling the label.
- **Icon-only button**: the button gets the name, the icon stays hidden. Add a visible tooltip on hover and focus with the same text.
- **Standalone meaningful icon** (a status icon in a table cell with no text): `role="img"` and `aria-label`, or a `<title>` as the first child of the SVG. Better: add the text.

```html
<button type="button" class="icon-button" aria-label="Download CSV">
  <svg class="icon icon--20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><use href="/icons.svg#download"></use></svg>
</button>
```

Icon-only buttons are acceptable for close, search, more-actions, and toolbar actions that also have a keyboard shortcut and a tooltip. Everything else gets a text label. A row of five unlabeled icons in a toolbar is a guessing game.

#### Never emoji

Emoji are banned as icons, bullets, heading decorations, status indicators, button labels, empty-state art, toast prefixes and commit message prefixes. Reasons that hold in every one of those places:

- Emoji render from the operating system's color font. The same code point looks different on iOS, Android, Windows and Linux, and you cannot style it to match your tokens.
- They ignore `currentColor`, dark mode and forced-colors mode.
- Screen readers announce their names: a heading `:rocket: Getting started` is read as "rocket, Getting started".
- They are the fastest way to make a README, a changelog or a UI look generated, because language models add them by default to headings and lists.

```slop
## :sparkles: Features
## :rocket: Getting Started
## :hammer_and_wrench: Tech Stack

Status: :green_circle: Online   :red_circle: Down

git commit -m ":sparkles: feat: add export"
git commit -m ":bug: fix login redirect"
```

```text
## Features
## Getting started
## Stack

git commit -m "Add CSV export to the invoices list"
git commit -m "Fix login redirect when the session cookie is expired"
```

Commit messages are plain text: an imperative summary under 72 characters, optionally a conventional prefix (`fix:`, `feat:`) if the repository uses one, and a body that says why. No Gitmoji, no shortcodes.

Status uses text plus a shape plus color, so it survives grayscale, color vision deficiency and screen readers:

```html
<span class="status status--bad">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><use href="/icons.svg#x-circle"></use></svg>
  Failed
</span>
<span class="status status--ok">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><use href="/icons.svg#check-circle"></use></svg>
  Running since 09:12
</span>
```

```css
.status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-4); font-size: var(--text-14); }
.status--ok  { color: var(--ok); }
.status--bad { color: var(--bad); }
```

No pulsing green dot. The "LIVE" or "Online" pill with an `animate-ping` dot is banned; it animates forever, carries no information beyond its text, and is a stock element of generated dashboards. "Running since 09:12" says more and does not move.

#### No icon in every heading

Generated docs and landing pages put an icon before every h2 and h3: a book for "Documentation", a shield for "Security", a gear for "Settings". The icon repeats the word next to it and pushes the heading text off the shared left edge. Headings are text. Use icons where they help recognition at speed: navigation, toolbars, file types, status.

#### No icons in colored circles or rounded squares

The feature-grid tell, copied from the Tailwind UI feature sections:

```slop
<div class="flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-indigo-600">
  <BoltIcon class="h-6 w-6 text-white" aria-hidden="true" />
</div>
<h3 class="mt-4 text-lg font-semibold">Lightning fast</h3>
```

```slop
<div class="mx-auto flex size-16 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-gradient-to-br from-purple-500 to-pink-500">
  <SparklesIcon class="size-8 text-white" />
</div>
```

A tinted container gives a generic glyph the visual weight of a logo, it is the same 48px square on every feature page on the web, and it says nothing about the feature. Drop the container and usually the icon too. If the item needs an anchor, use a number, a short label or a cropped screenshot of the feature itself:

```html
<li class="feature-item">
  <h3>Bank matching</h3>
  <p>Lines match on amount and reference. Unmatched lines wait in a review queue.</p>
  <img src="/img/review-queue-crop.png" alt="Review queue with three unmatched bank lines" width="640" height="320">
</li>
```

Same for avatars of icons in lists (an icon inside a 40px gray circle at the start of every notification row) and for "trust" rows (a shield in a circle, a lock in a circle, a globe in a circle). If a row needs a leading visual, the real one is better: the sender's avatar, the file type, the integration's logo at its own colors.

### 3.8 Images and illustration

#### Real images over generic art

Show the product. A real screenshot with real-looking data proves the product exists and shows what it does. The common substitutes each signal that nothing real was available:

- **3D blobs and glossy shapes**: iridescent spheres, chrome torus knots, floating glass cubes. Spline and Blender stock packs made these the default hero art for AI products.
- **Isometric illustrations**: a person on a giant laptop next to a floating chart. unDraw, Storyset, Humaaans and the "corporate Memphis" style (flat figures with tiny heads and long purple limbs) are recognized as free stock instantly.
- **AI-generated images**: plastic skin, symmetrical faces, six-fingered hands, glowing brains, robot hands touching human hands, neon circuit boards, abstract "neural network" meshes. Readers spot them, and some read them as a sign the rest of the content was generated too. Do not use them for people, products or places.
- **Background glows**: a blurred purple circle behind the hero (`absolute -top-40 h-96 w-96 rounded-full bg-purple-500 opacity-30 blur-3xl`). Decoration with no content.
- **Fake dashboards**: a screenshot built in Figma with round-number data, perfect upward lines and "John Doe" users. Readers notice that 12,345 and +23.5% repeat across every card.

```slop
<div class="relative">
  <div class="absolute -top-24 left-1/2 h-96 w-96 -translate-x-1/2 rounded-full bg-violet-500/30 blur-3xl"></div>
  <img src="/hero-3d-blob.png" class="animate-float" alt="">
</div>
```

#### Screenshots

- Capture at 2x device pixel ratio and serve 1x and 2x.
- Use realistic data: plausible names from several cultures, uneven numbers (1,284.17 not 1,000.00), a few empty cells, one error row if the product shows errors. Never "Lorem ipsum", never "John Doe", never "Acme Inc" in every row.
- Crop to the part that proves the claim. A full app window shrunk to 40 percent makes 14px text render at under 6px. Crop a region and show it at 100 percent or 75 percent.
- Match the theme: a light page shows light screenshots. If the site supports dark mode, provide both.
- Remove personal data, real email addresses and internal URLs.
- Update screenshots when the UI changes. A screenshot of the old navigation on the pricing page is a support ticket generator.

Frame a screenshot with a 1px border and the canonical radius. No shadow, no tilt, no fake browser chrome:

```css
.shot {
  display: block;
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--paper-2); /* shows while loading */
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

```slop
<div class="rounded-xl bg-gray-900/5 p-2 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-900/10 lg:-m-4 lg:rounded-2xl lg:p-4">
  <img src="/app-screenshot.png" class="rounded-md shadow-2xl ring-1 ring-gray-900/10" />
</div>
```

```slop
<div style="transform: perspective(2000px) rotateX(12deg) rotateY(-18deg) rotateZ(4deg)">
  <img src="/iphone-mockup.png" class="drop-shadow-2xl">
</div>
```

The first is the Tailwind UI screenshot frame: a ring, a padded tinted wrapper and `shadow-2xl`. The second is the floating device at an angle, which turns the product into a prop and makes every word in it unreadable. Show the screen flat.

Do not draw browser chrome (three colored circles and a fake address bar) around screenshots. It adds 40px of decoration and claims the product is a website, which the reader already knows. If the URL matters, put it in the caption.

#### Aspect ratios and sizing

Give every image box a ratio before the file loads, to prevent layout shift and to keep a grid of images even.

| Content | Ratio |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop app screenshot | 16:10 or the real window ratio |
| Cropped UI detail | whatever the crop is; set width and height attributes to match |
| Photos in articles | 3:2 |
| Hero photo, wide | 21:9 at most |
| Avatars, logos in a grid | 1:1 |
| Video | 16:9 |

```css
img, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
.ratio-16-10 { aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; width: 100%; object-fit: cover; }
.avatar { aspect-ratio: 1; width: 32px; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; }
```

`border-radius: 50%` on avatars is the one exception to the 4px radius ceiling: a circle is a shape, not a rounded corner.

Responsive sources, so a phone gets a phone-sized file:

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/avif"
          srcset="/img/review-640.avif 640w, /img/review-1280.avif 1280w, /img/review-2400.avif 2400w"
          sizes="(min-width: 64em) 960px, 100vw">
  <img src="/img/review-1280.png"
       srcset="/img/review-640.png 640w, /img/review-1280.png 1280w, /img/review-2400.png 2400w"
       sizes="(min-width: 64em) 960px, 100vw"
       width="2400" height="1500"
       alt="Review queue listing three unmatched bank lines, each with suggested invoices"
       class="shot" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
</picture>
```

- The largest image above the fold (usually the hero screenshot) gets `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"`.
- Everything below the fold gets `loading="lazy"`.
- AVIF first, WebP or PNG fallback. PNG for screenshots with text if AVIF artifacts blur small type; check at 100 percent.

Light and dark screenshots, when the theme follows the system:

```html
<picture>
  <source srcset="/img/editor-dark.png" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">
  <img src="/img/editor-light.png" width="1600" height="1000" alt="Editor with the outline panel open" class="shot">
</picture>
```

When the theme is a manual toggle (`data-theme`), media queries cannot see it. Render both images and hide one with `:root[data-theme="dark"] .only-light { display: none; }`.

#### Captions and alt text

Use `<figure>` and `<figcaption>` when the image needs context. The caption says what the reader is looking at and why it matters, in one or two sentences, left-aligned, 14px, `--ink-2`, 8px below the image.

```html
<figure class="figure">
  <img src="/img/approvals.png" width="1600" height="900" class="shot"
       alt="Approval panel showing a 4,200 euro purchase request with the remaining Q3 budget of 18,350 euros">
  <figcaption>Approvers see the remaining budget before they approve. Requests over the budget need a second approver.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

```css
.figure { margin: 0; }
.figure figcaption { margin-top: var(--space-8); font-size: var(--text-14); line-height: var(--lh-14); color: var(--ink-2); max-width: 66ch; }
```

Alt text describes what the image shows that the surrounding text needs: the numbers, the state, the action. Not "screenshot of our app" and not "image". Decorative images take `alt=""`. If an image is purely decorative, ask whether it should exist.

#### When illustration is right

Draw an illustration when it explains something a screenshot cannot: a data flow between systems, a sequence of states, a physical setup. Rules:

- Diagrams, not scenes. Boxes, lines, labels in the product's type, drawn in `--ink`, `--ink-2` and at most one accent.
- 1.5px strokes to match the icons, no fills beyond `--paper-2`, no gradients, no glow, no perspective.
- Real labels with real names (`orders-db`, `webhook worker`), not "Data" and "Cloud".
- Inline SVG with `currentColor` so the diagram follows the theme.
- One illustration style per product. If a team cannot commission one, use diagrams and screenshots only.

Photos of people: only real people who work on or use the product, with permission and names. A stock photo of a smiling team at a laptop on an "About" page says the opposite of what it intends.

Testimonials: real name, real role, real company, a real photo or initials. No stock headshots, no five-star rows, no generated portraits.

### 3.9 Motion

#### The budget

Every transition lasts 0 to 150ms, eases out, and animates only `opacity` and `transform`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, nothing moves at all.

| Interaction | Duration | Property |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button press, checkbox, toggle | 0ms | state change is instant |
| Hover color or underline change | 0 to 100ms | `color`, `background-color` (paint only, no layout) |
| Menu, popover, tooltip open | 100 to 150ms | `opacity`, `transform: translateY(4px)` to 0 |
| Menu, popover, tooltip close | 0 to 100ms | `opacity` |
| Toast enter | 150ms | `opacity`, `transform: translateY(8px)` to 0 |
| Disclosure caret | 100ms | `transform: rotate()` |
| Dialog open | 0 to 150ms | `opacity` |

Hover color changes are listed because they are paint-only and cheap; the "opacity and transform only" rule covers anything that moves.

```css
:root {
  --dur-0: 0ms;
  --dur-1: 100ms;
  --dur-2: 150ms;
  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
}

.popover {
  transition: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out);
}
.popover[data-state="closed"] { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); pointer-events: none; }
.popover[data-state="open"]   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }

a, .button { transition: color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out); }
```

Name the properties. `transition-all duration-300` (the Tailwind snippet in most generated components) animates every property that changes, including `height`, `padding` and `border-width`, which forces layout on every frame, and 300ms is twice the budget. Interfaces that respond in under 100ms read as direct; at 300ms the reader waits for the UI.

#### What may move

Motion is allowed when it tells the reader where something came from or that something is happening:

- A menu or popover appears near its trigger.
- A toast enters at the edge where it will stay.
- A caret rotates when a section expands.
- A progress bar fills, a spinner turns during a wait over 1 second. Show the spinner only after 400ms so fast requests never flash it, and pair it with text (`Saving…`).
- A row that was just added is marked with a static `--paper-3` background that clears after a few seconds. No pulsing.

Skeleton screens use static `--paper-2` blocks the shape of the content. The shimmering skeleton is an animated gradient and is banned twice over.

#### What never moves

```slop
<section data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="200">...</section>
<motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 40 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} transition={{ duration: 0.8 }}>
<div class="animate-bounce">Scroll down</div>
<img class="animate-float" src="/blob.png">
<div class="bg-[length:200%_200%] animate-gradient bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500">
<h1><Typewriter words={["faster", "smarter", "better"]} loop cursor /></h1>
<span class="absolute inline-flex h-full w-full animate-ping rounded-full bg-green-400 opacity-75"></span>
<div class="transition-transform duration-300 hover:scale-105">...</div>
```

- **Fade-up on scroll for every section** (AOS, Framer Motion `whileInView`, GSAP ScrollTrigger). Content is invisible until the script runs and the element enters the viewport. If the script fails, or a print, reader view or screenshot tool renders the page, the sections stay blank. Readers who scroll fast see empty space. This is the most common generated-page motion.
- **Floating** (`animate-bounce`, custom `float` keyframes that bob an image up and down). Endless motion in the reader's peripheral vision while they try to read.
- **Parallax**. Background and foreground scrolling at different speeds is a documented trigger for vestibular disorders, and it costs scroll performance on low-end phones.
- **Animated gradients**, moving glows, cursor-following spotlights on cards, shimmering borders, rotating conic borders.
- **Typing-effect headlines.** The headline is the one sentence that must be readable at once; a typewriter delays it and screen readers may announce partial words.
- **Confetti** (`canvas-confetti`) after sign-up or payment. A success message is text.
- **Count-up numbers** that roll from 0 to the value. The reader waits to read a number that was known at render.
- **Infinite logo marquees.** A moving row of customer logos cannot be read and cannot be paused without extra controls (WCAG 2.2.2 requires a pause for motion over 5 seconds).
- **Hover scale and tilt on cards** (`hover:scale-105`, 3D tilt libraries). The card is not more clickable for growing.
- **Pulsing status dots** (`animate-ping`). See 3.7.
- **Page transitions** over 150ms. If you use the View Transitions API, set the duration to 150ms or less and disable it under reduced motion.

#### Reduced motion

Respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` globally, then again in JavaScript for anything scripted.

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }
}
```

The duration is 0.01ms rather than 0 so that code listening for `transitionend` and `animationend` still receives the event; to the eye it is instant.

```ts
const reduce = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");
export const motionOK = () => !reduce.matches;

el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: motionOK() ? "smooth" : "auto", block: "nearest" });
```

```tsx
import { MotionConfig } from "framer-motion";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" transition={{ duration: 0.15, ease: [0.2, 0, 0, 1] }}>
      {children}
    </MotionConfig>
  );
}
```

In Tailwind, put motion behind the `motion-safe:` variant: `motion-safe:transition-opacity motion-safe:duration-150`. Spinners under reduced motion become static text: `Loading…`.

### 3.10 Accessibility as design quality

Accessibility is part of the visual spec. A focus ring, a contrast ratio and a target size are design values with numbers, and generated UIs fail them in the same places every time.

#### Focus rings

```css
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }

/* Inside a container that clips overflow, draw the ring inward */
.table-scroll :focus-visible, .tabs :focus-visible { outline-offset: -2px; }
```

- `--focus` is `--ink` in light mode and the light ink in dark mode: 16:1 against `--paper`, far past the 3:1 minimum for focus indicators.
- Never remove the outline without replacing it. `focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:ring-offset-2`, the Tailwind default pattern, draws the ring with `box-shadow`, and forced-colors mode (Windows contrast themes) sets `box-shadow` to none. The ring vanishes for exactly the people who need it most. `outline` survives.
- With the 2px offset, the ring sits on `--paper` even around an accent button, so one ring style works on every control.
- Every interactive element shows the ring: links, buttons, inputs, tabs, table rows that open, scroll containers with `tabindex="0"`.

#### Contrast

| Pair | Ratio | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ink` on `--paper` | 16.0:1 | body text |
| `--ink-2` on `--paper` | 8.4:1 | secondary text |
| `--ink-3` on `--paper` | 4.8:1 | metadata, placeholders; passes 4.5:1 |
| `--ink-3` on `--paper-2` | 4.4:1 | fails for small text: use `--ink-2` in table headers and code captions |
| `--accent` on `--paper` | 5.1:1 | accent text and links |
| `--accent-ink` on `--accent` | 5.5:1 | primary button label |
| `--rule` on `--paper` | 1.3:1 | decoration only |
| Tailwind `gray-400` on white | 2.5:1 | the generated placeholder color; fails |

Ratios use the WCAG 2 formula. Requirements: 4.5:1 for text under 24px (or under 18.66px bold), 3:1 for larger text, and 3:1 for the boundaries of controls and for focus indicators (WCAG 1.4.11).

The `--rule` line matters here. A text input whose only boundary is a 1px `--rule` border at 1.3:1 does not show where to type. Inputs, checkboxes, radios and select boxes use `--ink-3` for their border (4.8:1); `--rule` is for dividers between content.

```css
input, select, textarea { border: 1px solid var(--ink-3); background: var(--paper); border-radius: var(--radius); }
input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-3); opacity: 1; }
```

Firefox lowers placeholder opacity by default; `opacity: 1` keeps the measured ratio. Placeholders are hints, never labels.

#### Semantics

The visual layer sits on top of correct HTML. Generated components regularly ship `<div onClick>` buttons, headings chosen by size, and inputs without labels.

- Actions are `<button type="button">`; navigation is `<a href>`. A div with a click handler has no keyboard access, no role and no focus.
- One `h1` per page; heading levels do not skip. Pick the level by outline, the size by class (3.2).
- Landmarks: `header`, `nav` (with `aria-label` when there are several), `main` (one), `footer`.
- Every input has a visible `<label for>`. Help and error text connect through `aria-describedby`.
- Data tables use `<th scope>` and a `<caption>`.
- Async status messages ("Saved", "3 results") go in an `aria-live="polite"` region that exists before the message arrives.
- The `html` element carries the right `lang`.
- Color never carries meaning alone: errors have text and an icon, chart series have labels, required fields say "required".

```html
<div class="field">
  <label for="iban">IBAN</label>
  <input id="iban" name="iban" autocomplete="off" aria-describedby="iban-help iban-err" aria-invalid="true">
  <p id="iban-help" class="help">Starts with a two-letter country code.</p>
  <p id="iban-err" class="error">This IBAN has 21 characters; German IBANs have 22.</p>
</div>
<p class="sr-only" aria-live="polite" id="save-status"></p>
```

#### Skip link and visually hidden text

```html
<body>
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
  <header>...</header>
  <main id="main" tabindex="-1">...</main>
</body>
```

```css
.skip-link {
  position: absolute;
  left: var(--space-8);
  top: var(--space-8);
  padding: var(--space-8) var(--space-12);
  background: var(--ink);
  color: var(--paper);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  transform: translateY(-200%);
}
.skip-link:focus-visible { transform: none; }

.sr-only {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px; height: 1px;
  margin: -1px; padding: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border: 0;
}
```

#### Forced colors, zoom and text spacing

- Because depth in this system comes from borders, components keep their shape in forced-colors mode, where backgrounds and shadows are replaced. Check for borders set to `transparent`: they render in the system color, which is usually what you want for buttons.
- Use system colors for custom indicators in forced colors:

```css
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .status svg { color: CanvasText; }
  .tab[aria-selected="true"] { outline: 2px solid Highlight; }
}
```

- The page must work at 200 percent zoom and with WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing (line height 1.5, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em). Never set fixed heights on boxes that hold text; use `min-height`.

#### Targets and reduced motion

Target sizes are in 3.6 (44px touch, 24px minimum). Reduced motion is in 3.9. Both are accessibility rules and design rules at once, and both are tested in review with numbers, not impressions.

### 3.11 Review checklist for Part 3

Run this before merging any UI change. Each line is a yes or no.

Type:

- [ ] One sans family, at most one serif for long-form, one mono. All through `--font-sans`, `--font-serif`, `--font-mono`.
- [ ] At most five font files, at most two preloaded, all self-hosted WOFF2 with a metric-matched fallback.
- [ ] Weights are 400 and 600 (500 only in dense apps). No 300 and below, no 700 and above.
- [ ] Every font size is on the scale: 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 32, 40, 56. Body is 16.
- [ ] Body line height 1.5; headings 1.15 to 1.25; all line heights on the 4px grid.
- [ ] Negative letter spacing only at 32px and above, never past -0.02em. Uppercase only on 12px labels.
- [ ] Prose at most 66ch wide. Headings balanced.
- [ ] Landing h1 at most 56px and a real sentence about the product.
- [ ] Tabular numerals in tables and changing numbers; numeric columns right-aligned.

Text:

- [ ] No centered paragraphs. No gradient text. No accent-colored words in headings.
- [ ] Curly quotes, the ellipsis character, non-breaking spaces before units, unambiguous dates in `<time>`.
- [ ] Links in text are underlined.
- [ ] No emoji anywhere: bullets, headings, status, buttons, toasts, commit messages.

Space and layout:

- [ ] Every spacing value is one of 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. No arbitrary values.
- [ ] Inner space is smaller than outer space on every screen. Labels sit closer to their own fields.
- [ ] Section spacing varies with the relationship between sections; not `py-24` everywhere.
- [ ] No nested cards. Grouping is done with space and 1px rules first.
- [ ] One shared left edge per column. No centered section headings over left-aligned content.
- [ ] No row of three equal icon cards. Splits are uneven where importance is uneven.
- [ ] Grid tracks use `minmax(0, 1fr)`. Data screens use the full window width.

Responsive:

- [ ] Works at 320px with no horizontal page scroll. Breakpoints in em, two or three of them.
- [ ] Touch targets 44px; nothing under 24px anywhere.
- [ ] Tables keep their columns and scroll in a labeled, focusable container.
- [ ] Nav with five or fewer links is not collapsed; larger navs use a plain disclosure.

Icons and images:

- [ ] One icon set, stroke 1.5px, 16 or 20px, `currentColor`, `aria-hidden` when beside text.
- [ ] No icons in colored circles or squares. No icon before every heading.
- [ ] Real screenshots with realistic data, 1px border, no shadow, no tilt, no fake browser chrome.
- [ ] No 3D blobs, isometric stock, AI-generated images or background glows.
- [ ] Every image has width, height and useful alt text.

Motion and access:

- [ ] Every transition is 150ms or less, names its properties, and animates only opacity and transform.
- [ ] No scroll-triggered reveals, floating, parallax, typing effects, confetti, count-ups, marquees or pulsing dots.
- [ ] Reduced motion stops everything.
- [ ] Focus ring is the canonical outline on every interactive element.
- [ ] Text contrast at least 4.5:1; control borders at least 3:1.
- [ ] Real buttons, real links, labeled inputs, one `main`, a skip link.

A quick search catches most violations in a Tailwind codebase:

```bash
rg -n --glob '*.{tsx,jsx,html,vue,svelte}' \
  -e 'text-(5xl|6xl|7xl|8xl|9xl)' -e 'font-(light|extrabold|black)' \
  -e 'tracking-tight' -e 'bg-clip-text' -e '\bshadow' \
  -e 'animate-(bounce|ping|pulse)' -e 'whileInView' -e 'data-aos' \
  -e 'duration-(300|500|700|1000)' -e 'transition-all' \
  -e '\[[0-9]+px\]' -e 'rounded-(xl|2xl|3xl)' -e 'focus:outline-none'
```

Each hit is a question for the author, not an automatic fix. Most will be replaced by a token from this Part.

## Part 4. Components, A to M

25 components in alphabetical order. Each chapter has six sections: what the machine produces, rules, a reference build, states, copy, and a checklist.

Reference builds assume the canonical tokens on `:root`, `box-sizing: border-box`, and 16px body text at 1.5 line height. None use shadows, gradients or blur. Depth comes from 1px `var(--rule)` borders and the paper steps: `--paper` for the page, `--paper-2` for recessed surfaces, `--paper-3` for pressed and selected ones.

### 4.1 Accordions

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="space-y-4">
  {faqs.map((faq) => (
    <div key={faq.q} className="rounded-2xl border border-gray-200 bg-white shadow-sm transition-all duration-300 hover:shadow-md">
      <button onClick={() => setOpen(open === faq.q ? null : faq.q)} className="flex w-full items-center justify-between px-6 py-5 text-left">
        <span className="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900">{faq.q}</span>
        <div className="flex h-8 w-8 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-indigo-50">
          <ChevronDown className={`h-5 w-5 text-indigo-600 transition-transform duration-300 ${open === faq.q ? "rotate-180" : ""}`} />
        </div>
      </button>
      {open === faq.q && <div className="px-6 pb-5 text-gray-600">{faq.a}</div>}
    </div>
  ))}
</div>
```

This is the landing-page FAQ from every Tailwind starter: each question is its own floating `rounded-2xl` card, the chevron sits in an `indigo-50` circle, and `transition-all duration-300` animates every property for twice the time the eye needs. The `<button>` has no `aria-expanded`, the panel has no id, and the state forces one item open at a time, so a reader cannot compare two answers.

#### Rules

1. Use `<details>` and `<summary>`. They give keyboard support, the expanded state and find-in-page for free. Reach for a scripted button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` only when the panel content loads on demand.
2. Items are rows in one list, separated by a 1px `var(--rule)` line. No gap between items, no box around each item.
3. The summary row is at least 44px tall: 12px vertical padding, 16px text at weight 500.
4. The indicator is a 16px chevron or a plus and minus drawn in 1.5px strokes, placed before the label. No circle or tile behind it. It turns 90 degrees in 120ms `ease-out`, and not at all under reduced motion.
5. Allow several items open at once. If a design does need one open at a time, use the `name` attribute on each `<details>` (supported in Chromium 120, Safari 17.2 and Firefox 130) instead of state code.
6. Panel text runs to 66ch at most, indented 20px to line up with the label, with 16px below the last paragraph.
7. Give each item an id and open the one that matches `location.hash` on load (two lines of script), so support staff can link to a single answer.
8. Do not hide prices, cancellation terms or anything a person needs before paying inside a closed item.

#### Reference build

```html
<div class="acc">
  <details id="refund-window">
    <summary>Can I get a refund after 30 days?</summary>
    <div class="acc-body">
      <p>Yes, for annual plans. We refund the unused months, rounded down. Monthly plans are not refunded after the first 30 days.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details id="file-types">
    <summary>Which file types can I import?</summary>
    <div class="acc-body">
      <p>CSV, XLSX and JSON, up to 50 MB per file.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>
```

```css
.acc { max-width: 66ch; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.acc details { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.acc summary {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
  min-height: 44px; padding: 12px 0;
  font: 500 16px/1.4 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink);
  cursor: pointer; list-style: none;
}
.acc summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
.acc summary::before {
  content: ""; flex: none; width: 7px; height: 7px;
  border-right: 1.5px solid var(--ink-2); border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--ink-2);
  transform: rotate(-45deg); transition: transform 120ms ease-out;
}
.acc details[open] > summary::before { transform: rotate(45deg); }
.acc summary:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 3px; }
.acc summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.acc-body { padding: 0 0 16px 20px; color: var(--ink-2); }
.acc-body p { margin: 0 0 8px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .acc summary::before { transition: none; }
}
```

#### States

- Hover: the label gets a 1px underline at 3px offset. No row fill; a filled band reads as selection.
- Focus-visible: 2px `var(--focus)` outline at 2px offset around the summary.
- Open: the chevron points down. The label keeps its weight.

#### Copy

```slop
What makes us different?
How does the magic work?
Is it secure?
```

Write the summary as the question a customer types into a search box, with the noun they use.

- Can I get a refund after 30 days?
- Which file types can I import?
- Where is my data stored? (Answer: Frankfurt, eu-central-1.)

#### Checklist

- Native `details` and `summary`, no click handler on a div.
- One bordered list, rows separated by 1px rules, no per-item cards.
- Summary at least 44px tall, chevron before the label, 120ms or no motion.
- Multiple items can be open, or the `name` attribute is used deliberately.

### 4.2 Alerts and banners

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-600 to-purple-600 py-2 text-center text-sm text-white">
  <PartyPopper className="mr-2 inline h-4 w-4" /> We just launched v2.0! <a href="#" className="font-semibold underline">Check it out</a>
</div>

<div className="fixed right-4 top-4 z-50 flex items-start gap-3 rounded-xl border border-green-200 bg-green-50 p-4 shadow-lg animate-in slide-in-from-top-5">
  <CheckCircle2 className="h-5 w-5 text-green-500" />
  <div>
    <h3 className="font-semibold text-green-800">Success!</h3>
    <p className="text-sm text-green-700">Your changes have been saved successfully.</p>
  </div>
  <button className="ml-auto text-green-500 hover:text-green-700"><X className="h-4 w-4" /></button>
</div>
```

Two defaults stacked. The announcement bar is the `from-indigo-600 to-purple-600` strip that ships above every SaaS template. The toast is the shadcn and react-hot-toast pattern: top-right, `shadow-lg`, a slide-in, a `Success!` heading that adds nothing, and a body that says "successfully" after already saying success. Green 500 text on green 50 measures about 2.3:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum.

#### Rules

1. Put the message where the problem is: under the failed field, at the top of the failed table. A page-wide banner is only for account-wide states: billing failed, maintenance, read-only mode.
2. Banner: full width, 40px minimum height, 14px text, one sentence, at most one link and one dismiss button. Background `var(--paper-2)`, 1px bottom rule in the status color.
3. Inline alert: `var(--paper-2)` background, 1px border in the status color (`--bad`, `--warn`, `--ok`) or `--rule-strong` for neutral, 2px radius, 12px 16px padding. The first word is the status in weight 600 ("Error.", "Warning.", "Saved."), so the meaning survives without color.
4. Toasts confirm actions the person just took and nothing else. Bottom-left or bottom-center, 16px from the viewport edges, 360px wide at most. One visible at a time; queue the rest.
5. Toasts that only confirm stay 5 seconds and pause while hovered or focused. Toasts with an action ("Undo") stay 10 seconds. Errors never go in a toast; they stay on the page until fixed.
6. Use `role="status"` for confirmations and `role="alert"` only for errors that appear after the person acted. Never put `role="alert"` on content present at page load.

#### Reference build

```html
<div class="banner" role="region" aria-label="Account notice" data-tone="warn">
  <p>Your card ending 4421 was declined on 14 Oct. Service stops on 28 Oct. <a href="/billing">Update card</a></p>
  <button class="banner-close" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss notice">Dismiss</button>
</div>

<div class="alert" data-tone="bad" role="alert">
  <p><strong>Error.</strong> 3 of 120 rows were not imported because the date column is empty. <a href="#row-14">Go to row 14</a></p>
</div>

<div class="toast" role="status">
  <p>Invoice 1042 deleted.</p>
  <button type="button">Undo</button>
</div>
```

```css
[data-tone="bad"]  { --tone: var(--bad); }
[data-tone="warn"] { --tone: var(--warn); }
[data-tone="ok"]   { --tone: var(--ok); }

.banner {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px;
  min-height: 40px; padding: 8px 16px;
  background: var(--paper-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--tone, var(--rule-strong));
  font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink);
}
.banner p { margin: 0; max-width: 90ch; }
.banner-close {
  font: inherit; color: var(--ink-2); background: none; border: 0;
```
