```css
.set-label { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; }
.set-desc { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink-2); max-width: 66ch; }
.set-saved { grid-column: 2; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ok); justify-self: end; }
.set-saved:empty { display: none; }
.switch { position: relative; width: 36px; height: 20px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--ink-3); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--paper-3); cursor: pointer; }
.switch span { position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--ink-3); transition: transform 120ms ease-out; }
.switch[aria-checked="true"] { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); }
.switch[aria-checked="true"] span { transform: translateX(16px); border-color: var(--ink); }
.switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .switch span { transition: none; } }
```

The switch is square, with the same 2px radius as every other control. The `rounded-full` pill track is a shadcn default, not a requirement.

#### States

- Saving: the "Saved" slot reads "Saving..." and the control stays enabled.
- Save failed: the control reverts, and the slot reads "Not saved. Retry" in `--bad`.
- Locked by an admin: control disabled, description adds "Set by your workspace owner."
- Unsaved text changes when leaving: one confirm dialog listing the fields that would be lost.

#### Copy

```slop
Danger Zone
Manage how you receive updates
Delete
Your preferences have been updated successfully!
```

- Delete workspace
- Daily digest. One email at 08:00 with yesterday's payments and overdue invoices.
- Saved
- Type "harbor-supply" to delete this workspace and its 1,284 invoices.

#### Checklist

- Rows with 1px borders, no cards, no icon circles.
- One save model per section.
- Switches only for settings that apply at once.
- Destructive section names the object and asks for typed confirmation.
- Anchors on every setting.

### 5.10 Sliders

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="relative pt-8">
  <div className="absolute -top-1 left-[60%] -translate-x-1/2 rounded-lg bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 px-2 py-1 text-xs text-white shadow-lg">$600</div>
  <input type="range" className="h-2 w-full appearance-none rounded-full bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500
    [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:h-6 [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:w-6 [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:appearance-none
    [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:rounded-full [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:bg-white [&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:shadow-[0_0_0_4px_rgba(99,102,241,0.3)]" />
</div>
```

This is the custom range from a dozen Tailwind snippet sites: a three-stop gradient track, a white thumb ringed in an indigo glow, and a floating value bubble that sits exactly under the user's thumb on a phone. Most of these snippets paint the filled part of the track with a `linear-gradient` background that is recomputed on every input event.

#### Rules

1. Use a slider when relative position matters more than the exact number: volume, zoom, opacity, a rough budget. When the exact number matters, use a number input, or pair the slider with one.
2. Show the current value as text beside the label, in tabular numerals, with its unit: "Opacity 60%".
3. Track 4px tall, `--paper-3`. Thumb 16px with a 2px `--ink` border and `--paper` fill. The hit area is at least 24px tall on pointer devices and 44px on touch.
4. Use the native `<input type="range">` with `accent-color: var(--ink)`. Do not paint progress with a gradient background.
5. Label the ends with min and max in 12px `--ink-3`.
6. Keyboard: arrows move 1 step, Page Up and Page Down move 10 steps, Home and End go to the ends. The native input does this already.
7. Set `aria-valuetext` when the number alone is unclear: "60 percent", "3 days".
8. Avoid two-thumb ranges outside filters. In a filter, pair them with two number inputs labelled "Minimum" and "Maximum".
9. No floating value bubble. The value lives in the label.

#### Reference build

```html
<div class="rng">
  <div class="rng-head"><label for="op">Opacity</label><output for="op" id="op-out">60%</output></div>
  <input id="op" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="5" value="60" aria-valuetext="60 percent">
  <div class="rng-ends" aria-hidden="true"><span>0%</span><span>100%</span></div>
</div>
```

```css
.rng { max-width: 320px; font-size: 14px; }
.rng-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 4px; }
.rng-head label { font-weight: 600; }
.rng-head output { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink); }
.rng input { width: 100%; height: 24px; margin: 0; accent-color: var(--ink); cursor: pointer; }
.rng input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.rng-ends { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink-3); }
@media (pointer: coarse) { .rng input { height: 44px; } }
```

```js
const r = document.getElementById('op'), o = document.getElementById('op-out');
r.addEventListener('input', () => { o.value = r.value + '%'; r.setAttribute('aria-valuetext', r.value + ' percent'); });
```

#### States

- Default, hover (cursor only), focus (2px outline), dragging (no change in thumb size), disabled (`--ink-3` label, `accent-color: var(--ink-3)`).
- Out of range typed value in the paired input: clamp on blur and say so under the field, "Maximum is 100%".
- Snapped steps: when only a few values are valid (1, 3, 7, 30 days), use a segmented control instead (see 5.11).

#### Copy

```slop
Drag to adjust
Slide to unlock your perfect budget
```

- Opacity 60%
- Budget per month, $200 to $5,000
- Maximum is 100%

#### Checklist

- Native range with `accent-color`, no gradient fill trick.
- Value and unit in the label.
- 24px hit area, 44px on touch.
- Paired number input when exact values matter.
- No floating bubble, no glow ring.

### 5.11 Tabs and segmented controls

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList className="relative rounded-full bg-gray-100 p-1 shadow-inner">
    <motion.div layoutId="pill" className="absolute inset-y-1 rounded-full bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-500 shadow-lg" />
    <TabsTrigger value="overview" className="relative z-10 rounded-full px-6 py-2 data-[state=active]:text-white">Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="analytics" className="relative z-10 rounded-full px-6 py-2">Analytics</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
</Tabs>
<div className="rounded-full bg-gray-100 p-1">
  <button className="rounded-full bg-white px-4 py-1 shadow">Monthly</button>
  <button className="rounded-full px-4 py-1">Yearly <span className="ml-1 rounded-full bg-emerald-100 px-2 text-xs text-emerald-700">-20%</span></button>
</div>
```

This is the shadcn `Tabs` component with a Framer Motion `layoutId` pill sliding between triggers, a pattern copied from a popular Vercel demo. Tabs and segmented control end up looking identical, so the reader cannot tell "switch the whole view" from "change one parameter".

#### Rules

1. Tabs switch between views of the same object. A segmented control changes one parameter of the current view (unit, period, filter). Never style the two the same way.
2. Use at most 7 tabs. Past that, the content needs a sidebar or separate pages.
3. Tabs are 40px tall, 14px text, 16px horizontal padding, on a 1px `--rule` baseline. The selected tab gets `--ink` text, weight 600, and a 2px `--ink` underline that overlaps the baseline.
4. Reserve the bold width so tabs do not shift when selected: render the label twice and hide the bold copy with zero height.
5. In-page tabs use `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and `role="tabpanel"`. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump to the ends, and only the selected tab is in the Tab order.
6. Tabs that change the URL path are links in a `<nav>` with `aria-current="page"`, not ARIA tabs.
7. Segmented controls hold 2 to 4 options, are 32px tall, and are built from radio inputs. The group has a 1px `--ink` border, segments are divided by 1px `--ink` lines, and the checked segment is `--ink` with `--paper` text.
8. Indicator motion is 150ms or less, transform only, and none under reduced motion. No sliding pill.
9. On narrow screens, tabs scroll horizontally on one row. Never wrap tabs onto two rows.

#### Reference build

```html
<div role="tablist" aria-label="Invoice" class="tabs">
  <button role="tab" id="t1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="p1" data-label="Details">Details</button>
  <button role="tab" id="t2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="p2" tabindex="-1" data-label="Payments">Payments <span class="tab-n">3</span></button>
  <button role="tab" id="t3" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="p3" tabindex="-1" data-label="History">History</button>
</div>
<div role="tabpanel" id="p1" aria-labelledby="t1" tabindex="0">...</div>

<fieldset class="seg"><legend class="sr-only">Period</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="period" value="m" checked><span>Month</span></label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="period" value="q"><span>Quarter</span></label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="period" value="y"><span>Year</span></label>
</fieldset>
```

```css
.tabs { display: flex; gap: 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); overflow-x: auto; }
.tabs [role="tab"] { position: relative; display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; height: 40px; justify-content: center; padding: 0 16px; margin-bottom: -1px; background: none; border: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; color: var(--ink-2); font: 14px var(--font-sans); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; }
.tabs [role="tab"]::after { content: attr(data-label); height: 0; overflow: hidden; visibility: hidden; font-weight: 600; }
.tabs [aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; border-bottom-color: var(--ink); }
.tabs [role="tab"]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -2px; }
.tab-n { font: 12px var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink-3); }
.seg { display: inline-flex; margin: 0; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--ink); border-radius: var(--radius); }
.seg label + label { border-left: 1px solid var(--ink); }
.seg input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; }
.seg span { display: block; height: 30px; line-height: 30px; padding: 0 12px; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; }
.seg input:checked + span { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); }
.seg input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
```

The tab focus ring uses a -2px offset so the scroll container does not clip it.

#### States

- Selected, hover (`--ink` text), focus, disabled (`--ink-3`, `aria-disabled`, skipped by arrows only if it can never become active).
- Panel loading: switch tabs at once and show the panel's own loading state. Never block tab selection on a fetch.

#### Copy

```slop
Overview / Analytics / Insights / More
Yearly -20%
```

- Details / Payments 3 / History
- Month / Quarter / Year
- Billed yearly, $288 per user

#### Checklist

- Tabs and segmented controls look different.
- 7 tabs or fewer, single row, 2px underline on a 1px baseline.
- Bold width reserved, no layout shift.
- Full ARIA tab pattern with roving tabindex.
- No sliding gradient pill.

### 5.12 Testimonials

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="grid gap-8 md:grid-cols-3">
  <div className="rounded-2xl bg-white p-8 shadow-xl ring-1 ring-gray-100">
    <div className="flex gap-1 text-yellow-400"><StarIcon /><StarIcon /><StarIcon /><StarIcon /><StarIcon /></div>
    <p className="mt-4 text-lg text-gray-700">"This tool is an absolute game-changer! Our productivity skyrocketed and the team loves it."</p>
    <div className="mt-6 flex items-center gap-3">
      <img src="https://i.pravatar.cc/100?img=47" className="h-12 w-12 rounded-full ring-2 ring-indigo-500" />
      <div><p className="font-semibold">Sarah Johnson</p><p className="text-sm text-gray-500">CEO at TechCorp</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  ...
</div>
```

This is the Tailwind UI testimonial grid filled by a model: avatars from `i.pravatar.cc`, five yellow stars copied from review widgets, and a placeholder name with a placeholder company. The quote praises the product in general terms and contains no fact a reader could check. Readers have seen "Sarah Johnson, CEO at TechCorp" so often that it now marks the whole page as fake.

#### Rules

1. Publish only quotes from named people who approved the exact wording in writing. Keep the approval on file with its date. No real quote, no section.
2. Each quote carries one checkable claim: a number, a task, a before and after. At most 60 words. Cut with "..." if needed. Never reword.
3. Attribution is full name, role, company, and a link to the case study when one exists. Use a photo only if the person supplied it. Otherwise show no image at all, and no initials in a colored circle.
4. Star ratings only from a named review site, with the score, the review count and a link: "4.6 from 212 reviews".
5. At most 3 quotes on a page. One long quote with a link to the full case study beats a wall of 12. No carousel, no marquee.
6. Quote text is `--font-serif` at 21px with 1.4 line height. Attribution is 14px sans. No 120px decorative quotation mark.

#### Reference build

```html
<figure class="quote">
  <blockquote><p>We closed March in 3 days instead of 9. The bank import matched 96% of our transactions without a single manual edit.</p></blockquote>
  <figcaption>Dana Okafor, Controller, Harbor Supply. <a href="/customers/harbor-supply">Read how they set it up</a></figcaption>
</figure>
```

```css
.quote { max-width: 66ch; margin: 48px 0; padding-left: 24px; border-left: 2px solid var(--ink); }
.quote blockquote { margin: 0; }
.quote p { margin: 0; font: 21px/1.4 var(--font-serif); color: var(--ink); }
.quote figcaption { margin-top: 16px; font: 14px/1.5 var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink-2); }
.quote a { color: var(--ink); text-underline-offset: 3px; }
```

#### States

- One quote: full width, as above.
- Two or three: stacked vertically, 48px apart. A three-column grid of quotes forces equal lengths and invites padding.

#### Copy

```slop
"An absolute game-changer for our team!"
"I can't imagine working without it. Five stars!"
"Seamless, intuitive, and powerful."
Sarah Johnson, CEO at TechCorp
```

- "We closed March in 3 days instead of 9." Dana Okafor, Controller, Harbor Supply
- "Support answered our SAML question in 40 minutes, on a Sunday." Luis Ferreira, IT lead, Norte Freight
- 4.6 from 212 reviews

#### Checklist

- Real person, approved wording, approval on file.
- One checkable claim per quote, 60 words or fewer.
- No stock avatars, no initials circles, no unsourced stars.
- Three quotes or fewer, no carousel.

### 5.13 Timelines and changelogs

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="relative">
  <div className="absolute left-1/2 h-full w-1 bg-gradient-to-b from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500" />
  <div className="mb-12 flex w-1/2 justify-end pr-8">
    <div className="rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow-xl">
      <span className="rounded-full bg-gradient-to-r from-emerald-400 to-cyan-400 px-3 py-1 text-xs text-white">New</span>
      <h3 className="mt-2 text-xl font-bold">Introducing AI Insights</h3>
      <p className="text-gray-500">We're thrilled to announce our most powerful release yet...</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

This is the zigzag timeline from template marketplaces: a gradient spine down the middle, cards alternating left and right, and colored pills for "New", "Improved" and "Fixed". Alternating sides makes dates impossible to scan, and the entries open with excitement before saying what changed.

#### Rules

1. One column. The date sits in a fixed 128px left column. Newest first.
2. Write dates as "8 Oct 2026" and versions in `--font-mono`. Never "2 weeks ago" on a changelog.
3. One entry per release. The title says what changed in user terms: "Bank rules can match on amount ranges".
4. Group items under plain headings: Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed. No colored pills.
5. Each item is one sentence that starts with the thing that changed and links to its docs.
6. Every entry has an anchor. Publish an Atom or RSS feed.
7. In-app activity timelines use rows of time (12px mono), actor, action and object, grouped under a day heading. The spine, if any, is 1px `--rule`, with 8px square markers in `--ink`.

#### Reference build

```html
<article class="log" id="v4-12">
  <p class="log-date"><time datetime="2026-10-08">8 Oct 2026</time><br><code>v4.12</code></p>
  <div class="log-body">
    <h3>Bank rules can match on amount ranges</h3>
    <h4>Added</h4>
    <ul><li>Bank rules accept a minimum and maximum amount. <a href="/docs/rules#amount">Docs</a></li></ul>
    <h4>Fixed</h4>
    <ul><li>CSV export no longer drops the last row when a memo contains a line break.</li></ul>
  </div>
</article>
```

```css
.log { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 128px minmax(0, 66ch); gap: 24px; padding: 32px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.log-date { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink-2); }
.log-date code { font: 12px var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink-3); }
.log h3 { margin: 0 0 16px; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.25; }
.log h4 { margin: 16px 0 4px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-2); }
.log ul { margin: 0; padding-left: 16px; line-height: 1.6; }
@media (max-width: 600px) { .log { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 8px; } }
```

#### States

- Breaking change: an item under Changed that starts with "Breaking:" and says what to do before the date it takes effect.
- Rolled back: keep the entry, strike nothing, and add a dated note under it saying what was reverted.

#### Copy

```slop
Introducing AI Insights: our most powerful release yet!
We're thrilled to announce...
Various bug fixes and performance improvements.
```

- Bank rules can match on amount ranges
- Fixed: CSV export no longer drops the last row when a memo contains a line break.
- Breaking: the v1 invoices API stops accepting requests on 1 Feb 2027. Move to v2 first.

#### Checklist

- Single column, fixed date column, newest first.
- Absolute dates, versions in mono.
- Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed as text headings.
- No "Various bug fixes". Each fix is named.

### 5.14 Tooltips and popovers

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger><InformationCircleIcon className="h-4 w-4 text-gray-400" /></TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent className="rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-gray-900 to-indigo-900 px-4 py-3 text-white shadow-2xl">
    <p className="font-semibold">Pro tip</p>
    <p className="text-sm">Your API key is only shown once. <a href="/docs" className="underline">Learn more</a></p>
  </TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
<PopoverContent className="w-80 rounded-2xl border-white/20 bg-white/70 p-6 shadow-2xl backdrop-blur-xl">...</PopoverContent>
```

This is the shadcn `Tooltip` holding information the user cannot afford to miss, plus a link that nobody can reach because the tooltip closes when the pointer leaves the icon. Info icons get scattered beside every label, and popovers get the same glass treatment as modals, with `backdrop-blur-xl` over `bg-white/70`.

#### Rules

1. A tooltip holds a short label for an icon-only control, or the full text of a truncated value. At most 80 characters. No links, no buttons, nothing the user must know.
2. Show it after 500ms of hover and at once on keyboard focus. Hide it on Escape, on blur, and 100ms after the pointer leaves both trigger and tooltip. The pointer must be able to move onto it (WCAG 1.4.13).
3. Style: `--ink` background, `--paper` text, 12px/16px, 4px by 8px padding, `--radius` corners, 240px maximum width, 8px from the trigger. Flip to the other side at the viewport edge.
4. For an icon button, the tooltip text equals its `aria-label`. For extra information, connect it with `aria-describedby`.
5. Touch screens get no tooltips. Icon-only controls on touch need a visible text label.
6. If a screen needs more than 3 info icons, write the help text into the page under the labels.
7. Popovers hold interactive content: filters, date pickers, short forms. `--paper` background, 1px `--ink` border, 16px padding, 320px maximum width. No blur.
8. Use the HTML `popover` attribute or a non-modal dialog. Focus moves into the popover on open. Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

#### Reference build

```html
<span class="tip-wrap">
  <button type="button" class="icon-btn" aria-label="Duplicate invoice" aria-describedby="tip-dup">
    <svg class="i" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-copy"/></svg>
  </button>
  <span role="tooltip" id="tip-dup" class="tip">Duplicate invoice</span>
</span>

<button type="button" popovertarget="filters" class="btn-outline">Filters (2)</button>
<div id="filters" popover class="pop">
  <form>...</form>
</div>
```

```css
.tip-wrap { position: relative; display: inline-block; }
.tip { position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: calc(100% + 8px); transform: translateX(-50%); max-width: 240px; padding: 4px 8px; background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); font: 12px/16px var(--font-sans); border-radius: var(--radius); white-space: nowrap; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 100ms ease-out; }
.tip-wrap:hover .tip { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; transition-delay: 500ms; }
.tip-wrap:focus-within .tip { opacity: 1; transition-delay: 0ms; }
@media (hover: none) { .tip { display: none; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .tip { transition: none; } }
.pop { margin: 0; padding: 16px; width: 320px; max-width: calc(100vw - 32px); background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--ink); border-radius: var(--radius); }
.pop::backdrop { background: transparent; }
```

Escape-to-close needs a few lines of script. CSS cannot do it.

#### States

- Truncated text: the tooltip appears only when the text is actually cut off. Check `scrollWidth > clientWidth` before attaching it.
- Popover open: the trigger gets `aria-expanded="true"` and a `--paper-3` background.

#### Copy

```slop
Pro tip: Your API key is only shown once!
Hover for more info
Learn more
```

- Duplicate invoice
- Due 14 Nov 2026 (net 30)
- Filters (2)

#### Checklist

- Tooltips hold labels, never required information or links.
- 500ms hover delay, instant on focus, hoverable, Escape closes.
- `--ink` tooltip, `--paper` popover with 1px `--ink` border.
- No info icon farms, no blur, no tooltips on touch.

### 5.15 User menus and account switchers

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger className="relative rounded-full p-0.5 bg-gradient-to-tr from-indigo-500 to-pink-500">
    <img src={user.avatar} className="h-9 w-9 rounded-full border-2 border-white" />
    <span className="absolute bottom-0 right-0 h-3 w-3 rounded-full bg-green-500 ring-2 ring-white" />
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent className="w-64 rounded-xl shadow-xl">
    <DropdownMenuItem><UserIcon /> Profile</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 text-white"><SparklesIcon /> Upgrade to Pro</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem className="text-red-600"><ArrowRightOnRectangleIcon /> Log out</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

This is the shadcn `DropdownMenu` demo with an Instagram-style gradient ring on the avatar and a green online dot that tells the user they are online. An upgrade item is dressed as the primary action, and "Log out" is red as if signing out destroyed data. Workspace switchers built from the same kit show each workspace as a letter in its own gradient tile.

#### Rules

1. The trigger is a 32px avatar, square with `--radius` corners: the user's photo, or initials in `--ink` on `--paper-3`. Its accessible name is "Account: Priya Nair".
2. The menu header shows name, email, and the current workspace with the user's role, as text.
3. Order the items: Profile, Settings, Billing (owners only), Keyboard shortcuts, Help, then Sign out after a 1px `--rule` separator. At most 8 items.
4. Build it as a disclosure button controlling a list of links unless every item is an action. Use `role="menu"` only for action menus, with arrow-key handling to match.
5. The account switcher lists workspaces by name with the user's role in 12px `--ink-3`. The current one gets a 16px check SVG and `aria-current="true"`. Past 8 workspaces, add a filter field.
6. Workspace tiles are 20px squares with one letter in `--ink` on `--paper-3`, or the workspace's uploaded logo. No generated colors.
7. "Sign out" is plain `--ink` text. It is not destructive. When the user has more than one account signed in, say which one: "Sign out of Harbor Supply".
8. No presence dot on the user's own avatar.

#### Reference build

```html
<div class="acct">
  <button type="button" class="acct-btn" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="acct-menu" aria-label="Account: Priya Nair">PN</button>
  <div id="acct-menu" class="acct-menu">
    <div class="acct-head"><p class="n">Priya Nair</p><p class="e">priya@harborsupply.com</p><p class="e">Harbor Supply, Owner</p></div>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="/profile">Profile</a></li>
      <li><a href="/settings">Settings</a></li>
      <li><a href="/settings/billing">Billing</a></li>
      <li><a href="/help">Help</a></li>
    </ul>
    <form action="/signout" method="post"><button type="submit">Sign out</button></form>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.acct { position: relative; }
.acct-btn { width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--paper-3); color: var(--ink); font: 600 12px var(--font-sans); cursor: pointer; }
.acct-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.acct-menu { position: absolute; right: 0; top: 40px; width: 256px; background: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--ink); border-radius: var(--radius); font-size: 14px; z-index: 30; }
.acct-head { padding: 12px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.acct-head p { margin: 0; }
.acct-head .n { font-weight: 600; }
.acct-head .e { color: var(--ink-2); font-size: 12px; }
.acct-menu ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 4px 0; }
.acct-menu a, .acct-menu form button { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 8px 16px; color: var(--ink); text-align: left; text-decoration: none; background: none; border: 0; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; }
.acct-menu a:hover, .acct-menu form button:hover { background: var(--paper-2); }
.acct-menu form { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); padding: 4px 0; }
```

#### States

- Closed, open, item hover, item focus. Escape closes and returns focus to the avatar.
- Switching workspace: the whole page reloads into the new workspace. Show its name in the page title at once.
- Impersonation by support staff: a full-width `--warn` bar above the app, "Viewing as Priya Nair. Actions are logged. Stop".

#### Copy

```slop
Log out
Upgrade to Pro
Hey, Priya!
My Awesome Workspace
```

- Sign out
- Sign out of Harbor Supply
- Harbor Supply, Owner
- Switch workspace

#### Checklist

- Square 32px avatar, no gradient ring, no own presence dot.
- Header names the user, email, workspace and role.
- At most 8 items, Sign out last and not red.
- Workspace tiles plain or real logos.

### 5.16 Feature grids

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-8 md:grid-cols-3">
  {[
    { icon: BoltIcon, title: 'Lightning Fast', desc: 'Experience blazing-fast performance that scales with your business.' },
    { icon: ShieldCheckIcon, title: 'Secure by Default', desc: 'Enterprise-grade security to keep your data safe.' },
    { icon: PuzzlePieceIcon, title: 'Seamless Integrations', desc: 'Connect with all your favorite tools in one click.' },
    { icon: SparklesIcon, title: 'AI-Powered', desc: 'Harness the power of AI to work smarter, not harder.' },
    { icon: UsersIcon, title: 'Real-time Collaboration', desc: 'Work together with your team, anywhere.' },
    { icon: LifebuoyIcon, title: '24/7 Support', desc: 'Our dedicated team is always here to help.' },
  ].map(f => (
    <div className="rounded-2xl p-6 shadow-sm hover:shadow-xl transition">
      <div className="flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-indigo-100"><f.icon className="h-6 w-6 text-indigo-600" /></div>
      <h3 className="mt-4 font-semibold">{f.title}</h3><p className="text-gray-500">{f.desc}</p>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>
```

This is the most recognisable block in machine-made marketing: six tiles in a 3 by 2 grid, each a Heroicon in an `indigo-100` circle, an adjective title, and one sentence any product could claim. Six is chosen because it fills the grid, not because the product has six things to say. "Fast", "Secure" and "24/7 Support" are table stakes and tell the reader nothing.

#### Rules

1. The number of features equals what the product has worth saying. Three described properly, each with a screenshot, beat six tiles.
2. A feature title states what the product does to a named object: "Match bank lines to open invoices". No adjective titles.
3. The body is 2 or 3 sentences and contains a number, a limit or a mechanism: "Matches on amount, date within 5 days, and reference. 96% of lines match without edits in our median account."
4. No icon circles. If an icon helps scanning, it is 20px, stroked, `--ink`, inline with the title. A cropped real screenshot is better than any icon.
5. Lay out features as rows: title in the left third, text and screenshot in the right two thirds, 1px `--rule` between rows, 48px vertical padding.
6. Link each feature to its docs page.
7. Move table stakes (encryption, uptime, support hours) to a specs list or the FAQ, with numbers.
8. No hover lift, no hover glow. Rows are not clickable unless the whole row is one link.

#### Reference build

```html
<section class="feat" aria-labelledby="feat-h">
  <h2 id="feat-h">What it does</h2>
  <div class="feat-row">
    <h3>Match bank lines to open invoices</h3>
    <div>
      <p>Matches on amount, date within 5 days, and reference number. In the median account, 96% of lines match without edits.</p>
      <img src="/img/match-1x.png" width="640" height="360" alt="Bank line for $4,120.00 matched to invoice INV-2041 from Acme Freight">
      <p><a href="/docs/matching">How matching works</a></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```css
.feat { max-width: 1040px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 96px 16px; }
.feat h2 { font-size: 32px; margin: 0 0 32px; }
.feat-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr; gap: 32px; padding: 48px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.feat-row h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.25; }
.feat-row p { margin: 0 0 16px; max-width: 66ch; color: var(--ink-2); }
.feat-row img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; border: 1px solid var(--rule); margin-bottom: 16px; }
.feat-row a { color: var(--ink); text-underline-offset: 3px; }
@media (max-width: 768px) { .feat-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 16px; } }
```

#### States

- No screenshot available: text only. Never fill the slot with an abstract illustration or a 3D blob.
- Feature in beta: say "Beta, available on Team and Company plans" in the body text, not in a pill.

#### Copy

```slop
Lightning Fast
Seamless Integrations
AI-Powered
Harness the power of AI to work smarter, not harder.
Everything you need, all in one place.
```

- Match bank lines to open invoices
- Send reminders on day 1, 7 and 14 after the due date
- Export a VAT return as the CSV your tax office accepts

#### Checklist

- As many features as there are real ones, not six by default.
- Titles are verbs on objects. Bodies have numbers.
- No icon circles, no hover lift.
- Rows with screenshots and docs links.

### 5.17 Logo walls and social proof

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<p className="text-center text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-widest text-gray-500">Trusted by 10,000+ teams worldwide</p>
<div className="relative overflow-hidden [mask-image:linear-gradient(to_right,transparent,black_20%,black_80%,transparent)]">
  <div className="flex animate-marquee gap-16 grayscale opacity-60">
    <img src="/logos/google.svg" /><img src="/logos/microsoft.svg" /><img src="/logos/spotify.svg" />
    <img src="/logos/airbnb.svg" /><img src="/logos/stripe.svg" /><img src="/logos/notion.svg" />
  </div>
</div>
<div className="mt-8 flex items-center justify-center -space-x-2">
  {avatars.map(a => <img src={a} className="h-10 w-10 rounded-full ring-2 ring-white" />)}
  <span className="ml-4 text-sm">Join 5,000+ happy users</span>
</div>
```

This is the "Trusted by" strip from every landing template: logos of companies that are not customers, desaturated with `grayscale opacity-60`, scrolling in an infinite marquee behind a gradient edge mask, then an overlapping stack of stock avatars. The round number with a plus sign ("10,000+") signals that nobody counted.

#### Rules

1. Show only logos of current paying customers who gave written permission. Remove a logo within 30 days of a customer leaving.
2. Use 4 to 8 logos in one static row. No marquee, no carousel, no edge fade mask.
3. Normalise logos by visual weight, not by box. Start at 24px tall and adjust each one by eye so they read at the same size. Render them as single-color SVG using `fill: currentColor` in `--ink-2`.
4. The line above states an exact count and a date: "Used by 1,140 finance teams as of October 2026, including". No plus signs, no "worldwide".
5. Link a logo only when a case study exists, and say so in the alt text: "Harbor Supply case study".
6. Avatar stacks are banned.

#### Reference build

```html
<section class="logos" aria-labelledby="logos-h">
  <p id="logos-h">Used by 1,140 finance teams as of October 2026, including</p>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="/customers/harbor-supply"><svg role="img" aria-label="Harbor Supply case study" height="24" width="112"><use href="#logo-harbor"/></svg></a></li>
    <li><svg role="img" aria-label="Norte Freight" height="22" width="104"><use href="#logo-norte"/></svg></li>
    <li><svg role="img" aria-label="Calder Dental" height="26" width="96"><use href="#logo-calder"/></svg></li>
  </ul>
</section>
```

```css
.logos { max-width: 1040px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 48px 16px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.logos p { margin: 0 0 24px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink-2); }
.logos ul { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 24px 48px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; color: var(--ink-2); }
.logos svg { display: block; fill: currentColor; }
.logos a { color: var(--ink-2); }
.logos a:hover { color: var(--ink); }
.logos a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 4px; }
```

#### States

- Fewer than 4 permitted logos: drop the strip and use one named quote (see 5.12) instead.
- Dark theme: logos inherit `--ink-2` from the dark tokens. Never ship a second, inverted raster set.

#### Copy

```slop
Trusted by 10,000+ teams worldwide
Join 5,000+ happy users
Loved by industry leaders
```

- Used by 1,140 finance teams as of October 2026, including
- Harbor Supply closed March in 3 days. Read the case study

#### Checklist

- Real customers, written permission, dated count.
- 4 to 8 logos, static, single color.
- No marquee, no fade mask, no avatar stack, no plus signs.

### 5.18 Stats and KPI rows

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-8 md:grid-cols-4">
  {[['10x', 'Faster workflows'], ['99.9%', 'Uptime'], ['500K+', 'Happy users'], ['24/7', 'Support']].map(([n, l]) => (
    <div className="rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 text-center shadow-lg">
      <p className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 bg-clip-text text-5xl font-extrabold text-transparent"><CountUp end={n} /></p>
      <p className="mt-2 text-gray-500">{l}</p>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>
```

This is the stats band from SaaS templates: four numbers in gradient text that count up on scroll. "10x" has no baseline, "99.9%" has no period or scope, "500K+" is a rounded guess, and "24/7" is not a statistic. The `CountUp` animation means a screenshot taken mid-scroll shows the wrong numbers.

#### Rules

1. Every number carries its unit, period and scope: "99.95% API uptime, January to September 2026".
2. Comparative claims name the baseline: "Month-end close in 3 days, down from 9, median of 40 customers who switched in 2025". No bare multipliers.
3. Write the counted number: "1,140", not "1K+". Plus signs are banned.
4. Link each figure to its source: the status page, the study, the methods note.
5. At most 4 stats in a row, separated by 1px `--rule` lines. Value 32px `--ink`, tabular numerals, weight 600. Label 14px `--ink-2` below, at most 2 lines.
6. No gradient text, no count-up animation, no cards.
7. In product dashboards, a KPI shows value, change with sign and period ("+4.1% vs September"), and color only when the direction is good or bad for that metric. Churn going up is `--bad`. Keep the sign in the text so color is never the only signal.

#### Reference build

```html
<dl class="stats">
  <div><dt>API uptime, Jan to Sep 2026</dt><dd>99.95%</dd><dd class="src"><a href="https://status.example.com">Status history</a></dd></div>
  <div><dt>Median month-end close after switching, was 9 days</dt><dd>3 days</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Finance teams using it, October 2026</dt><dd>1,140</dd></div>
</dl>
```

```css
.stats { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)); margin: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.stats > div { display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; justify-content: flex-end; padding: 24px; border-left: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.stats > div:first-child { border-left: 0; }
.stats dt { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--ink-2); }
.stats dd { margin: 0; font-size: 32px; line-height: 1.15; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.stats dd.src { order: -1; margin-top: 8px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; }
.stats a { color: var(--ink-2); }
```

`column-reverse` keeps the label first for screen readers and puts the number first for the eye.

#### States

- Number not yet measured: leave the stat out. Never ship "XX%" or a rounded guess.
- Stale number: show the "as of" date in the label, and review every stat each quarter.
- Dashboard KPI with no prior period: show the value alone and "No September data" in place of the change.

#### Copy

```slop
10x faster
99.9% uptime
500K+ happy users
24/7 support
Skyrocket your ROI
```

- 99.95% API uptime, January to September 2026
- Month-end close in 3 days, down from 9
- 1,140 finance teams, October 2026
- Revenue $84,120, +4.1% vs September

#### Checklist

- Unit, period, scope and source on every number.
- No multipliers without baseline, no plus signs.
- No gradient text, no count-up, no cards.
- Direction-aware color with the sign in text.

### 5.19 Call-to-action sections

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<section className="relative overflow-hidden rounded-3xl bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-600 via-purple-600 to-pink-500 px-8 py-24 text-center shadow-2xl">
  <div className="absolute -top-24 left-1/2 h-96 w-96 -translate-x-1/2 rounded-full bg-white/20 blur-3xl" />
  <h2 className="text-5xl font-bold text-white">Ready to transform your workflow?</h2>
  <p className="mt-4 text-xl text-indigo-100">Join thousands of teams already building the future.</p>
  <div className="mt-10 flex justify-center gap-4">
    <button className="rounded-full bg-white px-8 py-4 font-semibold text-indigo-600 shadow-lg">Get started for free</button>
    <button className="rounded-full border border-white/30 px-8 py-4 text-white backdrop-blur">Book a demo</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

This is the closing band from Tailwind UI "CTA sections, brand panel": a three-stop gradient slab with a blurred white orb, a rhetorical question for a headline, and two pill buttons. The question and "Join thousands of teams" could close any page on the web.

#### Rules

1. The headline states the next step and what it costs: "Start a 14-day trial. Bring one month of bank statements."
2. One primary button and at most one text link. Never two equal buttons.
3. The band uses `--paper-2` with 1px `--rule` borders top and bottom, 96px vertical padding, left-aligned text at most 66ch.
4. Say what happens after the click in one 14px line under the button: "No card until day 14. Cancel in Settings."
5. One closing CTA per page. Repeating the hero button 4 times down the page is a template habit.
6. No questions, no "Ready to", no orbs, no full-bleed accent color.

#### Reference build

```html
<section class="cta" aria-labelledby="cta-h">
  <h2 id="cta-h">Start a 14-day trial. Bring one month of bank statements.</h2>
  <p>Import takes about 4 minutes. You will see matched and unmatched lines before you pay anything.</p>
  <a class="btn btn-fill" href="/signup">Start 14-day trial</a>
  <a class="cta-alt" href="/sales">or book a call with sales</a>
  <p class="cta-note">No card until day 14. Cancel in Settings.</p>
</section>
```

```css
.cta { padding: 96px max(16px, calc((100% - 1040px) / 2)); background: var(--paper-2); border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.cta h2 { max-width: 24ch; margin: 0 0 16px; font-size: 32px; line-height: 1.2; }
.cta p { max-width: 66ch; margin: 0 0 24px; color: var(--ink-2); }
.cta .btn { display: inline-block; padding: 12px 20px; }
.cta-alt { margin-left: 16px; color: var(--ink); text-underline-offset: 3px; }
.cta-note { margin: 16px 0 0; font-size: 14px; }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Ready to transform your workflow?
Join thousands of teams already building the future.
Get started for free
Take your business to the next level
```

- Start a 14-day trial. Bring one month of bank statements.
- Start 14-day trial
- No card until day 14. Cancel in Settings.

#### Checklist

- Headline names the step and its cost. No question.
- One primary button, one optional text link.
- `--paper-2` band with borders, no gradient, no orb.
- One closing CTA per page.

### 5.20 FAQ sections

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="mx-auto max-w-3xl space-y-4">
  <h2 className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 bg-clip-text text-center text-4xl font-bold text-transparent">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
  {faqs.map(f => (
    <Disclosure as="div" className="rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow-md">
      <Disclosure.Button className="flex w-full justify-between font-medium">{f.q}<ChevronDownIcon className="ui-open:rotate-180 transition duration-500" /></Disclosure.Button>
      <Disclosure.Panel className="mt-4 text-gray-500">{f.a}</Disclosure.Panel>
    </Disclosure>
  ))}
</div>
```

The FAQ from a landing template: centered gradient heading, each question in its own shadowed card, a chevron that spins over 500ms. The questions are written by marketing ("Is it easy to use?") and answered with a yes.

#### Rules

1. Questions come from support tickets and sales calls. Keep a source for each. "Is it easy to use?" is not a question anyone asks.
2. Answer in the first sentence: "Yes, up to 10,000 rows per file." Then details. At most 80 words, with a link for more.
3. Use native `<details>` and `<summary>`. Rows are separated by 1px `--rule` lines. No cards.
4. Question text 16px weight 600 in `--ink`, answer 16px `--ink-2` at most 66ch. Marker is a 16px stroked plus that turns into a minus, with no rotation animation.
5. At most 10 questions. Group by topic under 18px headings when there are more.
6. Each question has an anchor so support can link to it.

#### Reference build

```html
<section class="faq" aria-labelledby="faq-h">
  <h2 id="faq-h">Questions</h2>
  <details id="csv-limit">
    <summary>Is there a limit on CSV imports?</summary>
    <p>Yes, 10,000 rows per file and 20 files per hour. Larger files can be split with the import tool. <a href="/docs/import#limits">Import limits</a></p>
  </details>
  <details id="leave">
    <summary>What happens to our data if we cancel?</summary>
    <p>It stays read-only for 90 days, then we delete it. You can export everything as CSV or PDF at any point.</p>
  </details>
</section>
```

```css
.faq { max-width: 66ch; margin: 0 auto; padding: 96px 16px; }
.faq h2 { font-size: 32px; margin: 0 0 24px; }
.faq details { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.faq details:last-of-type { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.faq summary { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 0; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; list-style: none; }
.faq summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
.faq summary::after { content: "+"; font: 400 21px/1 var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink-2); }
.faq details[open] summary::after { content: "-"; }
.faq summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.faq p { margin: 0 0 16px; color: var(--ink-2); }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Frequently Asked Questions
Is it easy to use?
Absolutely! Our intuitive interface makes it a breeze.
Still have questions? Don't hesitate to reach out!
```

- Questions
- What happens to our data if we cancel?
- Yes, 10,000 rows per file and 20 files per hour.
- Not answered here? Email support@ledgerline.example. We reply within 4 working hours.

#### Checklist

- Real questions with a source, first sentence answers.
- Native `details`, rows with rules, no cards.
- 10 questions or fewer, each with an anchor.
- No spinning chevron.

### 5.21 Comparison tables

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<table className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-2xl shadow-xl">
  <thead className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 text-white">
    <tr><th>Feature</th><th>Us</th><th>Competitor A</th><th>Competitor B</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>AI-powered insights</td><td><CheckCircleIcon className="text-emerald-500" /></td><td><XCircleIcon className="text-red-400" /></td><td><XCircleIcon className="text-red-400" /></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Seamless integrations</td><td><CheckCircleIcon className="text-emerald-500" /></td><td><XCircleIcon className="text-red-400" /></td><td><MinusIcon /></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

The versus table from a "Why us" page: a gradient header, green checks in our column and red crosses in every other, and rows chosen so we win each one. Readers discount it to zero, and the claims are often out of date within a quarter.

#### Rules

1. Compare facts a buyer can check: limits, prices, supported formats, contract terms. Every competitor cell has a source link and a "checked on" date.
2. Include rows where you lose. A table with no losses is not believed.
3. Cells hold text or numbers: "10,000 rows", "CSV, OFX", "Not offered". No green checks against red crosses.
4. Header row `--paper-2` with a 1px `--ink` bottom border. Body rows separated by 1px `--rule`. First column left-aligned and sticky on narrow screens. Numbers right-aligned in tabular numerals.
5. Use `<th scope="col">` and `<th scope="row">`, and a `<caption>` that states the date.
6. Highlight your own column with `--paper-2` background only.

#### Reference build

```html
<div class="cmp-wrap">
  <table class="cmp">
    <caption>Checked against public pricing pages on 1 Oct 2026</caption>
    <thead><tr><th scope="col">Plan for 10 users</th><th scope="col" class="ours">Ledgerline Team</th><th scope="col">Other tool A</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th scope="row">Price per year</th><td class="ours num">$2,880</td><td class="num">$2,400</td></tr>
      <tr><th scope="row">Bank import formats</th><td class="ours">CSV, OFX, CAMT.053</td><td>CSV</td></tr>
      <tr><th scope="row">Rows per import</th><td class="ours num">10,000</td><td class="num">50,000</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

```css
.cmp-wrap { overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.cmp { width: 100%; min-width: 560px; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 14px; }
.cmp caption { caption-side: bottom; padding: 12px 16px; text-align: left; color: var(--ink-3); font-size: 12px; }
.cmp th, .cmp td { padding: 12px 16px; text-align: left; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); vertical-align: top; }
.cmp thead th { background: var(--paper-2); border-top: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
.cmp tbody th { position: sticky; left: 0; background: var(--paper); font-weight: 500; }
.cmp .ours { background: var(--paper-2); }
.cmp .num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Why we're the obvious choice
AI-powered insights
Competitor A: Limited
```

- Checked against public pricing pages on 1 Oct 2026
- Rows per import: 10,000 (Other tool A: 50,000)
- Not offered

#### Checklist

- Checkable facts with sources and dates.
- At least one row you lose.
- Text in cells, no check and cross icons.
- Real table markup with scoped headers and a dated caption.

### 5.22 Error pages

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center justify-center bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-50 via-white to-purple-50">
  <h1 className="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 bg-clip-text text-[12rem] font-black text-transparent">404</h1>
  <img src="/astronaut-floating.svg" className="w-64 animate-bounce" />
  <h2 className="text-3xl font-bold">Oops! Lost in space?</h2>
  <p className="text-gray-500">The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved.</p>
  <button className="mt-8 rounded-full bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 px-8 py-3 text-white shadow-lg">Take me home</button>
</div>
```

The 404 from template packs: a 192px gradient "404", a bouncing astronaut illustration, a joke headline, and one button home. The 500 page is usually the same layout with "Houston, we have a problem". Neither says what happened or what the user can do besides leave.

#### Rules

1. Keep the site header and navigation on error pages so the user can continue from where they are.
2. The heading says what happened in plain words: "This page does not exist", "Something failed on our side". The status code goes in 14px `--ink-3` text, not 192px.
3. Offer the 2 or 3 most likely next steps as links: search, the parent page, the home page.
4. For 404s on old URLs, add redirects. Log every 404 with its referrer and fix the top 20 each month.
5. For 500s, show a reference ID the user can quote to support, the time in UTC, and a link to the status page. Never show a stack trace.
6. For 503 maintenance, give the end time in the user's time zone.
7. No jokes, no illustrations, no animation. The user is already annoyed.
8. Return the real HTTP status. A 404 page served with 200 pollutes search indexes.

#### Reference build

```html
<main class="err">
  <p class="err-code">Error 500</p>
  <h1>Something failed on our side</h1>
  <p>Your last change was not saved. Try again in a minute. If it fails twice, send support the reference below.</p>
  <dl class="err-ref"><dt>Reference</dt><dd><code>req_7f3a91c2</code></dd><dt>Time</dt><dd>15 Oct 2026, 14:22 UTC</dd></dl>
  <ul><li><a href="javascript:location.reload()">Try again</a></li><li><a href="https://status.example.com">Service status</a></li><li><a href="/invoices">Back to invoices</a></li></ul>
</main>
```

```css
.err { max-width: 66ch; margin: 0 auto; padding: 96px 16px; }
.err-code { margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink-3); }
.err h1 { margin: 0 0 16px; font-size: 32px; line-height: 1.2; }
.err p { color: var(--ink-2); }
.err-ref { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr; gap: 4px 16px; margin: 24px 0; padding: 16px; background: var(--paper-2); border: 1px solid var(--rule); font-size: 14px; }
.err-ref dt { color: var(--ink-2); }
.err-ref dd { margin: 0; }
.err ul { padding-left: 16px; line-height: 2; }
.err a { color: var(--ink); text-underline-offset: 3px; }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Oops! Lost in space?
Houston, we have a problem.
Something went wrong. Please try again later.
Take me home
```

- This page does not exist. It may have been renamed when we moved the docs in June.
- Something failed on our side. Your last change was not saved.
- Down for maintenance until 16:00 your time (15:00 UTC).
- Reference req_7f3a91c2

#### Checklist

- Header and navigation kept.
- Plain heading, small status code, real HTTP status.
- Next steps as links, reference ID on 500s.
- No jokes, illustrations or bouncing.

### 5.23 Auth screens

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<div className="grid min-h-screen lg:grid-cols-2">
  <div className="hidden bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-600 via-purple-600 to-pink-500 p-12 lg:flex lg:flex-col lg:justify-end">
    <p className="text-2xl text-white">"This platform changed everything for us."</p>
  </div>
  <div className="flex items-center justify-center">
    <div className="w-full max-w-md rounded-3xl bg-white/80 p-10 shadow-2xl backdrop-blur">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold">Welcome back!</h1>
      <div className="mt-6 grid grid-cols-4 gap-3">{['Google','GitHub','Apple','X'].map(p => <button className="rounded-xl border p-3 shadow-sm"><Logo name={p} /></button>)}</div>
      <input className="mt-6 w-full rounded-xl border p-3" placeholder="Email" />
      <input className="mt-3 w-full rounded-xl border p-3" type="password" placeholder="Password" onPaste={e => e.preventDefault()} />
      <button className="mt-6 w-full rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 py-3 text-white"><SparklesIcon /> Sign in with magic link</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

This is the shadcn "Authentication" example: a split screen with a gradient art panel and an anonymous quote, a glass card, four icon-only provider buttons, and placeholder-only fields. Blocking paste breaks password managers, and the icon-only buttons have no accessible names.

#### Rules

1. One column, 400px maximum, on `--paper`, with the product name at the top. No split-screen art panel.
2. Every field has a visible label. Use `autocomplete="email"`, `current-password` on sign-in and `new-password` on sign-up. Never block paste.
3. Show or hide the password with a text button, "Show", inside the field. No confirm-password field.
4. State password rules before typing: "At least 12 characters." No rainbow strength meter.
5. Offer at most 3 identity providers, as full-width outlined buttons with the name in text: "Continue with Google".
6. Password reset never confirms whether an account exists: "If an account exists for ana@harbor.co, we sent a link. It expires in 30 minutes."
7. After 5 failed attempts, say when the user can try again: "Try again at 14:40, or reset your password."
8. Pick "Sign in" or "Log in" and use the same verb for signing out.

#### Reference build

```html
<main class="auth">
  <p class="auth-brand">Ledgerline</p>
  <h1>Sign in</h1>
  <a class="btn-outline auth-sso" href="/sso/google">Continue with Google</a>
  <p class="auth-or">or with email</p>
  <form method="post" action="/signin">
    <label for="em">Email</label>
    <input id="em" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>
    <label for="pw">Password</label>
    <div class="pw"><input id="pw" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="current-password" required><button type="button" aria-controls="pw" aria-pressed="false">Show</button></div>
    <button type="submit" class="btn-fill">Sign in</button>
  </form>
  <p class="auth-links"><a href="/reset">Reset password</a> <a href="/signup">Create an account</a></p>
</main>
```

```css
.auth { max-width: 400px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 64px 16px; }
.auth-brand { margin: 0 0 32px; font-weight: 600; }
.auth h1 { margin: 0 0 24px; font-size: 24px; }
.auth label { display: block; margin: 16px 0 4px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; }
.auth input { width: 100%; height: 40px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--paper); font: 16px var(--font-sans); }
.auth input:focus-visible, .auth button:focus-visible, .auth a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.pw { position: relative; }
.pw input { padding-right: 64px; }
.pw button { position: absolute; right: 4px; top: 4px; height: 32px; padding: 0 8px; background: none; border: 0; color: var(--ink-2); font: 14px var(--font-sans); cursor: pointer; }
.auth .btn-fill, .auth-sso { display: block; width: 100%; margin-top: 24px; padding: 10px; text-align: center; border-radius: var(--radius); }
.auth-or { margin: 24px 0 0; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink-3); }
.auth-links { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 24px; font-size: 14px; }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Welcome back!
Oops! Invalid credentials.
We couldn't find an account with that email.
Sign in with magic link
```

- Sign in
- Email or password is wrong. Check both, or reset your password.
- If an account exists for ana@harbor.co, we sent a link. It expires in 30 minutes.

#### Checklist

- One 400px column, visible labels, correct `autocomplete`.
- Paste allowed, "Show" as text, no confirm field.
- Provider buttons named in text, 3 or fewer.
- Reset never reveals whether an account exists.

### 5.24 Chat and AI assistant interfaces

#### What the machine produces

```slop
<button className="fixed bottom-6 right-6 flex h-14 w-14 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-gradient-to-br from-violet-500 to-fuchsia-500 shadow-2xl shadow-purple-500/50 animate-pulse">
  <SparklesIcon className="h-6 w-6 text-white" />
</button>
<div className="fixed bottom-24 right-6 w-96 rounded-3xl bg-white/90 shadow-2xl backdrop-blur-xl">
  <div className="rounded-t-3xl bg-gradient-to-r from-violet-600 to-indigo-600 p-4 text-white">AI Assistant <span className="text-xs">Powered by AI</span></div>
  <div className="space-y-3 p-4">
    <div className="ml-auto w-fit rounded-2xl rounded-br-sm bg-gradient-to-r from-violet-500 to-purple-600 px-4 py-2 text-white">How many invoices are overdue?</div>
    <div className="flex gap-1"><span className="h-2 w-2 animate-bounce rounded-full bg-purple-400" /><span className="h-2 w-2 animate-bounce rounded-full bg-purple-400 [animation-delay:150ms]" /><span className="h-2 w-2 animate-bounce rounded-full bg-purple-400 [animation-delay:300ms]" /></div>
  </div>
  <input placeholder="Ask me anything..." className="m-4 rounded-full border px-4 py-2" />
</div>
```

This is the AI widget every product added in 2023 and 2024: a pulsing violet sparkle bubble in the corner, a chat panel with a purple header, gradient user bubbles, and three bouncing dots that pretend someone is typing. The sparkle and the purple come from early AI product launches and now mean "bolted on".

#### Rules

1. Name the feature by what it does with the user's data: "Ask about invoices". Never "AI Assistant", never a sparkle icon.
2. Put it in the page as a 400px side panel or inline under the thing it answers about. No floating corner bubble, no pulse.
3. Use the product's own palette. `--accent` appears only on the send button. No purple, no gradients.
4. Messages are full-width blocks, not bubbles. Each has a 12px speaker label, "You" or "Assistant". User messages sit on `--paper-2`, answers on `--paper`. Text is 16px at 66ch.
5. Stream text as it arrives. Before the first token, describe the real step: "Reading 214 invoices". No typing dots.
6. While streaming, the send button becomes "Stop". Stopping keeps the partial answer, marked "Stopped".
7. Any answer drawn from the user's records cites them as links: "INV-2041, INV-2057".
8. An answer that proposes a change shows the change as a diff and an "Apply" button. Nothing changes without that click.
9. The composer grows to 8 lines. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line. Show that hint once, in 12px `--ink-3`.
10. Show at most 3 suggested questions, only in the empty state, and make them about the current page.
11. The transcript is `role="log"`. Announce a finished answer, not each token.

#### Reference build

```html
<aside class="ask" aria-labelledby="ask-h">
  <h2 id="ask-h">Ask about invoices</h2>
  <div class="ask-log" role="log" aria-live="polite">
    <div class="msg msg-you"><p class="who">You</p><p>How many invoices are overdue?</p></div>
    <div class="msg"><p class="who">Assistant</p><p>7 invoices are overdue, $18,240.00 in total. The oldest is INV-2041 from Acme Freight, 41 days late.</p>
      <p class="src">Sources: <a href="/invoices?status=overdue">7 overdue invoices</a></p></div>
  </div>
  <form class="ask-form"><label for="ask-q" class="sr-only">Question</label>
    <textarea id="ask-q" rows="1" placeholder="Ask about amounts, customers or dates"></textarea>
    <button type="submit" class="btn-fill">Send</button></form>
</aside>
```

```css
.ask { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 400px; max-width: 100%; height: 100%; border-left: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--paper); }
.ask h2 { margin: 0; padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.ask-log { flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; }
.msg { padding: 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.msg-you { background: var(--paper-2); }

.ask-form { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: flex-end; padding: 12px 16px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.ask-form textarea { flex: 1; min-height: 40px; max-height: 192px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: var(--radius); font: 16px/1.5 var(--font-sans); resize: none; field-sizing: content; }
.ask-form .btn-fill { height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; }
```

#### Copy

```slop
Hi there! I'm your AI-powered assistant. How can I help you today?
Ask me anything...
Great question! Let me dive into that for you.
As an AI, I cannot...
```

- Ask about invoices
- Reading 214 invoices
- 7 invoices are overdue, $18,240.00 in total.
- I can only see invoices in Harbor Supply. Payroll data is not connected.

#### Checklist

- Named by task, placed in the page, no corner bubble.
- No sparkle, no purple, no gradient, no typing dots.
